3.1.0: I bow to Maheśvara, who is great bliss, whose play is endless, the all-pervading Lord of all, the Great One, beloved of Gaurī, the source from whom Kārttika and the King of Obstacles Gaṇeśa arose: Śaṅkara, the primal God.
3.1.1: Śaunaka said: O disciple of Vyāsa, most fortunate Sūta, treasury of knowledge and compassion, tell us of the incarnations of Śambhu, through which he brought about the welfare of the good. ॥1॥
3.1.2: Sūta said: O sage Śaunaka, I shall tell you, the sage, the incarnations of Śiva; listen with true devotion, with attentive mind and senses subdued. ॥2॥
3.1.3: Long ago, O sage, Nandī, who is a form of Śiva and the refuge of the good, was asked this by Sanatkumāra; remembering Śiva, he spoke to him. ॥3॥
3.1.4: Nandīśvara said: Countless indeed are the incarnations of the all-pervading Lord of all across the kalpas; even so, I shall tell of them here as far as my understanding goes. ॥4॥
3.1.5: The nineteenth kalpa is to be known as Śvetalohita; in it the incarnation Sadyojāta is proclaimed as the first. ॥5॥
3.1.6: In that kalpa, as Brahmā was meditating on the supreme Brahman, a boy with a topknot, white and red in colour, came forth. ॥6॥
3.1.7: Seeing that Person, the Lord whose form is Brahman, Brahmā recognised him, meditated on him in his heart, and bowed with folded hands. ॥7॥
3.1.8: Knowing him to be Śiva Sadyojāta, the Lord of the worlds rejoiced, and again and again with a pure mind he contemplated that Supreme One. ॥8॥
3.1.9: Then, as he meditated, there appeared glorious white youths, embodiments of supreme knowledge and the supreme Brahman. ॥9॥
3.1.10: Sunanda, Nandana, Viśvananda and Upanandana—these great-souled ones were his disciples, by whom that Brahman was encompassed. ॥10॥
3.1.11: And Śambhu as Sadyojāta, the Supreme Lord, being pleased, lovingly gave knowledge to Brahmā (Vedhas), and also the power of creation. ॥11॥
3.1.12: Then came the twentieth kalpa, called Rakta (Red), in which the greatly radiant Brahmā assumed a red colour. ॥12॥
3.1.13: As Brahmā (Vidhi), desiring a son, meditated, a son appeared to him, wearing red garlands and garments, red-eyed, with red ornaments. ॥13॥
3.1.14: Seeing that great-souled boy, Brahmā, absorbed in meditation, recognised him as Śiva Vāmadeva and bowed with folded hands. ॥14॥
3.1.15: Then he had four sons clad in red: Viraja, Vivāha, Viśoka and Viśvabhāvana. ॥15॥
3.1.16: That Śambhu as Vāmadeva, the Supreme Lord, being pleased, lovingly gave knowledge to Brahmā, and also the power of creation. ॥16॥
3.1.17: The twenty-first kalpa is known as Pītavāsas, in which the illustrious Brahmā became clad in yellow. ॥17॥
3.1.18: As Brahmā, desiring a son, meditated, a boy was born to him, splendid in yellow garments and the like, greatly radiant and mighty-armed. ॥18॥
3.1.19: Seeing him absorbed in meditation and knowing him to be Śiva Tatpuruṣa, Brahmā (Vidhi) bowed; then, with understanding, he recited the Śaiva Gāyatrī— ॥19॥
3.1.20: —having recited that great goddess the Gāyatrī, revered by all the worlds, with a mind absorbed in meditation, Mahādeva was pleased. ॥20॥
3.1.21: Then at his side appeared divine boys, all clad in yellow, promoters of the path of yoga. ॥21॥
3.1.22: Then, when that yellow kalpa of the Self-born Brahmā had passed, another kalpa began again, and it was named Śiva. ॥22॥
3.1.23: When the single ocean of dissolution had lasted a thousand divine years, Brahmā, wishing to create beings, pondered in distress. ॥23॥
3.1.24: Then the greatly radiant Brahmā saw a boy appear, black in colour, of great might, blazing with his own splendour, ॥24॥
3.1.25: wearing black garments and a black turban, with a black sacred thread, adorned with a black crown, with black bathing-unguents. ॥25॥
3.1.26: Seeing that great-souled Aghora of terrible valour, the wondrous lord of the god of gods, black and tawny, he bowed to him. ॥26॥
3.1.27: Then Brahmā meditated on Aghora, whose form is Brahman, and praised with pleasing words the imperishable one, tender to his devotees. ॥27॥
3.1.28: Then at his side four great-souled boys came into being, black, with black bathing-unguents. ॥28॥
3.1.29: Kṛṣṇa, Kṛṣṇaśikha, Kṛṣṇāsya and Kṛṣṇakaṇṭhadhṛk—these were they, of mysterious names, Śiva-formed and very radiant. ॥29॥
3.1.30: Being such, these great souls, for the sake of Brahmā's creation, set in motion the great and wondrous yoga called Ghora. ॥30॥
3.1.31: Then, O lords of sages, another kalpa of Brahmā began, supremely wondrous, known by the name Viśvarūpa. ॥31॥
3.1.32: As Brahmā, desiring a son, meditated on Śiva in his mind, Sarasvatī appeared, of mighty sound and universal form. ॥32॥
3.1.33: Likewise appeared the blessed Īśāna, the Supreme Lord, resembling pure crystal, adorned with every ornament. ॥33॥
3.1.34: Seeing him, Brahmā bowed to Īśāna, the unborn, all-pervading, omnipresent giver of all, who is all, beautiful in form yet devoid of form. ॥34॥
3.1.35: Īśāna, the all-pervading, having thus taught the true path to Brahmā, together with his Śakti created four auspicious boys. ॥35॥
3.1.36: Jaṭī, Muṇḍī, Śikhaṇḍī and Ardhamuṇḍa were born; having taught the true dharma through yoga and accomplished their task, they attained the goal of yoga. ॥36॥
3.1.37: Thus, O omniscient Sanatkumāra, the origin of Sadyojāta and the others has been told in brief, out of desire for the welfare of the worlds. ॥37॥
3.1.38: Now, O greatly wise one, hear their activity in due order, all of which, established throughout the cosmic egg, brings about the welfare of the three worlds. ॥38॥
3.1.39: Īśāna, Tatpuruṣa, Aghora, the one called Vāmadeva, and likewise the one called Brahma Sadyojāta—these are the five renowned forms of Maheśa. ॥39॥
3.1.40: Īśāna, of the form of Śiva, is remembered as the first and the weightiest. He directly presides over the kṣetrajña, the enjoyer of prakṛti. ॥40॥
3.1.41: The second form of Śiva, called Tatpuruṣa, presides over the object of enjoyment, whose nature is to be the substratum of the guṇas, and which is all-knowing. ॥41॥
3.1.42: The third, the form of the Pināka-bearer called Aghora, abides within the principle of intellect (buddhi-tattva), joined with its own limbs, for the sake of dharma. ॥42॥
3.1.43: The fourth form of Śaṅkara, called Vāmadeva, is the presiding principle of ego (ahaṅkāra), ever performing many works. ॥43॥
3.1.44: The form of Śaṅkara named Īśāna is ever the lord of hearing, of speech, and likewise of the all-pervading ether. ॥44॥
3.1.45: The wise who are skilled in discernment declare the lordly form named Tatpuruṣa to be the lord of skin, hand, touch and air. ॥45॥
3.1.46: The wise call the form named Aghora the presiding principle of the body, of form (sight) and likewise of fire. ॥46॥
3.1.47: The form of Śaṅkara named Vāmadeva is regarded as the lord of the tongue, of the anus, of taste and likewise of the waters. ॥47॥
3.1.48: They know the form of Śaṅkara named Sadyojāta as the lord of the nose, of the genital organ, of smell and likewise of the earth. ॥48॥
3.1.49: These forms of Śambhu, the sole causes of all welfare, should always be worshipped with effort by men who seek welfare. ॥49॥
3.1.50: Whoever reads or hears of the origin of Sadyojāta and the others, having enjoyed all desires, attains the supreme goal. ॥50॥
3.1.iti: Thus ends the first adhyāya, named The five Brahmā incarnations of Śiva, in the third saṃhitā, the Śatarudra-saṃhitā, of the Śrī Śivamahāpurāṇa. ॥1॥
3.2.1: Nandīśvara said: Listen, dear one, O lord, O sage, to the supreme incarnations of Maheśa, which accomplish every purpose in the world and give happiness to all. ॥1॥
3.2.2: This world consists of the eight forms of that Śambhu, the supreme Lord; the universe abides pervaded in him, like clusters of gems on a thread. ॥2॥
3.2.3: Śarva, Bhava, Rudra, Ugra, Bhīma, Paśupati, Īśāna and Mahādeva—these are the eight renowned forms. ॥3॥
3.2.4: Earth, water, fire, wind, space, the knower of the field (the soul), the sun and the moon are presided over by Śiva's eight forms beginning with Śarva. ॥4॥
3.2.5: The form of Śaṅkara, Maheśa, that is all-sustaining (earth) bears the moving and unmoving universe; such is the settled conclusion of scripture. ॥5॥
3.2.6: The form of the Supreme Self Bhava that consists of water, the life-giver of the entire world, is called Bhava. ॥6॥
3.2.7: The form of the good lord Ugra that sustains the whole world outside and within and itself moves (wind) is called Ugra by the wise. ॥7॥
3.2.8: The form of Bhīma consisting of the sky, which gives room to all and pervades all, is called Bhīma; it breaks the hosts of wicked kings. ॥8॥
3.2.9: The form of Paśupati should be known as the support of all souls, dwelling in all fields (bodies), cutting the bonds of the bound souls. ॥9॥
3.2.10: Illuminating the whole world, the form of Maheśa named Īśāna, called the sun (Divākara), moves across the sky. ॥10॥
3.2.11: The nectar-rayed moon that nourishes the universe is the form of Mahādeva, and it bears the name Mahādeva. ॥11॥
3.2.12: The self is the eighth form of that Śiva, the Supreme Self, pervading the other forms; therefore the universe is of the nature of Śiva. ॥12॥
3.2.13: The branches of a tree flourish by watering the tree's root; likewise the universe, his body, flourishes through the worship of Śiva. ॥13॥
3.2.14: Just as here a father is pleased by the happiness of his sons, grandsons and others, so Śaṅkara is pleased by the happiness of the universe. ॥14॥
3.2.15: If harm is done to any embodied being whatsoever, that is surely an offence done to the Eight-formed One; there is no doubt. ॥15॥
3.2.16: Worship with your whole being Śiva, Rudra, the supreme cause, who abides presiding over the universe in his eightfold form. ॥16॥
3.2.17: Thus have been described to you, O son of Brahmā, his eight renowned forms, devoted to the welfare of all; they should be served by men seeking the highest good. ॥17॥
3.2.iti: Thus ends the second adhyāya, named The eight forms of Śiva, in the third saṃhitā, the Śatarudra-saṃhitā, of the Śrī Śivamahāpurāṇa. ॥2॥
3.3.1: Nandīśvara said: Listen, dear one of great wisdom, to the unsurpassed form of Śiva called Ardhanārīnara (half-woman, half-man), which fulfilled the desire of Vidhi (Brahmā). ॥1॥
3.3.2: When all the creatures created by the Creator did not multiply, he became troubled with anxiety, distressed by that grief. ॥2॥
3.3.3: Then a voice arose from the sky: Make a creation born of couples. Hearing that, Brahmā resolved to produce sexual creation. ॥3॥
3.3.4: But since the race of women had not previously come forth from Īśāna, the lotus-born one was unable to make a creation born of union. ॥4॥
3.3.5: Without the power of Śambhu these creatures cannot be born — reflecting thus, Brahmā began to perform austerity. ॥5॥
3.3.6: Meditating lovingly in his heart on the Supreme Lord united with Śivā, the supreme Śakti, he performed supreme austerity. ॥6॥
3.3.7: By the intense austerity of that Self-born one, so absorbed, Śiva was quickly pleased in a very short time. ॥7॥
3.3.8: Then Hara, entering the wish-granting form of the Lord who is perfect consciousness, became half-woman, half-man, and came near Brahmā. ॥8॥
3.3.9: Seeing the god Śaṅkara accompanied by the supreme Śakti, Brahmā prostrated like a staff and, with joined palms, praised him. ॥9॥
3.3.10: Then the god Mahādeva, Maheśvara the maker of the universe, greatly pleased, spoke with a voice deep as a thundercloud, for the sake of creation's increase. ॥10॥
3.3.11: Īśvara said: Child, child, most fortunate one, my son, Grandsire, I have truly understood your entire wish. ॥11॥
3.3.12: You have now performed austerity solely for the increase of creatures. I am pleased with that austerity and I grant what you desire. ॥12॥
3.3.13: Having spoken these most generous, naturally sweet words, Śiva separated the goddess Śivā from a portion of his body. ॥13॥
3.3.14: Seeing that supreme Śakti, separated and come forth from Śiva, Vidhi bowed down humbly and entreated her. ॥14॥
3.3.15: Brahmā said: O Śivā, I was created in the beginning by the God of gods, your husband, and all creatures were appointed to me by Śambhu, the Supreme Self. ॥15॥
3.3.16: O Śivā, all the gods and others were fashioned by me with the mind; though created again and again, they do not increase. ॥16॥
3.3.17: Henceforth, by making creation arise from couples, I wish to make all my creatures increase. ॥17॥
3.3.18: The imperishable race of women has not previously come forth from you; therefore I do not have the power to create the race of women. ॥18॥
3.3.19: Surely all powers originate from you; therefore I entreat you, the supreme Śakti, Mistress of all. ॥19॥
3.3.20: O Śivā, give me the power to create the race of women; salutation to you, O Mother, beloved of Śiva, for the sake of the increase of the moving and unmoving world. ॥20॥
3.3.21: And I ask another boon of you, O sovereign of boon-givers; grant it to me out of compassion, O Mother of the world; salutation to you. ॥21॥
3.3.22: O all-pervading one, for the increase of the moving and unmoving, united with the one Lord, become the daughter of my son Dakṣa, O Bhavāmbikā. ॥22॥
3.3.23: Thus entreated by Brahmā, the goddess, the Supreme Mistress, said so be it and gave that power to Vidhi. ॥23॥
3.3.24: Therefore that goddess Śivā, the Śakti of Śiva who pervades the world, created from between her brows a single Śakti radiant like herself. ॥24॥
3.3.25: Looking at that Śakti, Bhavāmbikā, Hara the best of gods, the ocean of compassion, the great Lord who acts in play, smiling, said to her: ॥25॥
3.3.26: Śiva said: O Goddess, you have been worshipped with austerity by Brahmā Parameṣṭhin; be gracious with great love and fulfil all his wishes. ॥26॥
3.3.27: Receiving that command of the Supreme Lord with her head bowed, the goddess, at Brahmā's request, became the daughter of Dakṣa. ॥27॥
3.3.28: Having thus given incomparable power to Brahmā, O sage, that Śivā entered the body of Śambhu, and the Lord Śambhu vanished. ॥28॥
3.3.29: From then on in this world a share was assigned to woman; Vidhi attained joy, and creation through union came about. ॥29॥
3.3.30: Thus I have told you, dear one, this most excellent form of Śiva, half-woman and half-man, which bestows great auspiciousness on the good. ॥30॥
3.3.31: Whoever reads or even hears this sinless narrative enjoys all pleasures and attains the supreme goal. ॥31॥
3.3.iti: Thus ends the third adhyāya, named Śiva's incarnation as Ardhanārīśvara, in the third saṃhitā, the Rudra-saṃhitā, of the Śrī Śivamahāpurāṇa. ॥3॥
3.4.1: Nandīśvara said: O all-knowing Sanatkumāra, hear gladly the story of Śaṅkara, ever bestowing happiness, which Rudra lovingly narrated to Brahmā. ॥1॥
3.4.2: Śiva said: In the seventh, Vārāha kalpa, in the period called manvantara, then the blessed lord of the kalpa, who illumines all the worlds, ॥2॥
3.4.3: he, the son of Manu Vaivasvata, will be your great-grandson. Then, O Vidhi, in that manvantara, the four yugas will come, ॥3॥
3.4.4: For the grace of the worlds and for the welfare of brāhmaṇas, I shall be born, O Vidhi, O Brahmā, near the end of the age called Dvāpara. ॥4॥
3.4.5: And then, by the course of the yugas, in that first yuga — in the first Dvāpara, O Brahmā, when the Vyāsa is Svayamprabhu (the self-luminous lord), ॥5॥
3.4.6: then, for the sake of the brāhmaṇas, at the end of that age in the Kali, I shall become, united with Śivā, a great sage named Śveta, ॥6॥
3.4.7: on the lovely Himalayan peak Chāgala, the best of mountains. Then, O Vidhi, I shall have disciples wearing tufts of hair: ॥7॥
3.4.8: Śveta, Śvetaśikha, Śvetāśva and Śvetalohita — these four, through the yoga of meditation, will go to my city. ॥8॥
3.4.9: Then, having known me in truth as the imperishable, they will become devotees, free from birth, death and old age, absorbed in the supreme Brahman. ॥9॥
3.4.10: I cannot be seen by men except through meditation, O Grandsire, not, dear son, by means such as charity and dharma, which are rooted in action. ॥10॥
3.4.11: In the second Dvāpara, when the Vyāsa is the Prajāpati named Satya, then in the Kali I shall be the sage named Sutāra. ॥11॥
3.4.12: There too I shall have disciples, twice-born knowers of the Veda: Dundubhi, Śatarūpa, Hṛṣīka and Ketumān. ॥12॥
3.4.13: These four, through the yoga of meditation, will go to my city; then, having known me in truth as the imperishable, they will be liberated. ॥13॥
3.4.14: And in the third Dvāpara, when the Vyāsa is Bhārgava, then too, at the end of the age, I shall be Damana. ॥14॥
3.4.15: There too I shall have four sons: Viśoka, Viśeṣa, Vipāpa and Pāpanāśana. ॥15॥
3.4.16: With my disciples I shall render help to the Vyāsa, O four-faced one, and here in the Kali I shall firmly establish the path of renunciation. ॥16॥
3.4.17: And in the fourth Dvāpara, when Aṅgiras is remembered as the Vyāsa, then too I shall be the one named Suhotra. ॥17॥
3.4.18: There too I shall have four sons, great-souled practitioners of yoga; I tell you their names, O Vidhi: ॥18॥
3.4.19: Sumukha, Durmukha, Durdama and Duratikrama. With these disciples I shall then help the Vyāsa, O Vidhi. ॥19॥
3.4.20: And in the fifth Dvāpara, Savitṛ is known as the Vyāsa; then I shall be a yogin named Kaṅka, of great austerity. ॥20॥
3.4.21: There too I shall have four sons, great-souled practitioners of yoga; hear their names from me: ॥21॥
3.4.22: Sanaka, Sanātana, the lord Sanandana, and the mighty Sanatkumāra — pure and free of egoism. ॥22॥
3.4.23: There too, I, named Kaṅka, O Vidhi, shall give help to Savitṛ the Vyāsa, furthering the path of renunciation. ॥23॥
3.4.24: Again, in the sixth cycle, in the Dvāpara, Mṛtyu, maker of the worlds, will be the Vyāsa, the divider of the Veda. ॥24॥
3.4.25: Then too I shall be the one named Lokākṣi, for the good assistance of the Vyāsa, furthering the path of renunciation. ॥25॥
3.4.26: There too I shall have four disciples, firm in their vows: Sudhāmā, Virajā, Sañjaya and Vijaya. ॥26॥
3.4.27: In the seventh cycle, when Śatakratu is the Vyāsa, then too, O Vidhi, I shall be the mighty Jaigīṣavya. ॥27॥
3.4.28: Skilled in the great yoga, I shall make yoga firm, dwelling in a cave in Kāśī, a divine place, lying on a bed of kuśa grass. ॥28॥
3.4.29: And I shall help Śatakratu the Vyāsa, and I shall lift the devotees out of the fear of saṃsāra, O Vidhi. ॥29॥
3.4.30: In that age too I shall have four sons: Sārasvata, Yogīśa, Meghavāha and Suvāhana. ॥30॥
3.4.31: In the eighth cycle, Vasiṣṭha, the best of sages, will be the Veda-Vyāsa, the divider of the Veda. ॥31॥
3.4.32: There too I shall be the one named Dadhivāhana, and I shall indeed help the Vyāsa, O best of yoga-knowers. ॥32॥
3.4.33: Kapila, Āsuri, Pañcaśikha and Śālvala — four yogin sons equal to me will be born. ॥33॥
3.4.34: In the ninth cycle, in that same age, O Vidhi, the best of sages called Sārasvata will be the Vyāsa. ॥34॥
3.4.35: For the growth of the path of renunciation of that meditating Vyāsa, I too shall then be born, known by the name Ṛṣabha. ॥35॥
3.4.36: Parāśara, Garga, Bhārgava and Giriśa — these four excellent yogins will be my disciples there. ॥36॥
3.4.37: Together with them I shall make firm the path of yoga, O Prajāpati, and I shall indeed give help to Veda-Vyāsa, the good sage. ॥37॥
3.4.38: In that form, O Vidhi, I, the compassionate one, shall indeed bring about the deliverance of many suffering devotees from worldly existence. ॥38॥
3.4.39: That incarnation of mine, O Vidhi, called Ṛṣabha, accomplisher of true yoga, will shape the mind of the Vyāsa Sārasvata and perform manifold acts of help. ॥39॥
3.4.40: By which incarnation of mine Bhadrāyu, the king's young son, who had died from the effect of poison and was abandoned by his father, was restored to life. ॥40॥
3.4.41: Then, when that royal child reached his sixteenth year, that Ṛṣabha, who is Śiva's own self, suddenly went to his house again. ॥41॥
3.4.42: Honoured by him, that sage, of true form and a treasury of compassion, taught him the duties of kings and the royal yogas, O Prajāpati. ॥42॥
3.4.43: Then he, pleased at heart, gave him a divine armour, a conch, and a shining sword, destroyer of all enemies. ॥43॥
3.4.44: Touching his body with sacred ash out of compassion, he who is kind to the afflicted gave him the strength of twelve thousand elephants. ॥44॥
3.4.45: Having thus fully reassured Bhadrāyu together with his mother, the lord Ṛṣabha, honoured by the two of them, departed, moving as he willed. ॥45॥
3.4.46: Bhadrāyu too, the royal sage, having conquered the hosts of his enemies, O Vidhi, married Kīrtimālinī and ruled the kingdom righteously. ॥46॥
3.4.47: Thus I have told you of the Ṛṣabha incarnation of mine, Śaṅkara, of such power—the ninth, the refuge of the good and friend of the afflicted. ॥47॥
3.4.48: The story of Ṛṣabha is indeed supremely purifying and great; it bestows heaven, fame and long life, and should be listened to with diligence. ॥48॥
3.4.iti: Thus ends the fourth adhyāya, named The story of Ṛṣabha, in the third saṃhitā, the Śatarudra-saṃhitā, of the Śrī Śivamahāpurāṇa. ॥4॥
3.5.1: Śiva said: In the tenth Dvāpara the Vyāsa will be the sage named Tridhāmā; I shall then appear on the lovely peak of Himavat, on Bhṛgutuṅga, the best of mountains. ॥1॥
3.5.2: There too will be my sons, headed by Bhṛgu, in accord with the Veda: Balabandhu, Narāmitra, and Ketuśṛṅga, rich in austerity. ॥2॥
3.5.3: In the eleventh Dvāpara, when Trivṛta is the Vyāsa, then in the Kali phase at Gaṅgādvāra I shall be born by the name Tapas. ॥3॥
3.5.4: Lambodara, Lambākṣa, Keśalamba, and Pralambaka—there too four sons of firm vows will be born. ॥4॥
3.5.5: In the twelfth cycle Śatatejas will be the compiler of the Veda; there too I shall be born, here in the Kali at the end of the Dvāpara. ॥5॥
3.5.6: Having reached Hemakañcuka, I shall be named Atri, steeped in yoga, to assist that very Vyāsa, establishing the path of renunciation. ॥6॥
3.5.7: Sarvajña, Samabuddhi, Sādhya, and Śarva, excellent yogins—these four will be my sons there, O great sage. ॥7॥
3.5.8: In that thirteenth age, when Dharma Nārāyaṇa is the Vyāsa, then I shall be the great sage named Bali. ॥8॥
3.5.9: I shall dwell in the hermitage of the Vālakhilyas on Gandhamādana, the best of mountains; my sons will be Sudhāmā, Kāśyapa, Vasiṣṭha, and Virajas, auspicious ones. ॥9॥
3.5.10: When, in the fourteenth turn, the Vyāsa is the one called Rakṣa, then there in the lineage of Aṅgiras I shall be Gautama. ॥10॥
3.5.11: There too, in that Kali, those sons of mine will be: Atri, Davaśada, Śravaṇa, and Śraviṣkaṭa. ॥11॥
3.5.12: When in the fifteenth Dvāpara the Vyāsa is Trayyāruṇi, then I shall be Vedaśiras, and likewise there will be Vedaśiras— ॥12॥
3.5.13: —that weapon of great power, and the mountain Vedaśīrṣa, I having reached the slope of Himavat, likewise to the north of the Sarasvatī. ॥13॥
3.5.14: There too four steadfast sons of mine will be: Kuṇi, Kuṇibāhu, Kuśarīra, and Kunetraka. ॥14॥
3.5.15: In the sixteenth age, when Deva will be the Vyāsa, then I shall indeed be Gokarṇa, for bestowing yoga. ॥15॥
3.5.16: And right there is that most holy forest named Gokarṇa. There too my sons, yogins, will be born, equal in number to the four oceans. ॥16॥
3.5.17: Kāśyapa, Uśanas, Cyavana, and Bṛhaspati—they too, by that very path, will go to Śiva's abode. ॥17॥
3.5.18: In the seventeenth cycle the Vyāsa is Devakṛtañjaya; I shall be by name Guhāvāsin, on the auspicious peak of Himavat, ॥18॥
3.5.19: in the great abode, very lofty, the Himālaya, a field of Śiva; my sons will be Utathya, Vāmadeva, Mahāyoga, and Mahābala. ॥19॥
3.5.20: In the eighteenth cycle, when Ṛtañjaya is the Vyāsa, then I shall be by name Śikhaṇḍin, on the auspicious peak of Himavat, ॥20॥
3.5.21: in the most holy Siddhakṣetra, where there is the mountain named Śikhaṇḍin, or the forest of Śikhaṇḍin, frequented by siddhas. ॥21॥
3.5.22: Vācaḥśravas, Rucīka, Śyāvāsya, and Yatīśvara—these sons, rich in austerity, will be there too. ॥22॥
3.5.23: In the nineteenth cycle the Vyāsa will be the great sage Bharadvāja; then too I shall be born, named Jaṭī Mālī. ॥23॥
3.5.24: There on the peak of Himavat will be my sons, numbering as the oceans four: Hiraṇyanāmā, Kauśalya, Lokākṣī, and Pradhimi. ॥24॥
3.5.25: In the twentieth cycle Gautama will be the Vyāsa; there I shall be named Aṭṭahāsa, and men will be fond of loud laughter. ॥25॥
3.5.26: Right there on the slope of Himavat is the great mountain Aṭṭahāsa, frequented by gods, humans, lords of yakṣas, siddhas, and cāraṇas. ॥26॥
3.5.27: There too those sons of mine, excellent yogins, will be: Sumantu, the learned Barbari, Kabandha, and Kuśikandhara. ॥27॥
3.5.28: In that twenty-first age, when Vācaḥśravas is the Vyāsa, then I shall be named Dāruka; from that comes the name of the auspicious Dāruvana. ॥28॥
3.5.29: There too those sons of mine, excellent yogins, will be: Plakṣa, Dārbhāyaṇi, Ketumān, and Gautama. ॥29॥
3.5.30: In the twenty-second cycle, when Śuṣmāyaṇa is the Vyāsa, then too I shall be a great sage at Vārāṇasī, ॥30॥
3.5.31: named Lāṅgalī Bhīma, where the gods together with Vāsava (Indra) will see me in that Kali as Bhava bearing the plough as weapon. ॥31॥
3.5.32: There too those sons of mine, very righteous, will be: Bhallavī, Madhupiṅga, and likewise Śvetaketu. ॥32॥
3.5.33: In the twenty-third cycle, when the sage Tṛṇabindu is the Vyāsa, then I shall be named Śveta, on the auspicious mountain Kālañjara. ॥33॥
3.5.34: There too those sons of mine, ascetics, will be: Uśika, Bṛhadaśva, Devala, and Kavi. ॥34॥
3.5.35: In the twenty-fourth cycle, when the mighty Yakṣa is the Vyāsa, then in that age I shall be the great yogin named Śūlī, in Naimiṣa. ॥35॥
3.5.36: There too those disciples of mine, ascetics, will be: Śālihotra, Agniveśa, Yuvanāśva, and Śaradvasu. ॥36॥
3.5.37: In the twenty-fifth, when the Vyāsa will be named Śakti, then too I shall be the great yogin, the lord Daṇḍī Muṇḍīśvara. ॥37॥
3.5.38: There too those disciples of mine, ascetics, will be: Chagala, Kuṇḍakarṇa, Kumbhāṇḍa, and Pravāhaka. ॥38॥
3.5.39: When Parāśara is the Vyāsa in the twenty-sixth, I too shall be born, having reached the city of Bhadravaṭa, called by name Sahiṣṇu. ॥39॥
3.5.40: There too those disciples of mine, ascetics, will be: Ulūka, Vidyuta, Śambūka, and Āśvalāyana. ॥40॥
3.5.41: In the twenty-seventh Dvāpara, when Jātūkarṇya will be the Vyāsa, then too I shall be Somaśarmā, having resorted to the Prabhāsa pilgrimage site. ॥41॥
3.5.42: There too those disciples of mine will be ascetics: Akṣapāda, Kumāra, Ulūka, and likewise Vatsa. ॥42॥
3.5.43: But in the twenty-eighth Dvāpara, when Hari, the son of Parāśara, the lord, will be the Vyāsa named Dvaipāyana, ॥43॥
3.5.44: then, with a sixth portion of Viṣṇu, Kṛṣṇa, the best of beings, the excellent son of Vasudeva, will be born as Vāsudeva. ॥44॥
3.5.45: Then too I shall appear, as the Self of yoga, through yogic māyā, in the body of a celibate student, to astonish the world. ॥45॥
3.5.46: Seeing a dead body abandoned in a cremation ground, yet free of defect, I shall enter it by yogic māyā for the welfare of the brāhmaṇas, ॥46॥
3.5.47: and entering the divine, holy cave of Meru together with you and Viṣṇu, I shall then, O Brahmā, be known by the name Laṅkulī. ॥47॥
3.5.48: Then the supreme siddha-field called Kāyāvatāra will be very famous as long as the earth endures. ॥48॥
3.5.49: There too those disciples of mine will be ascetics: Kuśika, Garga, Mitra and Kauruṣya. ॥49॥
3.5.50: These yogin brāhmaṇas, masters of the Vedas, celibate, having attained Maheśvara's yoga, will go to the city of Śiva. ॥50॥
3.5.51: Thus in the Vaivasvata Manvantara the incarnations of the Lord of Yoga in all the cycles have been properly declared by the Supreme Self, O you of good vows. ॥51॥
3.5.52: And the twenty-eight Vyāsas, in each Dvāpara, O lord, and the incarnations of the Lord of Yoga at the beginning of each Kali age. ॥52॥
3.5.53: Of the incarnations of the Lord of Yoga, each has four imperishable disciples, great Śaivas, promoters of the path of yoga. ॥53॥
3.5.54: These Pāśupata disciples have bodies smeared with ash, are adorned with rudrākṣa garlands, and their foreheads are marked with the tripuṇḍra. ॥54॥
3.5.55: All the disciples are devoted to dharma, masters of the Vedas and Vedāṅgas, ever devoted to the worship of the liṅga, established in it outwardly and inwardly, ॥55॥
3.5.56: steadfast in meditation on me through devotion and yoga, with senses conquered; in number they are counted by the wise as one hundred and twelve. ॥56॥
3.5.57: Thus I have declared the characteristics of the incarnations, from Manu up to Kṛṣṇa, in the sequence of twenty-eight yugas. ॥57॥
3.5.58: There, in that kalpa, when Kṛṣṇa Dvaipāyana appears, the arrangement of the collections of śruti, bearing the mark of Brahman, will take place. ॥58॥
3.5.59: Having spoken thus and blessed Brahmā, Maheśvara, the lord of the gods, looked at him once more and vanished right there. ॥59॥
3.5.iti: Thus ends the fifth adhyāya, named The nineteen incarnations of Śiva, in the account of Śiva's incarnations, in the third saṃhitā, the Śatarudra-saṃhitā, of the Śrī Śivamahāpurāṇa. ॥5॥
3.6.1: Sanatkumāra said: How did you, born of a portion of Mahādeva, attain Śiva? I wish to hear all of that; please tell it to me, O lord. ॥1॥
3.6.2: Nandīśvara said: O all-knowing Sanatkumāra, listen attentively to how I, born of a portion of Mahādeva, attained Śiva, O sage. ॥2॥
3.6.3: Śilāda became desirous of offspring, having been respectfully told by his ancestors, who longed for deliverance, to beget a son; and he, with devotion, set his mind on delivering them. ॥3॥
3.6.4: The mighty one named Śilāda, with downcast eyes and righteous soul, had his way of life among the sages, and later he went to Śiva's world. ॥4॥
3.6.5: Directing it towards Śakra, that sage named Śilāda, steady of mind and firm in his vow, performed a most unbearable austerity for a long time. ॥5॥
3.6.6: Śatakratu was pleased by the austerity of him as he practised it; and then the lord of all gods went to grant a boon. ॥6॥
3.6.7: Śakra said to Śilāda with great affection: I am pleased with you, O sinless one; therefore, O tiger among sages, choose boons. ॥7॥
3.6.8: Then, bowing to the lord of gods and reverently praising him with hymns, Śilāda, the tiger among sages, with hands folded, said to him: ॥8॥
3.6.9: Śilāda said: O Śatakratu, lord of the gods, if you are pleased with me, O lord, I desire a son not born of a womb, free from death, and of good vows. ॥9॥
3.6.10: Śakra said: I will give you a son, O seeker of a son, born of a womb and subject to death. Otherwise I will not give one to you; for there are indeed none free from death. ॥10॥
3.6.11: I will not give you a son free from death and not born of a womb. Not even Hari and the blessed Vidhi can—what then of anyone else, O great sage? ॥11॥
3.6.12: Even those two, born from the body of the enemy of Tripura, are subject to death; the measure of their lifespans too is stated separately in the Veda. ॥12॥
3.6.13: Therefore, O best of brahmins, earnestly give up hope for a son not born of a womb and free from death; accept a son befitting yourself. ॥13॥
3.6.14: But if Rudra, lord of the gods, Maheśvara, is gracious, then a most rare son, free from death and not born of a womb, may be yours. ॥14॥
3.6.15: I, the blessed Viṣṇu, and Druhiṇa, O great sage, are unable to give a son not born of a womb and free from death. ॥15॥
3.6.16: Worship Mahādeva with the desire for such a son; he, lord of all and supremely powerful, will grant you a son. ॥16॥
3.6.17: Nandīśvara said: Having spoken thus to the best of brahmins and having favoured him, the compassionate lord of the gods, surrounded by the gods, went to his own world, O sage. ॥17॥
3.6.18: When that boon-giving thousand-eyed one had gone, Śilāśana (Śilāda), worshipping Mahādeva, pleased Bhava through austerity. ॥18॥
3.6.19: Then for that brahmin, thus ceaselessly absorbed in it, a thousand divine years passed, wondrously, like a moment. ॥19॥
3.6.20: The sage's body was covered by an anthill and on all sides by hosts of hundreds of thousands of insects, and by other blood-sucking creatures with mouths like diamond needles. ॥20॥
3.6.21: Remaining in that hollow, without flesh, blood or skin, Śilāda, best of sages, at length became nothing but bones. ॥21॥
3.6.22: Then the Lord, pleased, showed him his own form—divine, endowed with divine qualities, unattainable by the perverse-minded. ॥22॥
3.6.23: To him who had been practising austerity for a thousand divine years, the trident-bearer, overlord of all gods, said: I am the giver of boons. ॥23॥
3.6.24: Absorbed in deep samādhi, that great sage Śilāda did not hear those words of Śambhu, who is so wholly subject to devotion. ॥24॥
3.6.25: When the sage was touched with his hand by the enemy of Tripura, at that very moment the tiger among sages gave up the course of his austerity. ॥25॥
3.6.26: Then the sage opened his eyes and, beholding Śambhu together with Umā, quickly bowed with joy and fell at his feet, O sage. ॥26॥
3.6.27: With a voice choked with joy, shoulders bowed and hands folded, Śilāda, his heart gladdened, praised the Supreme Lord. ॥27॥
3.6.28: Then the blessed god of gods, the three-eyed one, being pleased, said to Śilāda, the bull among sages: I am the giver of boons. ॥28॥
3.6.29: What need have you of this austerity, O great-minded one? I give you a son, all-knowing, who has mastered the meaning of all scriptures. ॥29॥
3.6.30: Then, having heard that and bowed to the lord of gods, Śilāśana spoke, with a voice choked with joy, to the moon-adorned one. ॥30॥
3.6.31: Śilāda said: O Maheśa, if you are pleased, or if you are indeed granting me a boon, I desire a son equal to you, free from death and not born of a womb. ॥31॥
3.6.32: Nandīśvara said: Thus addressed by him, the god Tryambaka Śaṅkara, pleased at heart, replied to Śilāda, best of sages. ॥32॥
3.6.33: Śiva said: Formerly, O brahmin rich in austerity, I was propitiated through austerity by Brahmā, and by the sages and the best of gods, for the sake of my incarnation. ॥33॥
3.6.34: I shall become your son, named Nandī, not born of a womb; and you, O sage, shall be the father of me, the father of the worlds. ॥34॥
3.6.35: Nandīśvara said: Having spoken thus and looked upon the sage, who stood after prostrating, the compassionate Hara, together with Umā, quickly gave him instruction and vanished right there. ॥35॥
3.6.36: When that Mahādeva had gone, the great sage Śilāda went to his own hermitage and then told the sages what had happened. ॥36॥
3.6.37: And after some time, that father of mine, foremost among knowers of sacrifice, quickly ploughed the sacrificial ground for a sacrifice. ॥37॥
3.6.38: Then in an instant, by Śambhu's command, I—born of his body—was born even at the outset of the ploughing, radiant like the fire at the end of an age. ॥38॥
3.6.39: Then the Puṣkara, Āvartaka and other clouds poured rain; the sky-dwellers, Kinnaras, Siddhas and Sādhyas sang; and when I had become the son of Śilāda, the chief sages showered flowers all around. ॥39॥
3.6.40: Then the gods headed by Brahmā and all the wives of the gods came there with great joy, and Hari too, and Śiva and Ambikā. ॥40॥
3.6.41: Then there was a great festival, and the troops of Apsarases danced. Having honoured me and embraced me, they, delighted, praised me. ॥41॥
3.6.42: Having highly commended that Śilāda and having praised Śiva and Śivā with fine hymns, all went to their abodes; Śiva and Śivā, the lords of all, also departed. ॥42॥
3.6.43: Śilāda too, seeing me—radiant like the fire of the sun at the time of dissolution, three-eyed, four-armed, a child, wearing a crown of matted locks— ॥43॥
3.6.44: bearing weapons such as the trident, blazing, in every way having the form of Rudra—he, filled with great bliss, lovingly bowed to me, who was worthy of obeisance. ॥44॥
3.6.45: Śilāda said: Since I have been gladdened by you, O lord of the gods, you are Nandī by name. Therefore I bow to you, the god who is bliss, the lord of the world. ॥45॥
3.6.46: Nandīśvara said: My father, joyful, having bowed deeply to Maheśvara, quickly went with me to his own hut, like a pauper who has found a treasure. ॥46॥
3.6.47: When I had gone to Śilāda's hut, O great sage, then I abandoned that form and assumed a human state. ॥47॥
3.6.48: Seeing me in human form, my father, honoured by the world, lamented, deeply afflicted with grief, surrounded by his kinsmen. ॥48॥
3.6.49: Śilāda, son of Śālaṅkāyana, loving towards his son, performed for me all the rites beginning with the birth ceremony (jātakarma). ॥49॥
3.6.50: In my fifth year my father taught me the Vedas completely, together with their auxiliaries and subsidiary branches, and other scriptures as well. ॥50॥
3.6.51: When my seventh year was complete, two sages named Mitra and Varuṇa came to his hermitage to see me, at the command of the Lord. ॥51॥
3.6.52: Honoured by that sage and comfortably seated, the two great-souled great sages, gazing at me again and again, spoke. ॥52॥
3.6.53: Mitra and Varuṇa said: Dear one, your Nandī, though he has mastered the meaning of all scriptures, is short-lived. Indeed, no life beyond one year from now is seen; we have not seen it. ॥53॥
3.6.54: When the two brahmins had spoken thus, Śilāda, loving his son, embraced him and, stricken with grief, wept loudly in a broken voice. ॥54॥
3.6.55: Seeing my father and grandfather fallen as if dead, I, serene in mind, remembering the lotus feet of Śiva, replied: ॥55॥
3.6.56: From what sorrow, dear father, do you weep, trembling? Whence has your sorrow arisen? I wish to know it truly. ॥56॥
3.6.57: The father said: I am exceedingly grieved by the sorrow of your early death, my little son. Who will remove my sorrow? To him I go for refuge. ॥57॥
3.6.58: The son said: Whether a god or a demon, or Yama or Kāla—even if these, and other beings too, should rise against me, ॥58॥
3.6.59: even so, early death will not befall me; do not torment yourself. I speak the truth, father; I swear it to you. ॥59॥
3.6.60: The father said: What austerity, what knowledge, what yoga, and who is your lord, by which you will evade this dreadful sorrow, my son? ॥60॥
3.6.61: The son said: Not by austerity, father, nor by learning shall I evade death; by the worship of Mahādeva I shall conquer death, not otherwise. ॥61॥
3.6.62: Nandīśvara said: Having said this, O sage, I bowed my head at my father's feet, circumambulated him, and went to an excellent forest. ॥62॥
3.6.iti: Thus ends the sixth adhyāya, named The incarnation as Nandikeśa, in the third saṃhitā, the Śatarudra-saṃhitā, of the Śrī Śivamahāpurāṇa. ॥6॥
3.7.1: Nandīśvara said: Having gone there, O sage, I, wise as I was, stayed in a secluded spot and performed fierce austerity, hard to do even for the best of sages. ॥1॥
3.7.2: Meditating in the cavity of the lotus of my heart on the god Tryambaka, the three-eyed, ten-armed, peaceful, five-faced Sadāśiva, ॥2॥
3.7.3: I performed the japa of the Rudra hymn, established in supreme meditation, on the holy northern bank of the river, single-minded and composed. ॥3॥
3.7.4: Then, pleased with that japa, the Supreme Lord Mahādeva, together with Umā, adorned with the half-moon, satisfied, spoke to me as I stood there. ॥4॥
3.7.5: Śiva said: O son of Śilāda, I am pleased by this austerity and will grant you a boon. Well have you performed austerity, O wise one; tell me what is in your mind. ॥5॥
3.7.6: Thus addressed by the god, I bowed my head at his feet and praised the Supreme Lord, the destroyer of old age and sorrow. ॥6॥
3.7.7: Then Śambhu, seeing me, Nandin, full of supreme devotion, eyes filled with tears, bowed properly with my head at his feet, ॥7॥
3.7.8: the Supreme Lord, remover of the greatest affliction, bull-bannered, raised me up, took hold of me with both hands facing me, and touched me. ॥8॥
3.7.9: Looking at the gaṇa leaders and at the goddess, daughter of Himavat, the Lord of the worlds, gazing on me with a compassionate look, spoke to me: ॥9॥
3.7.10: Dear child Nandin, greatly wise one, whence your fear of death? It was I who sent the two brahmins. You are equal to me, no doubt. ॥10॥
3.7.11: You will be immortal, free from old age, without sorrow, ever a lord of gaṇas, imperishable, undecaying, beloved, together with your father and your friends. ॥11॥
3.7.12: Having my strength, always at my side, you will be dear to me forever. By my grace there will be no old age, birth or death for you. ॥12॥
3.7.13: Nandīśvara said: Having said this, the treasure of compassion took off his own head-garland made of lotuses and quickly tied it around my neck. ॥13॥
3.7.14: By that auspicious garland clinging to my neck, O brahmin, I became three-eyed and ten-armed, like a second Śaṅkara. ॥14॥
3.7.15: Then, taking me by the hand, the Supreme Lord said: Tell me, what excellent boon shall I give you today? ॥15॥
3.7.16: Then the bull-bannered one took water held in his matted locks, pure as a pearl necklace, and saying, become a river here, released it. ॥16॥
3.7.17: Then five rivers began to flow, bringing auspiciousness, with good water, of great speed, divine in form and beautiful. ॥17॥
3.7.18: Jaṭodakā, Trisrotā, Vṛṣadhvani, Svarṇodakā and Jambunadī: thus are the five rivers celebrated. ॥18॥
3.7.19: This is called Pañcanada, auspicious and most closely connected with Śiva; near Japeśvara it is supremely purifying, O sage. ॥19॥
3.7.20: Whoever reaches Pañcanada, bathes, does japa and worships the Lord of lords, surely attains union with Śiva; there is no doubt. ॥20॥
3.7.21: Then Śambhu said to Umā: I shall consecrate Nandin; I shall proclaim him lord of the gaṇas. What do you think, O imperishable one? ॥21॥
3.7.22: Umā said: You should grant it to Nandin, O lord of gods, O Supreme Lord. The son of Śilāda is my most dearly beloved son, O master. ॥22॥
3.7.23: Nandīśvara said: Then that Śaṅkara, the independent Supreme Lord, giver of all, affectionate to devotees, called to mind his own excellent gaṇa leaders. ॥23॥
3.7.24: At Rudra's mere remembrance the lords of gaṇas arrived, countless, greatly joyful, all of them in Śaṅkara's form. ॥24॥
3.7.25: Those gaṇa lords, bowing to Śiva and the Goddess, spoke auspicious words; bowing, with joined hands and lowered shoulders, those mighty ones said: ॥25॥
3.7.26: The chiefs of the attendants said: For what purpose have we been remembered, O god? Command us, great lord, your servants who have come, O destroyer of Tripura, granter of desires. ॥26॥
3.7.27: Shall we dry up the oceans, or slay Yama along with his servants, Death, the Great Death, or especially the aged lotus-born Brahmā? ॥27॥
3.7.28: Shall we bind and bring Indra with the gods, or Viṣṇu with his attendants, or the furious Daityas together with the Dānavas? ॥28॥
3.7.29: On whom shall we bring dreadful calamity today at your command? Or for whom shall there be a festival today, O god, for the fulfilment of all desires? ॥29॥
3.7.30: Nandīśvara said: Hearing these words of the heroically speaking gaṇas, the Supreme Lord praised those gaṇa lords and spoke to them. ॥30॥
3.7.31: Śiva said: This Nandīśvara is my son, lord of lords over all, dear, foremost of the gaṇas. Let my word be carried out by all. ॥31॥
3.7.32: All of you, with love, consecrate him as the refuge and lord of my gaṇas. From today this Nandīśvara is your master. ॥32॥
3.7.33: Nandīśvara said: Thus addressed by Śaṅkara, all those gaṇa leaders said so be it and then brought the requisites. ॥33॥
3.7.34: Then the gods with Indra, those headed by Nārāyaṇa, the sages and the worlds came from all sides with joyful faces. ॥34॥
3.7.35: The Grandsire too, O venerable one, at Śaṅkara's command, attentively performed the entire consecration of Nandin. ॥35॥
3.7.36: Then Viṣṇu, then Śakra, and likewise the guardians of the worlds and the sages, headed by the Grandsire, offered praise. ॥36॥
3.7.37: While they were praising, Viṣṇu, lord of all worlds, placing joined palms on his head, also praised attentively. ॥37॥
3.7.38: With joined palms and bowing, he raised the cry of victory; then all the gaṇa chiefs, then the gods, then the asuras did so. ॥38॥
3.7.39: Thus was I, Nandīśvara, O best of brahmins, praised and consecrated then by the gods together with Brahmā, at the command of the Supreme Lord. ॥39॥
3.7.40: And there, at the command of the Supreme One, my marriage was performed with love by Viṣṇu, Brahmā and the others, accompanied by a great festival. ॥40॥
3.7.41: And the daughter of the Maruts, the charming goddess Suyaśā, divine and a delight to mind and eyes, became my wife. ॥41॥
3.7.42: There, a parasol radiant as the moon was obtained, adorned by her, accompanied by chowries and by groups of women whose fingertips held the chowries. ॥42॥
3.7.43: And the supreme lion-throne was occupied by me together with her; I was adorned by Mahālakṣmī with fine ornaments, a crown and the rest. ॥43॥
3.7.44: Likewise I obtained a supreme necklace that had been on the Goddess's neck, and a lordly bull, a white elephant, a lion, and a lion-banner too. ॥44॥
3.7.45: and a chariot, and an auspicious golden necklace like the disc of the moon; other things too were obtained by me, O sage. ॥45॥
3.7.46: Thus, having been married to that wife, O great sage, I bowed at the feet of Śambhu, of Śivā, of Brahmā and of Hari. ॥46॥
3.7.47: To me, in that state and together with my wife, the Lord of the three worlds, the master Śiva, affectionate to devotees, spoke with supreme love. ॥47॥
3.7.48: Īśvara said: Listen, good son: you are dear, and this Suyaśā is your beloved. With love I grant you the boon that is desired in your mind. ॥48॥
3.7.49: I am always pleased with you, O Nandīśa, lord of the gaṇas, together with the Goddess; dear child, hear my supreme word. ॥49॥
3.7.50: You shall be ever dear and distinguished, endowed with supreme lordship, a great yogin, a great archer, together with your father and grandfather; ॥50॥
3.7.51: invincible, all-conquering, ever worthy of worship, of great strength. Where I am, there you are; and where you are, there too am I. ॥51॥
3.7.52: And this father of yours, son, endowed with supreme lordship, will be a chief of the gaṇas, my devotee, of great strength. ॥52॥
3.7.53: Your grandfather too, dear child—let it be so; these are the decrees. Likewise, having received boons from me, they will come to my presence. ॥53॥
3.7.54: Nandīśvara said: Then the most fortunate Goddess, the giver of boons, said to Nandin: Tell me a boon, son—all desires as you wish. ॥54॥
3.7.55: Hearing that speech of the Goddess, he then spoke with joined palms: May I always have excellent devotion to your feet, O Goddess. ॥55॥
3.7.56: Hearing my words, the Goddess said, so be it, and with great affection spoke to that auspicious Suyaśā, the most beloved of Nandin. ॥56॥
3.7.57: The Goddess said: Dear daughter, receive a boon as you desire: be three-eyed and free from birth; and may there be devotion to me through your sons and grandsons, and likewise to your husband. ॥57॥
3.7.58: Nandīśvara said: Then Brahmā and Viṣṇu and all the hosts of gods, greatly pleased, lovingly gave boons to the two of them at Śiva's command. ॥58॥
3.7.59: Then the Lord Īśāna, taking me with my lineage, along with relatives and kinsmen, mounted the bull and went with the Goddess to his own abode. ॥59॥
3.7.60: Then all those gods headed by Viṣṇu, praising this, went joyfully to their own abodes, extolling the auspicious Śiva. ॥60॥
3.7.61: Thus, dear child, O great sage, my own incarnation has been told to you—ever bringing joy to people and increasing devotion to Śiva. ॥61॥
3.7.62: Whoever would hear, or cause to be heard, this account of Nandin's birth, likewise the bestowal of boons on me, the consecration and the marriage, ॥62॥
3.7.63: or would read it or have it read, full of faith and devotion, enjoys all happiness here and attains the supreme goal hereafter. ॥63॥
3.7.iti: Thus ends the seventh adhyāya, named The consecration and marriage of the incarnation Nandikeśvara, in the third saṃhitā, the Śatarudra-saṃhitā, of the Śrī Śivamahāpurāṇa. ॥7॥
3.8.1: Nandīśvara said: O Sanatkumāra, all-knowing one, listen to the story of Bhairava, by merely hearing which devotion to Śiva becomes firm. ॥1॥
3.8.2: Bhairava is indeed the complete form of Śaṅkara, the Supreme Self. Fools, deluded by Śiva's māyā, do not know him. ॥2॥
3.8.3: O Sanatkumāra, even four-armed Viṣṇu, even four-faced Brahmā does not know the greatness of the Great Lord. ॥3॥
3.8.4: There is nothing surprising in this: Śambhu's māyā is truly hard to comprehend. Deluded by it, all fail even to worship him, the Supreme. ॥4॥
3.8.5: If the Supreme Lord himself makes himself known, then they all know him; no one knows him by his own will. ॥5॥
3.8.6: Though all-pervading, Maheśāna is not seen by the dull-minded. He who transcends minds and words is regarded in the world as just a god. ॥6॥
3.8.7: On this I shall relate an ancient account, O great sage. Listen to it with faith, dear one; it is a supreme cause of knowledge. ॥7॥
3.8.8: All the divine sages went to Lord Brahmā, who was seated on a wondrous, lovely peak of Meru, wishing to know the true reality. ॥8॥
3.8.9: Arriving there and bowing to Brahmā, all those chief sages, with joined palms and bent shoulders, questioned him with great reverence. ॥9॥
3.8.10: The divine sages said: O God of gods, lord of creatures, creator, leader of the worlds, tell us truly: what is the one imperishable reality? ॥10॥
3.8.11: Nandīśvara said: The lotus-born Brahmā, deluded by Maheśa's māyā, not knowing the supreme truth, replied out of self-esteem. ॥11॥
3.8.12: Brahmā said: O gods and sages, all of you, listen attentively with a good mind: I shall tell you truly the supreme, imperishable reality. ॥12॥
3.8.13: I am the womb of the world, the Creator, self-born, unborn, the Lord; I am without beginning, Brahman, the one stainless Self. ॥13॥
3.8.14: I alone set the worlds in motion, I withdraw them and dissolve them; there is no one else greater than me, O best of gods. ॥14॥
3.8.15: Nandīśvara said: As the Creator spoke thus, Viṣṇu, who was present there, O sage, angered and deluded by the unborn māyā, laughingly said these words: ॥15॥
3.8.16: O Brahmā, this foolishness does not befit one endowed with yoga. Not knowing the supreme reality, you speak this in vain. ॥16॥
3.8.17: I am the maker of all the worlds, the Supreme Self, the highest Person, the Sacrifice, the god Nārāyaṇa, lord of māyā, the supreme goal. ॥17॥
3.8.18: O Brahmā, it is by my command that this creation is carried out by you; and there is no life for the worlds if I, the Lord, am disregarded. ॥18॥
3.8.19: Thus quarrelling out of delusion, each desiring victory over the other, they called upon the Vedas, present here in bodily form, as the authority in every respect. ॥19॥
3.8.20: They should especially be asked, for they stand here bearing forms. Having said this, the two questioned all four of them, the knowers of authority. ॥20॥
3.8.21: Brahmā and Viṣṇu said: O Vedas, you are the authority everywhere and have attained the highest standing. Tell us confidently: what is the one imperishable reality? ॥21॥
3.8.22: Nandīśvara said: Hearing their words, the Ṛg and the other Vedas, all remembering the Supreme Lord, spoke truthfully again. ॥22॥
3.8.23: If we are respected by you, O two mighty gods who bring about creation and preservation, then we shall state the authority that dispels your doubt. ॥23॥
3.8.24: Nandīśvara said: Hearing the condition stated by the Śrutis, the two gods said to them: What you say is authority for us; let the reality be properly stated. ॥24॥
3.8.25: The Ṛgveda said: That within which all beings abide, from which everything proceeds, which they call the supreme reality — that is Rudra alone, the One. ॥25॥
3.8.26: The Yajurveda said: The Lord who is worshipped by all sacrifices and by yoga, through whom we are indeed authoritative — he is the one all-seeing Śiva. ॥26॥
3.8.27: The Sāmaveda said: He by whom this universe is set revolving, who is contemplated by yogins, by whose light the universe shines — he is the one supreme Tryambaka. ॥27॥
3.8.28: The Atharvaṇaveda said: The Lord of gods whom people favoured through devotion behold — him they call the One, Kaivalya liberation itself, Śaṅkara, beyond sorrow. ॥28॥
3.8.29: Nandīśvara said: Hearing this declared by the Śrutis, Brahmā and Hari, utterly deluded by māyā and bereft of sense, smiled and said to those Vedas: ॥29॥
3.8.30: Brahmā and Hari said: O Vedas, what is this you say, as if you had lost your senses? What has happened to you today? All your excellent, supreme knowledge is lost. ॥30॥
3.8.31: How can that lord of the Pramathas — who sports ceaselessly with Śivā, naked, yellowish in hue, grey with dust, ॥31॥
3.8.32: of hideous attire, matted-haired, riding a bull, adorned with snakes — have attained the state of the supreme Brahman? And where is that Brahman which is free of attachment? ॥32॥
3.8.33: Hearing what they had said, the all-pervading Praṇava, formless yet assuming form, manifesting with goodwill, spoke to the two. ॥33॥
3.8.34: The Praṇava said: The Lord, the blessed Rudra, Hara, who takes on forms in play, never sports with a Śakti separate from himself. ॥34॥
3.8.35: He is the Supreme Lord, self-luminous, eternal; and this Śakti of his, Śivā, whose nature is bliss, is not something adventitious. ॥35॥
3.8.36: Nandīśvara said: Though thus addressed, the ignorance of Brahmā and Viṣṇu was not then destroyed, owing to the māyā of Śrīkaṇṭha alone. ॥36॥
3.8.37: Then a great light appeared between the two, filling with its own radiance the space between heaven and earth. ॥37॥
3.8.38: There, in the middle of the circle of light, O sage, a figure in human form with a most wondrous body was seen by Brahmā and Viṣṇu. ॥38॥
3.8.39: Then Brahmā's fifth head blazed with anger: Who is this who bears a human form between the two of us? ॥39॥
3.8.40: Even as Brahmā was pondering thus, in an instant that three-eyed Great Person, blue and red Nīlalohita, was seen. ॥40॥
3.8.41: He appeared trident in hand, with an eye on his forehead, adorned with serpents and the moon. Seeing him, Hiraṇyagarbha, deluded, laughed and said: ॥41॥
3.8.42: Brahmā said: O Nīlalohita, I know you; do not be afraid, O Candraśekhara. Long ago you came forth from my forehead as Rudra. ॥42॥
3.8.43: Because of your weeping, I also gave you the name Rudra long ago. Take refuge in me alone, son; I will protect you. ॥43॥
3.8.44: Nandīśvara said: Then the Lord, hearing the arrogant words of the lotus-born one, became exceedingly angry at that moment, as if about to bring about dissolution, O sage. ॥44॥
3.8.45: The Supreme Lord, out of anger, brought forth a certain being, Bhairava, blazing with great splendour, and with affection spoke to him: ॥45॥
3.8.46: Īśvara said: First, this lotus-born one is to be punished by you, O Kālabhairava. You shine like Kāla (Time) himself; therefore you are Kālarāja. ॥46॥
3.8.47: You are able to sustain the universe; because you are terrifying you are called Bhairava. Even Kāla will fear you; therefore you are Kālabhairava. ॥47॥
3.8.48: Since you, when angered, will crush the wicked-souled, you will gain fame everywhere as Āmardaka (the Crusher). ॥48॥
3.8.49: Since you will devour the sins of devotees at that very instant, your name will be Pāpabhakṣaṇa (Devourer of Sins). ॥49॥
3.8.50: Kāśī, my city of liberation, greater than all cities — sovereignty over it is yours forever, O Kālarāja. ॥50॥
3.8.51: Of the sinful men there, you alone are the punisher; and Citragupta will record their deeds, good and bad. ॥51॥
3.8.52: Nandīśvara said: Having received these boons, Kālabhairava then, at that very moment, cut off Vidhi's head with the tip of the nail of his left finger. ॥52॥
3.8.53: Whichever limb offends, that alone should be punished. Therefore the fifth head, by which the censure was uttered, was cut off. ॥53॥
3.8.54: Then, seeing Vidhi's head severed, Hari, greatly frightened, praised Śaṅkara with devotion using the Śatarudriya mantras. ॥54॥
3.8.55: Hiraṇyagarbha too, frightened, recited the Śatarudriya. Thus those two became free of pride at that very moment, O sage. ॥55॥
3.8.56: They attained the knowledge that Śiva is directly the Supreme Brahman, characterized by being, consciousness and bliss, the Supreme Self, beyond the guṇas. ॥56॥
3.8.57: O omniscient Sanatkumāra, hear from me this supremely auspicious truth: as long as there is pride, so long is knowledge especially concealed. ॥57॥
3.8.58: Having given up self-conceit, a person comes to know the Supreme Lord. The Lord of the universe destroys the proud, having become the remover of pride. ॥58॥
3.8.59: Then the Supreme Lord, knowing Viṣṇu and Vidhi to be free of pride, became pleased; the Lord Mahādeva made them both fearless. ॥59॥
3.8.60: Having reassured the two, Mahādeva, pleased and affectionate to those who bow to him, spoke to his other form, that matted-haired Bhairava. ॥60॥
3.8.61: Mahādeva said: This Viṣṇu is to be honoured by you, and likewise Śatadhṛti (Brahmā) himself. And carry Vedhas's skull, O Nīlalohita. ॥61॥
3.8.62: For the removal of the sin of brahmin-slaying, show the world this vow: having adopted the skull-vow, wander constantly for alms. ॥62॥
3.8.63: Having said this, Śiva, whose form is radiance, brought forth, while he (Bhairava) looked on, a maiden renowned as Brahmahatyā, and spoke to her: ॥63॥
3.8.64: Until this one reaches the divine city of Vārāṇasī, until then you follow this terrible Kāla of fierce form. ॥64॥
3.8.65: You may enter everywhere except the city of Vārāṇasī. When he goes to Vārāṇasī, at that very instant be released from him. ॥65॥
3.8.66: Nandīśvara said: Having thus appointed that Brahmahatyā, the Lord Śiva, greatly wondrous, then vanished from there. ॥66॥
3.8.iti: Thus ends the eighth adhyāya, named The incarnation as Bhairava, in the third saṃhitā, the Śatarudra-saṃhitā, of the Śrī Śivamahāpurāṇa. ॥8॥
3.9.1: Nandīśvara said: O omniscient Sanatkumāra, listen with delight to another story of Bhairava, which destroys great sins and increases devotion. ॥1॥
3.9.2: Bhairava too, Kāla, who brings even Time to its end, was accompanied by her Brahmahatyā; at the word of the God of gods he bore the Kāpālika vow, ॥2॥
3.9.3: and, skull in hand, the Self of the universe wandered through the three worlds; yet the dreadful Brahmahatyā did not leave that god. ॥3॥
3.9.4: Though wandering to every sacred ford, he was not freed from Brahmahatyā. From this let the whole greatness of the foe of Kāma be understood. ॥4॥
3.9.5: Once Hara, though attended by the Pramathas, roaming freely as a Kāpālika, went to the abode of Nārāyaṇa. ॥5॥
3.9.6: Then, seeing Bhairava approaching—Mahākāla, three-eyed, with serpents for earrings, born of a portion of Mahādeva, yet of complete form— ॥6॥
3.9.7: having seen him, the Garuḍa-bannered Viṣṇu fell flat on the ground like a stick, and so did the gods, the sages and the celestial women all around. ॥7॥
3.9.8: Then Viṣṇu, the lord of Kamalā, having bowed to him, came forward and, placing his joined palms on his head, praised him with various hymns. ॥8॥
3.9.9: Then, O great sage, Hari, joyful and serene at heart, gladly spoke to Padmā, who dwells in the lotus and arose from the churning of the milk-ocean. ॥9॥
3.9.10: Viṣṇu said: Beloved, look, O lotus-eyed one. You are blessed, O fortunate and sinless one; and I am blessed, O goddess of lovely hips, since we two behold the Lord of the world. ॥10॥
3.9.11: He is the sustainer and the ordainer of the worlds, their master and Lord; beginningless, the refuge, the tranquil one, the twenty-sixth principle, standing before us. ॥11॥
3.9.12: He is omniscient, lord of all yogins, the sole leader of all beings, the inner Self of all beings, ever the giver of everything to all. ॥12॥
3.9.13: He whom the sleepless, those who have stilled their breath, the tranquil ones devoted to meditation, see with their intellect in the heart—behold him here, O Padmā. ॥13॥
3.9.14: He whom knowers of the essence of the Veda and yogins with controlled minds know—he, the formless, having taken form, is coming here, the all-pervading one. ॥14॥
3.9.15: Ah, how wondrous is the conduct of the supreme God! For one who constantly utters his name there is no further body, yet he himself bears a body. ॥15॥
3.9.16: Having seen him, men on earth do not obtain rebirth. He, the blessed Tryambaka adorned with the moon, is coming here. ॥16॥
3.9.17: Blessed today are my two eyes, long as lotus petals, O Lakṣmī, since Mahādeva, the great Lord, is seen by them. ॥17॥
3.9.18: Fie, fie on the status of the gods, where, even after seeing the supreme Śaṅkara, nirvāṇa, which puts an end to all sorrow, is not attained! ॥18॥
3.9.19: In the world of the gods there is nothing more inauspicious than godhood, since all of us, even having seen the Lord of gods, do not obtain liberation. ॥19॥
3.9.20: Nandīśvara said: Having spoken thus, Hṛṣīkeśa, his hair bristling with delight, bowed down to Mahādeva, the bull-bannered one, and said this: ॥20॥
3.9.21: Viṣṇu said: What is this being done by you, O all-pervading one, God of gods, omniscient sustainer of the worlds, O imperishable remover of all sins? ॥21॥
3.9.22: This is your play, O Lord of gods, three-eyed, great-minded one. What is the reason for this conduct of yours, O Virūpākṣa, tormentor of Smara? ॥22॥
3.9.23: For what purpose, O blessed Śambhu, lord of Śakti, do you go about begging alms? This is my doubt, O Lord of the world, giver of sovereignty over the three worlds. ॥23॥
3.9.24: Nandīśvara said: Thus addressed by Viṣṇu, Śambhu—Hara as Bhairava, the lord of wondrous deeds—then replied to Viṣṇu, laughing. ॥24॥
3.9.25: Bhairava said: Brahmā's head was cut off by the tip of the nail of my finger; to destroy that sin I am observing this auspicious vow. ॥25॥
3.9.26: Nandīśvara said: Thus addressed by Maheśa as Bhairava, the lord of Ramā reflected for a moment, and with head slightly bowed, again submitted thus: ॥26॥
3.9.27: Viṣṇu said: Sport as you wish, O remover of all obstacles; but, Mahādeva, you should not cover me with your illusion. ॥27॥
3.9.28: From the cup of the lotus of my navel, in age after age of old, lotus-seated Brahmās arose by the millions, through the power of your command, O all-pervading one. ॥28॥
3.9.29: Give up this illusion, O God, hard to cross for those of unperfected self; Brahmā and the others, O Mahādeva, are deluded by your illusion. ॥29॥
3.9.30: I understand your conduct as it truly is, O lord of Śivā, only by your grace, O Śambhu, Lord of all, goal of the good. ॥30॥
3.9.31: When the time of dissolution arrives and you, O Hara, withdraw all the sages together with the gods, and the worlds with their classes and stages of life— ॥31॥
3.9.32: then, O Mahādeva, though sin such as the slaying of Brahmā is committed, there is no subjection to it for you, O Śambhu; therefore you sport freely. ॥32॥
3.9.33: A garland of the bones of past Brahmās shines on your neck; even so, O sinless Śambhu, Brahmahatyā follows you. ॥33॥
3.9.34: Even having committed a very great sin, the man who remembers you, O Lord, the support of the worlds—his sin dissolves away. ॥34॥
3.9.35: Just as darkness cannot remain in the presence of the sun, so the sin of one who is your devotee goes to destruction. ॥35॥
3.9.36: The virtuous soul who meditates on your two lotus feet—even his sin of brahmin-slaying goes to destruction. ॥36॥
3.9.37: O Lord of the world, the man whose speech is devoted to your name—sin, even if equal to a mountain peak, does not afflict him. ॥37॥
3.9.38: O Supreme Self, supreme abode, who assume a form by your own will, O Lord, this subjection like that of a wretched one is merely your playful whim, O Īśvara. ॥38॥
3.9.39: Today I am blessed, O Lord of gods, since I see him whom the yogins do not see—the supreme, imperishable Lord whose form is the universe. ॥39॥
3.9.40: Today is my supreme gain, today my supreme blessing; having seen you, for me, sated with nectar, heaven and liberation are mere straw. ॥40॥
3.9.41: While Govinda was speaking thus, that pure Padmā Lakṣmī placed in the bowl alms named Manorathavatī ('wish-fulfilling'). ॥41॥
3.9.42: The god then went forth on his alms-round with supreme joy; Mahādeva as Bhairava, having taken on a bodily form, went to other places as well. ॥42॥
3.9.43: Seeing her following him, Janārdana called Brahmahatyā to him and entreated her: Release the trident-bearer. ॥43॥
3.9.44: Brahmahatyā said: Under this very pretext I shall serve this bull-bannered one, whose sight frees one from rebirth, and so purify myself. ॥44॥
3.9.45: Nandīśvara said: Though addressed by Murāri, she did not leave his side. Then Śambhu, as Bhairava, with a smiling face, spoke these words to Hari. ॥45॥
3.9.46: Bhairava said: By drinking the nectar of your words I am satisfied, O giver of great honour. What you say, O lord of Mā, is indeed the very nature of the good. ॥46॥
3.9.47: Choose a boon, Govinda; I am ready to grant you a boon, O sinless one. You, O Hari, free from all change, are the foremost of my devotees. ॥47॥
3.9.48: Mendicants are not delighted even by finely prepared alms so much as those feverish from the begging round are by drinking the nectar of respect. ॥48॥
3.9.49: Nandīśvara said: Having heard these words of Śambhu Bhairava, the supreme Self, Viṣṇu became exceedingly pleased and spoke to Maheśvara. ॥49॥
3.9.50: Viṣṇu said: This alone is the praiseworthy boon: that I behold you, the lord of the deities, O God of gods, who lie beyond the path of mind and speech. ॥50॥
3.9.51: This nectar-like glance is abundant; through it I have a great festival. This sight of you, O Hara, is for the good the gaining of a treasure without effort. ॥51॥
3.9.52: May there be no separation for me, O God, from your pair of feet. This alone is the boon, Śambhu; I choose no other boon. ॥52॥
3.9.53: Śrī Bhairava said: Let it be for you just as you have said, dear one, O great-minded one. You will also be the giver of boons to all the gods. ॥53॥
3.9.54: Nandīśvara said: Having thus favoured the enemy of the Daityas, and wandering through regions, mountains and worlds, he reached the city Avimukta, the city named Vārāṇasī. ॥54॥
3.9.55: Then, the moment Bhairava of terrifying form entered the sacred field, Brahmahatyā cried alas and at once entered the netherworld (Pātāla). ॥55॥
3.9.56: Brahmā's skull at once fell from Bhairava's lotus-hand to the ground; that place became the tīrtha Kapālamocana ('release of the skull'). ॥56॥
3.9.57: Seeing Brahmā's skull falling from his hand while all looked on, Rudra danced with supreme joy. ॥57॥
3.9.58: The skull of Vidhi (Brahmā), utterly unbearable, did not leave the hand of the Supreme as he wandered anywhere else; in Kāśī it fell away in an instant. ॥58॥
3.9.59: The sin of slaying Brahmā, which did not leave the trident-bearer anywhere, perished in Kāśī in an instant; therefore Kāśikā should indeed be resorted to. ॥59॥
3.9.60: Whoever remembers Kapālamocana, the supreme tīrtha in Kāśī — whatever sin he has done here or elsewhere quickly perishes. ॥60॥
3.9.61: Coming to this best of tīrthas, bathing according to rule, and offering libations to the ancestors and gods, one is freed from the sin of brahmin-slaying. ॥61॥
3.9.62: Placing the tīrtha Kapālamocana before him, Bhairava stayed right there, devouring the continuous stream of his devotees' sins. ॥62॥
3.9.63: On the eighth day of the dark fortnight of the month Mārgaśīrṣa, the Supreme Lord, engaged in noble sport and dear to the good, manifested in the form of Bhairava. ॥63॥
3.9.64: On the dark eighth of Mārgaśīrṣa, one who fasts and keeps vigil in the presence of Kālabhairava is freed from great sins. ॥64॥
3.9.65: Even elsewhere, the man who performs that vow with devotion, together with the vigil, will be freed from great sins and go to a good destiny. ॥65॥
3.9.66: Whatever sin has been committed by living beings over many myriads of births — all of it dissolves through the sight of Kālabhairava. ॥66॥
3.9.67: Whoever commits offences against the devotees of Kālabhairava, that fool becomes wretched and again falls into an evil state. ॥67॥
3.9.68: Those who are devoted to Viśveśvara but not devoted to Kālabhairava obtain great suffering, and especially in Kāśī. ॥68॥
3.9.69: The man who lives in Vārāṇasī yet does not worship Bhairava — his sins grow like the moon in the bright fortnight. ॥69॥
3.9.70: Whoever in Kāśī does not worship Kālarāja on every fourteenth (bhūta), eighth and Tuesday — his merit wanes like the moon in the dark fortnight. ॥70॥
3.9.71: Having heard this sacred narrative, called The Origin of Bhairava, which removes the sin of brahmin-slaying, one is freed from all sins. ॥71॥
3.9.72: Even one confined in prison, even one who has met the gravest calamity, would be freed from distress by hearing of Bhairava's manifestation. ॥72॥
3.9.iti: Thus ends the ninth adhyāya, named The sport of the Bhairava incarnation, in the third saṃhitā, the Śatarudra-saṃhitā, of the Śrī Śivamahāpurāṇa. ॥9॥
3.10.1: Nandīśvara said: The destroyer of Dakṣa's sacrifice, named Vīrabhadra, should be known as an incarnation of the Lord Śiva, the Supreme Self. ॥1॥
3.10.2: His story has been told in full in the account of Satī; you too have heard it many times, so it is not narrated here at great length. ॥2॥
3.10.3: Next, O best of sages, out of affection for you I shall tell it: hear of the incarnation called Śārdūla of the Lord Śaṅkara. ॥3॥
3.10.4: For the welfare of the gods, Sadāśiva assumed a wondrous, divine Śarabha form, radiant like blazing flames. ॥4॥
3.10.5: Śiva's incarnations are countless, bringing good to true devotees; O best of sages, it is impossible to count them. ॥5॥
3.10.6: The stars of the sky, the dust particles of the earth, and the drops of rain may perhaps at some time be counted by one grown old over many kalpas— ॥6॥
3.10.7: —counting them is possible for the very wise over many births, but not of Śiva's incarnations; know my word to be true. ॥7॥
3.10.8: Even so, according to my understanding and as I have heard, I shall tell the divine Śarabha story, which reveals his supreme lordship. ॥8॥
3.10.9: When Jaya and Vijaya were cursed by you sages, then, O sage, the two were born as sons of Diti from Kaśyapa. ॥9॥
3.10.10: Hiraṇyakaśipu was the elder, and the mighty Hiraṇyākṣa the younger; those two attendants of Viṣṇu were born as the sons of Diti. ॥10॥
3.10.11: Formerly, entreated by the Creator for the uplifting of the earth, the Lord Viṣṇu, assuming the form of a boar, slew Hiraṇyākṣa. ॥11॥
3.10.12: Hearing that his heroic brother, dear as his own life, had been slain, Hiraṇyakaśipu became extremely angry with Hari, O sage. ॥12॥
3.10.13: After performing austerities for ten thousand years, he obtained a boon from the pleased Brahmā: May no one in your creation kill me. ॥13॥
3.10.14: Going to the city called Śoṇita, summoning the gods from all sides, and bringing the three worlds under his control, he ruled a kingdom free of foes. ॥14॥
3.10.15: The sinful Hiraṇyakaśipu, O sage, destroyer of all dharma and tormentor of the twice-born, oppressed the gods and sages. ॥15॥
3.10.16: When the king of the Daityas, an enemy of Hari above all, showed hatred toward his own son Prahlāda, a devotee of Hari, ॥16॥
3.10.17: then, O sage, Viṣṇu swiftly appeared from a pillar of the assembly hall at twilight, filled with wrath, in the form of Nṛsiṃha. ॥17॥
3.10.18: O tiger among sages, the terrible body of the Man-Lion blazed forth, utterly frightening, terrifying the foremost Daityas. ॥18॥
3.10.19: Then the Daityas were slain by Nṛsiṃha in that very instant, and Hiraṇyakaśipu then waged a most dreadful battle. ॥19॥
3.10.20: A great battle took place between the two for a muhūrta, O best of sages—fierce, fearsome, and hair-raising for all. ॥20॥
3.10.21: At dusk, Nṛsiṃha, the lord of the gods and lord of Ramā, dragged the chief of Daityas to the threshold, while the gods watched from the sky. ॥21॥
3.10.22: Then, placing him on his lap, he swiftly tore open his belly with his nails and killed him as the dwellers of heaven looked on. ॥22॥
3.10.23: When Hiraṇyakaśipu was slain by Viṣṇu as Nṛsiṃha, the world then regained its well-being, but the gods in particular did not. ॥23॥
3.10.24: The gods' kettledrums sounded; Prahlāda was astonished, and Lakṣmī too was amazed on seeing the wondrous form of Hari. ॥24॥
3.10.25: Although the lord of Daityas was slain, the gods did not attain complete happiness, for that blaze of Nṛsiṃha did not subside. ॥25॥
3.10.26: By it the whole world was again thrown into turmoil, and the gods fell into distress, thinking: What will happen now? ॥26॥
3.10.27: Speaking thus, the gods headed by the Lotus-born Brahmā, tormented by the blaze born of Nṛsiṃha's wrath, stood far off out of fear. ॥27॥
3.10.28: They sent Prahlāda near Hari to pacify it; entreated by all of them together, Prahlāda then went. ॥28॥
3.10.29: Nṛsiṃha, the treasury of compassion, embraced him to his chest; his heart grew cool, yet the blaze of wrath did not subside. ॥29॥
3.10.30: When even so the Man-Lion's blaze of wrath did not subside, the gods, distressed, sought refuge with Śaṅkara. ॥30॥
3.10.31: Going there, all the gods headed by Brahmā, and the sages too, praised Śaṅkara for the happiness of the worlds. ॥31॥
3.10.32: The gods said: O God of gods, Mahādeva, loving to those who come for refuge, protect us, all the gods who have sought refuge, and the worlds. ॥32॥
3.10.33: Salutations to you, salutations to you, salutations to you, O Sadāśiva. Whenever distress arose before, we were protected by you. ॥33॥
3.10.34: When the ocean was churned and the gods divided the jewels, then, O Śambhu, the poison was taken by you. ॥34॥
3.10.35: Then we were protected, O Lord, and you became known as Nīlakaṇṭha; had you not drunk the poison, all would then have been reduced to ashes. ॥35॥
3.10.36: It is well known, O Lord, that whenever anyone has distress, then by your name alone all distress dissolves. ॥36॥
3.10.37: Now, O Sadāśiva, protect us who are tormented by the Man-Lion's blaze; you, O God, are surely able to quell it. ॥37॥
3.10.38: Nandīśvara said: Thus praised by the gods, Śaṅkara, the supreme Lord, loving to his devotees, gracious at heart, granted fearlessness and replied. ॥38॥
3.10.39: Śaṅkara said: Go to your own abodes, all you gods headed by Brahmā, free from fear. I shall quell this distress entirely; that indeed is my vow. ॥39॥
3.10.40: Whoever has come to me for refuge, his distress has come to an end. One who has sought refuge in me is dearer to me than life itself; there is no doubt. ॥40॥
3.10.41: Nandīśvara said: Having heard this, the gods then attained supreme joy, and they went back the way they had come, joyfully remembering Śaṅkara. ॥41॥
3.10.iti: Thus ends the tenth adhyāya, named The story of Nṛsiṃha, in the Śārdūla incarnation, in the third saṃhitā, the Śatarudra-saṃhitā, of the Śrī Śivamahāpurāṇa. ॥10॥
3.11.1: Nandīśvara said: Thus entreated by the gods, the Supreme Lord, abode of compassion, resolved to withdraw the great fiery energy called Nṛsiṃha. ॥1॥
3.11.2: Thereupon Rudra called to mind the mighty Vīrabhadra, whom he declared to be his own terrible (Bhairava) form, the bringer of dissolution. ॥2॥
3.11.3: Then at once there came, laughing, the foremost of the gaṇas, with excellent gaṇas laughing loudly and leaping here and there, ॥3॥
3.11.4: surrounded by crores of exceedingly fierce beings in the form of Nṛsiṃha, and on all sides by heroes who were frenzied, dancing and filled with joy, ॥4॥
3.11.5: and by great heroes playing with Brahmā and the others as if with balls, and by other beings never seen before—thus encircled, honoured by heroes, ॥5॥
3.11.6: blazing like the fire at the end of the aeon, with three shining eyes, weaponless, with matted locks, adorned with the radiant crescent moon, ॥6॥
3.11.7: with a pair of sharp budding tusks shaped like the curve of the crescent moon, with creeper-like brows resembling a segment of Indra's bow (the rainbow), ॥7॥
3.11.8: deafening the quarters with his tremendously fierce huṃ roar, dark as a blue cloud or collyrium, terrifying, bearded, wondrous, ॥8॥
3.11.9: whirling again and again with his two unbroken arms the instrument-piece and the three-pointed trident—the blessed Vīrabhadra too, swelling with heroic power, ॥9॥
3.11.10: himself submitted: What is the reason for calling me to mind here? Command me, O Lord of the world; let your grace be shown to me. ॥10॥
3.11.11: Nandīśvara said: Having heard these words spoken by Vīrabhadra with respect, and regarding him with affection, Maheśāna, who wields the rod against the wicked, spoke. ॥11॥
3.11.12: Śaṅkara said: An untimely, dreadful fear has arisen even among the gods. That fire of Nṛsiṃha is blazing; pacify it, hard to approach as it is. ॥12॥
3.11.13: First, consoling him, bring him to understanding. If by that he is not calmed, then reveal my supreme terrible form. ॥13॥
3.11.14: Withdrawing the subtle by the subtle and the gross by gross energy, bring that fire under control, O Vīrabhadra, by my command. ॥14॥
3.11.15: Nandīśvara said: Thus commanded, the chief of the gaṇas assumed a calm form and went swiftly to where the Man-Lion was. ॥15॥
3.11.16: Then Vīrabhadra, a form of Hara, addressed Hari; the Lord spoke words as a father to his own son. ॥16॥
3.11.17: Vīrabhadra said: O Lord Mādhava, you have descended for the happiness of the world. You, a supreme lord, have been appointed by the Supreme Being for its preservation. ॥17॥
3.11.18: Long ago, in the single ocean, you, the Lord in the form of a fish, bound the hidden host of creatures with your tail alone and moved about carrying them. ॥18॥
3.11.19: In the form of a tortoise you bear the earth; by the Boar the earth was lifted up; by this lion form Hiraṇyakaśipu has been slain. ॥19॥
3.11.20: Again, as Vāmana striding forth, you bound Bali. You alone are the origin of all beings, the imperishable Lord. ॥20॥
3.11.21: Whenever any sorrow arises for the world, then you descend and will make it free of affliction. ॥21॥
3.11.22: O Hari, there is none greater than you, nor even equal to you, in devotion to Śiva. By you the Vedas and the dharmas are established on the auspicious path. ॥22॥
3.11.23: That demon for whose sake this incarnation took place, Hiraṇyakaśipu, has indeed been slain, and Prahlāda too is well protected. ॥23॥
3.11.24: O Lord, your Man-Lion body is exceedingly terrible. O Soul of the universe, withdraw it yourself in my presence. ॥24॥
3.11.25: Nandīśvara said: Addressed thus by Vīrabhadra in gentle speech, Nṛsiṃha, greatly arrogant, became even more terribly enraged. ॥25॥
3.11.26: And then, O sage, terrifying the great hero Vīrabhadra with his fangs, he spoke very dreadful, harsh words. ॥26॥
3.11.27: Nṛsiṃha said: Go back to where you came from; do not speak to me of my good. Now I shall destroy this world of moving and unmoving beings. ॥27॥
3.11.28: For the destroyer there is no destruction, either from himself or from another. My rule extends everywhere; there is no ruler over me at all. ॥28॥
3.11.29: By my grace everything proceeds free from fear. I indeed am the one who sets in motion and withdraws all powers. ॥29॥
3.11.30: Whatever being is glorious, splendid or mighty, know that, O chief of the gaṇas, to be an expansion of my splendour. ॥30॥
3.11.31: The deities know me alone as the Supreme, the knower of ultimate truth. Brahmā, Śakra and the other gods, endowed with power, are portions of me. ॥31॥
3.11.32: Long ago Brahmā, maker of the world, was born from the lotus of my navel. I am supreme over all, independent, the creator, the destroyer, lord of all. ॥32॥
3.11.33: This is my supreme splendour; what more do you wish to hear? Therefore, taking refuge in me, go, free from anxiety. ॥33॥
3.11.34: Know, O lord of the gaṇas, this supreme state that has come into being: the entire universe, with gods, demons and humans, is mine. ॥34॥
