3.11.35: I am Time, the cause of the world's destruction; I have set out to withdraw the worlds. Know me, O Vīrabhadra, as the death of Death; these gods live by my grace. ॥35॥
3.11.36: Nandīśvara said: Hearing Hari's arrogant words, Vīrabhadra of immeasurable prowess laughed and then spoke contemptuously, his lip quivering. ॥36॥
3.11.37: Vīrabhadra said: Do you not know Pinākin, the Lord of the universe, the destroyer? False talk and quarrel lead to nothing but destruction for you. ॥37॥
3.11.38: Which of your various incarnations now remain? They were brought about by someone or other; you will remain only as a tale. ॥38॥
3.11.39: Name that fault through which you have come to such a state. By that One skilled in destruction you will be brought to a mere remnant, like Dakṣa's sacrifice. ॥39॥
3.11.40: You are Prakṛti; Rudra is the Person (Puruṣa); his seed is deposited in you. From the lotus of your navel was born the five-faced Grandsire Brahmā. ॥40॥
3.11.41: For the creation of the three worlds, he Brahmā, established in fierce austerity, meditated in his forehead on Śaṅkara, the blue-red one (Nīlalohita). ॥41॥
3.11.42: From his forehead Śambhu arose for the sake of creation; by him Brahmā was adorned. Therefore I, of that god of gods who has the form of Bhairava, — ॥42॥
3.11.43: — am appointed for your destruction, with both restraint and force, by Rudra, the god of gods, the lord of all, O Hari. ॥43॥
3.11.44: Having merely torn apart a single demon, while endowed with a fraction of his power, you roar tirelessly in the arrogance of your ego. ॥44॥
3.11.45: A kindness done to the good is indeed held to lead to happiness; but a kindness done to the wicked leads only to harm. ॥45॥
3.11.46: If, O Nṛsiṃha, you regard the great lord as one who has been born again, then you are ignorant, greatly conceited, and wholly subject to distortion. ॥46॥
3.11.47: You are not the creator, not the destroyer, nor even the sustainer, O little Nṛsiṃha; you are dependent, deluded in mind, and never independent anywhere. ॥47॥
3.11.48: Like a potter's wheel you are set in motion by the power of Pinākin; you, the maker of various incarnations, are always dependent on him, O Hari. ॥48॥
3.11.49: Even today the skull of you, when you were in the form of a tortoise, lies set, burnt, in the middle of Hara's necklace-string — yet is no one restrained by this? ॥49॥
3.11.50: Have you forgotten how, by his portion, you in the boar form were tormented by the uprooting of your tusk, crying out today in the hand of the obstacle-remover, by the foe of Tāraka? ॥50॥
3.11.51: See: you were burnt by the fire of the trident, under the guise of Viṣvaksena; at Dakṣa's sacrifice your head was cut off by me, embodied as splendour. ॥51॥
3.11.52: Even today the fifth head of Brahmā, your son, once cut off, has not been restored again; O Hari, have you forgotten that? ॥52॥
3.11.53: You, together with the hosts of Maruts, were defeated by Dadhīca in battle; how, as you scratch your head, have you forgotten that? ॥53॥
3.11.54: The discus dear to you, O Cakrapāṇi — from whose prowess was it obtained, by whom was it made? That too you have forgotten. ॥54॥
3.11.55: When all the worlds are seized in dissolution by me, you lie in the ocean overpowered by sleep; how then are you called sāttvika? ॥55॥
3.11.56: From you down to a blade of grass, everything is the unfolding of Rudra's power; and though you appear endowed with power all around, you are deluded by his fire. ॥56॥
3.11.57: No person is able to behold the greatness of that splendour; only those who are not gross perceive that supreme abode of Viṣṇu. ॥57॥
3.11.58: Of heaven and earth, of Indra and Agni, of Yama and of Varuṇa, within the belly of darkness and in the moon, the Supreme Lord is the generator. ॥58॥
3.11.59: You are Time; Maheśvara is the Great Time, the Time of Time. Therefore, by his fierce portion, you will meet the death of death. ॥59॥
3.11.60: He is steady, imperishable, the hero, the hero, the protector of all, the lord, the destroyer of fever, the terrible one — beast, bird, golden. ॥60॥
3.11.61: The ruler of the entire world is not you, nor the four-faced Brahmā, nor others; Śambhu alone is the ruler of all — there is no doubt. ॥61॥
3.11.62: Having thus considered everything — him whose very self is destruction — do not, by your own doing, bring yourself to ruin, O foolish man-lion. ॥62॥
3.11.63: Otherwise, now death from the wrath of the one in the form of Mahābhairava will fall upon you, like a thunderbolt upon a tree-trunk. ॥63॥
3.11.64: Nandīśvara said: Having spoken thus, Vīrabhadra, who feared nothing from any quarter — he, the embodiment of Śiva's wrath — fell silent, having observed Nṛsiṃha's intention. ॥64॥
3.11.iti: Thus ends the eleventh adhyāya, named The incarnation as Śarabha, in the third saṃhitā, the Śatarudra-saṃhitā, of the Śrī Śivamahāpurāṇa. ॥11॥
3.12.1: Sanatkumāra said: O Nandīśvara, most wise one, you know what happened after that. Show me kindness and, out of affection, tell it to me now. ॥1॥
3.12.2: Nandīśvara said: Addressed thus by Vīrabhadra, Nṛsiṃha, overwhelmed with anger, roared and rushed forward to seize him. ॥2॥
3.12.3: Meanwhile a radiance of Śiva arose: exceedingly terrible, a visible cause of fear, pervading the sky, and irresistible. ॥3॥
3.12.4: Then in a moment that form of Vīrabhadra became invisible. That radiance was golden and gentle, neither of the sun nor born of fire, ॥4॥
3.12.5: not like lightning or the moon, incomparable, belonging to Maheśvara. Then all radiances merged into that Śaṅkara. ॥5॥
3.12.6: Then the sky was no longer to be seen. That great radiance became manifest within it, marked with the emblems common to Rudra, and of a monstrous shape. ॥6॥
3.12.7: Then, as all the gods looked on, amid auspicious sounds such as cries of victory, the Supreme Lord became clearly manifest in the form of destruction: ॥7॥
3.12.8: thousand-armed, with matted hair, with the half-moon as his crest; a bird with a mighty, fierce body, two wings and a beak; ॥8॥
3.12.9: exceedingly sharp, with huge fangs, with claws like thunderbolts for weapons, black at the throat, mighty-armed, four-footed, blazing like fire; ॥9॥
3.12.10: with a dreadful, deep roar like storm clouds risen at the end of an age, his three eyes rolling like the fire of a furious kṛtyā; ॥10॥
3.12.11: with fangs and lips plainly visible, accompanied by roars of huṃ. In such a form the fierce Hara appeared. ॥11॥
3.12.12: At the very sight of him Hari lost his strength and valour, looking like a firefly beneath the brilliance of the sun. ॥12॥
3.12.13: Then, wheeling about with his wings and tearing at his navel and feet, he bound his feet with his tail and the ring of his arms with his arms. ॥13॥
3.12.14: Piercing him in the chest with his arms, Hara seized Hari. Then he went up into the sky together with the gods and great sages. ॥14॥
3.12.15: Fearlessly and suddenly he carried Viṣṇu off as a hawk carries a snake, tossing him up again and again, catching him, and dashing him down again and again. ॥15॥
3.12.16: Flying up again and again, the blessed Hara, the infinite Lord, bore that Hari, the foremost of gods, stunned by the blows of his wings, and entered the sky. ॥16॥
3.12.17: All the gods, following him, praised him with words of homage, and Brahmā and the others and the chief sages bowed with reverence and love. ॥17॥
3.12.18: Being carried off, helpless, with a downcast face and folded hands, Hari praised that Supreme Lord in graceful words. ॥18॥
3.12.19: Having praised that Mṛḍa with a hundred and eight names, Nṛsiṃha then entreated the Lord Śarabha: ॥19॥
3.12.20: Whenever this ignorant mind of mine becomes tainted by pride, then, O Supreme Lord, it must be removed by you alone. ॥20॥
3.12.21: Nandīśvara said: Thus lovingly entreating Śaṅkara, Viṣṇu the man-lion bowed and became powerless, vanquished to the end of his life. ॥21॥
3.12.22: Then in a moment Vīrabhadra took his face, severed where the rest of the body ended, making it his whole embodiment, and his limb (skin) endowed with power. ॥22॥
3.12.23: Nandīśvara said: Then Brahmā and the other gods praised the god Śaṅkara, who had assumed the Śarabha form, the sole benefactor of all the worlds. ॥23॥
3.12.24: The gods said: O Maheśvara, all the gods such as Brahmā, Viṣṇu, Indra and Candra, all the great sages, and the sons of Diti and others are born from you. ॥24॥
3.12.25: You create, protect and devour Brahmā, Viṣṇu, great Indra, the Sun and the others, the asuras and the gods; you alone are the Lord of all. ॥25॥
3.12.26: Because you take away saṃsāra, you are called Hara by the wise; because Hari was subdued by you, you are called Hara by the wise. ॥26॥
3.12.27: Since you sustain everything by dividing your body eightfold, therefore, O Lord, protect us gods with the gifts we desire. ॥27॥
3.12.28: You are the Great Person, Śambhu, Lord of all, leader of the gods, whose self owns nothing, whose self is changeless, the supreme Brahman, the refuge of the good. ॥28॥
3.12.29: You are the friend of the afflicted, an ocean of compassion, of wondrous protection, the seer of the supreme Self, the wise one, Virāṭ, all-pervading, the true, characterised by being, consciousness and bliss. ॥29॥
3.12.30: Nandīśvara said: Having heard these words of the gods, Śambhu, the Supreme Lord, spoke to those gods and to the ancient great sages. ॥30॥
3.12.31: As water poured into water, milk into milk, ghee into ghee becomes one, so Viṣṇu has then merged into Śiva as one, and not otherwise. ॥31॥
3.12.32: Viṣṇu alone, in the form of Nṛsiṃha, proud and mighty, the man-lion, had set about destroying the world. ॥32॥
3.12.33: He is to be entreated by my devotees who seek success; homage to him. He is foremost among my devotees and grants boons to my devotees. ॥33॥
3.12.34: Nandīśvara said: Having said this much, the blessed, mighty king of birds vanished right there as all the gods looked on. ॥34॥
3.12.35: The blessed Vīrabhadra too, the mighty chief of the gaṇas, stripped off Nṛsiṃha's hide, took it and went to the mountain. ॥35॥
3.12.36: From then on Śaṅkara wears the hide of Nṛsiṃha as his garment, and that face was set as the central jewel in his garland of skulls. ॥36॥
3.12.37: Then the gods, freed from fear, recounting this story, their eyes wide with wonder, all went back as they had come. ॥37॥
3.12.38: Whoever reads or hears this supreme, holy narrative, filled with the essence of the Vedas, will obtain all his desires. ॥38॥
3.12.39: It is blessed, conferring fame, long life and health, increasing prosperity, allaying all obstacles, destroying all diseases, ॥39॥
3.12.40: allaying sorrow, granting fulfilment of wishes, an abode of auspiciousness, removing untimely death, bestowing intelligence, and destroying enemies. ॥40॥
3.12.41: This supreme form of Pināka-bearer Śaṅkara in the shape of a Śarabha should be revealed only to his devotees, those who follow (walk in the path of) Śaṅkara. ॥41॥
3.12.42: It should be read and heard only by them, whose very self is devoted to Śiva; it is divine, it grants the ninefold devotion, and it bestows purity of the inner faculty and understanding. ॥42॥
3.12.43: One should recite it at all festivals of Śiva, on the fourteenth and eighth lunar days, and at the time of an image's installation, for it brings about the presence of Śiva; ॥43॥
3.12.44: and in fears arising from thieves, tigers, lions, from oneself, or from the king; and in other calamities such as portents, earthquakes, bandits and the like, and showers of dust; ॥44॥
3.12.45: in the fall of meteors, in great gales, in drought and in excessive rain — in all these the learned devotee of Śiva, self-controlled and firm in his vows, should recite it. ॥45॥
3.12.46: Whoever, free from desire, reads or even listens to this observance relating to the Lord (Īśvara), attains the world of Rudra and becomes an attendant of Rudra. ॥46॥
3.12.47: Having reached the world of Rudra, he rejoices together with Rudra; then, O sage, by Śiva's grace he attains union (sāyujya) with him. ॥47॥
3.12.iti: Thus ends the twelfth adhyāya, named The incarnation as Śarabha, in the third saṃhitā, the Śatarudra-saṃhitā, of the Śrī Śivamahāpurāṇa. ॥12॥
3.13.1: Nandīśvara said: Listen with affection, O son of Brahmā, to the story of the moon-crested Lord: how Śiva, out of love, became incarnate in the house of Viśvānara. ॥1॥
3.13.2: He was named Gṛhapati, O sage, the lord of the world of Agni, fire-formed and radiant, the Self of all, the supreme Lord. ॥2॥
3.13.3: Long ago, in the city of Narmapura on the lovely bank of the Narmadā, there lived a sage Viśvānara, a devotee of the Enemy of the Cities (Śiva), pure of soul. ॥3॥
3.13.4: He was steadfast in the stage of celibate studenthood, always devoted to the Brahma-yajña (Vedic recitation), of the Śāṇḍilya lineage, pure, a treasure-house of brahmanical splendour, and self-controlled. ॥4॥
3.13.5: He knew the meaning of all the scriptures, was ever devoted to right conduct, highly skilled in Śaiva observance, and excellent in knowledge of worldly custom. ॥5॥
3.13.6: Having weighed in his mind the auspicious qualities desirable in a wife, Viśvānara married, according to rite, a maiden of good family suited to himself. ॥6॥
3.13.7: He was devoted to tending the sacred fire, intent on the five sacrifices, constantly engaged in the six duties, and fond of gods, ancestors and guests. ॥7॥
3.13.8: When a long time had thus passed, the wife of that brāhmaṇa, named Śuciṣmatī, faithful to her vows, spoke to her husband. ॥8॥
3.13.9: Lord, through your grace, having come to you, I have enjoyed all the pleasures that are fitting for women and that bring delight. ॥9॥
3.13.10: Yet, lord, there is a wish of mine that has long dwelt in my heart, fitting for householders; you should grant it. ॥10॥
3.13.11: Viśvānara said: What indeed cannot be given to you, O fair-hipped one, you who seek my dear welfare? Ask for it, O fortunate one; I will grant it without delay. ॥11॥
3.13.12: By the grace of the Great Lord, the bringer of all welfare, nothing is hard for me to obtain, here or hereafter, O auspicious one. ॥12॥
3.13.13: Nandīśvara said: Hearing these words of her husband, she, to whom her husband was a deity, with a joyful face and folded hands, humbly spoke. ॥13॥
3.13.14: Śuciṣmatī said: If I am worthy of a boon, lord, if a boon is to be given to me, give me a son like Maheśa; I choose no other boon. ॥14॥
3.13.15: Nandīśvara said: Hearing her words, that brāhmaṇa of pure vows entered meditation for a moment and pondered this in his heart: ॥15॥
3.13.16: Ah, what an extremely rare thing that slender woman has asked of me! It lies far beyond the path of desire—yet he indeed accomplishes all. ॥16॥
3.13.17: It was uttered by that very Śambhu, dwelling in her mouth in the form of speech; who could dare to make it otherwise? This shall come to pass. ॥17॥
3.13.18: Having reflected thus, that noble-minded sage Viśvānara, steadfast in the vow of having one wife, then spoke to his wife. ॥18॥
3.13.19: Nandīśvara said: Having thus consoled his wife, the sage went for austerity to where Viśveśvara, the Lord of Kāśī, dwells in person. ॥19॥
3.13.20: Quickly reaching Vārāṇasī and beholding Maṇikarṇikā, he cast off the threefold affliction, even that accumulated over a hundred births. ॥20॥
3.13.21: Having seen all the liṅgas headed by Viśveśa, and having bathed in all the pools, step-wells, wells and lakes, ॥21॥
3.13.22: having bowed to all the Vināyakas, saluted Gaurī the consort of Śarva, and worshipped Kālarāja Bhairava, the devourer of sins, ॥22॥
3.13.23: having diligently praised the gaṇas headed by Daṇḍanāyaka, and propitiated Keśava in his forms headed by Ādikeśava, ॥23॥
3.13.24: having bowed again and again to the Suns headed by Lolārka, and tirelessly made piṇḍa offerings at all the tīrthas, ॥24॥
3.13.25: having gratified sages and brāhmaṇas with feasts for thousands and the like, and devoutly worshipped the liṅgas with the offerings of great worship, ॥25॥
3.13.26: he pondered repeatedly: Which liṅga grants success quickly, where austerity undertaken in desire of a son attains steadfastness? ॥26॥
3.13.27: Having reflected thus for a moment, the wise sage Viśvānara extolled the liṅga Vīreśa as the swift bestower of a son: ॥27॥
3.13.28: Countless thousands of siddhas have attained perfection from it; therefore the supreme Vīreśvara is renowned as the Siddhaliṅga. ॥28॥
3.13.29: By worshipping the great liṅga Vīreśvara with devotion for a year, people obtain long life, every wish, sons and the like, in many ways. ॥29॥
3.13.30: I too, worshipping Vīreśa here at the three times of day, shall quickly obtain a son such as my wife desires. ॥30॥
3.13.31: Nandīśvara said: Having thus made up his mind, the steadfast and accomplished brāhmaṇa Viśvānara bathed in the water of Candrakūpa and, keeping vows, undertook a discipline. ॥31॥
3.13.32: For a month he ate once a day; for a month he ate only at night; for a month he ate only what came unasked; and for a month again he gave up food altogether. ॥32॥
3.13.33: For a month he lived on milk; for a month on vegetables and fruits; for a month on a fistful of sesame; for a month on water alone. ॥33॥
3.13.34: For a month he took the five products of the cow; for a month he kept the Cāndrāyaṇa vow; for a month he drank only water from the tips of kuśa grass; for a month he lived on air. ॥34॥
3.13.35: Thus for a period of a year he performed wondrous austerity, and three times a day he devoutly worshipped the excellent liṅga Vīreśa. ॥35॥
3.13.36: Then in the thirteenth month, having bathed in the waters of the Gaṅgā (the river of three paths), just as that brāhmaṇa was coming to Vīreśa at dawn, ॥36॥
3.13.37: at that very moment the ascetic beheld in the middle of the liṅga a child adorned with sacred ash, a boy with the appearance of eight years, ॥37॥
3.13.38: with eyes stretching to his ears, deep-red lips, a lovely crown of tawny matted hair, naked, with a smiling face, ॥38॥
3.13.39: wearing attire befitting childhood, bearing the ash of the pyre, reciting Vedic hymns, and laughing in his own play. ॥39॥
3.13.40: Seeing him, the sage was filled with joy, his hair bristling like a garment, and from his heart he cried out again and again, salutation be to you. ॥40॥
3.13.41: With eight verses that grant one's desires, the accomplished Viśvānara praised Śambhu, the supreme bliss, who had taken the form of a child. ॥41॥
3.13.42: Viśvānara said: Brahman alone is one, without a second, and it is everything — this is truth, truth; here there is no diversity whatsoever. Rudra alone is one; no second stood beside him. Therefore I take refuge in you, the one Great Lord. ॥42॥
3.13.43: O Śambhu, you indeed are the creator and destroyer of all; among many forms you are of a single form, and yet formless. Just as the inner Self is one and yet many, so are you; therefore I take refuge in no lord other than you. ॥43॥
3.13.44: Like a snake seen in a rope, silver in mother-of-pearl, and a flood of water in the sun's rays called a mirage — whatever thus appears as real, so is this whole world all around seen through when he is known; in that Great Lord I take refuge. ॥44॥
3.13.45: Coolness in water, the power of burning in fire, heat in the sun, serene light in the moon, fragrance in the flower, and ghee even within milk — whatever that is, O Śambhu, that is you; therefore I take refuge in you. ॥45॥
3.13.46: Without ears you grasp sound; without a nose you smell; without feet you come from afar; without eyes you see; without a tongue you know taste. Who can rightly know you? Therefore I take refuge in you. ॥46॥
3.13.47: O Lord, not even the Veda knows you directly, nor Viṣṇu, nor the Ordainer of all Brahmā, nor the lords of yogis, nor the gods led by Indra; only the devotee knows you. Therefore I take refuge in you. ॥47॥
3.13.48: O Lord, you have no lineage, no birth, no name, no form, no character, and no place; yet, being such, you are the Lord of the three worlds and fulfil all desires. I worship you. ॥48॥
3.13.49: From you comes everything; you indeed are everything, O foe of Smara. You are the lord of Gaurī, and you are the naked one, supremely tranquil. You are the old man, you the youth, and you the child. What reality is there that is not you? Hence, turning from all else, I bow to you. ॥49॥
3.13.50: Nandīśvara said: Having praised thus, the Brahmin fell to the ground; while he remained there with joined palms, that child — the eldest of all elders — greatly delighted, spoke to the Brahmin. ॥50॥
3.13.51: The boy said: O Viśvānara, best of sages, O Brahmin, today I have been pleased by you and am thoroughly gracious at heart; choose a supreme boon. ॥51॥
3.13.52: Then, rising up, the accomplished sage Viśvānara, best of sages, joyful at heart, replied to Śaṅkara who had the form of a child. ॥52॥
3.13.53: Viśvānara said: O Maheśvara, O Lord, what is unknown to you, the all-knowing? You are the inner Self of all, the blessed Śarva, the giver of everything. ॥53॥
3.13.54: Why do you urge me toward begging, which brings humiliation? Knowing this, O Maheśāna, do as you yourself wish. ॥54॥
3.13.55: Nandīśvara said: Having heard these words of Viśvānara of pure vows, the pure god in the form of a child then smiled a pure smile and spoke. ॥55॥
3.13.56: O pure one, the desire you have cherished in your heart concerning Śuciṣmatī will without doubt be fulfilled in a very short time. ॥56॥
3.13.57: O great-minded one, I shall become your son through Śuciṣmatī, renowned by the name Gṛhapati, pure and dear to all the immortals. ॥57॥
3.13.58: This holy hymn, the Abhilāṣāṣṭaka, uttered by you, grants desires when recited three times a day for a year in the presence of Śiva. ॥58॥
3.13.59: Reciting this hymn grants sons, grandsons and wealth; it also brings complete peace and destroys all calamities. ॥59॥
3.13.60: It brings about heaven, liberation and prosperity — there is no doubt of this. Indeed it equals all hymns and always grants every desire. ॥60॥
3.13.61: Rising at dawn, well bathed, having worshipped Śambhu's liṅga, one without a son who recites this hymn for a year will obtain a son. ॥61॥
3.13.62: This Abhilāṣāṣṭaka should not be given to just anyone; it must be carefully guarded, for it brings childbirth even to a woman who is utterly barren. ॥62॥
3.13.63: Whether by a woman or by a man, this hymn recited with discipline for a year near a liṅga grants a son; there is no doubt of this. ॥63॥
3.13.64: Nandīśvara said: Having said this, Śambhu in the form of a child, the refuge of the good, vanished; and the Brahmin Viśvānara, joyful at heart, went to his own home. ॥64॥
3.13.iti: Thus ends the thirteenth adhyāya, named The incarnation as Gṛhapati, in the third saṃhitā, the Śatarudra-saṃhitā, of the Śrī Śivamahāpurāṇa. ॥13॥
3.14.1: Nandīśvara said: That Brahmin came home, filled with great joy, and told his beloved wife the whole account of what had happened. ॥1॥
3.14.2: Hearing that, the Brahmin's wife Śuciṣmatī was delighted; full of deep love, she praised her own destiny. ॥2॥
3.14.3: Then, in due time, after he had duly performed the rite called garbhādhāna (conception), that woman became pregnant. ॥3॥
3.14.4: Then, before the foetus began to stir, that learned man duly performed the puṃsavana rite according to the procedure taught in the Gṛhya sūtras, for the increase of male qualities. ॥4॥
3.14.5: Then in the eighth month that knower of rites performed the sīmanta (hair-parting) rite, which enriches the form of the embryo, and for the accomplishment of an easy delivery. ॥5॥
3.14.6: Then, under auspicious stars, with Jupiter in a kendra (angular house), in an auspicious ascendant, with benefic planets in favourable conjunctions, a son whose face was lovely like the lord of stars (the moon) — ॥6॥
3.14.7: — outshining the lamps of the lying-in chamber and destroying all misfortunes, a son was born to her, Śuciṣmatī. ॥7॥
3.14.8: He was Śarva himself, giver of every happiness to the dwellers of Bhūḥ, Bhuvaḥ and Svaḥ. And the clouds, borne by the winds, became perfumes for the faces of the maidens of the quarters; ॥8॥
3.14.9: those dense clouds rained showers of flowers with delightful fragrance. The drums of the gods resounded, and all the directions became serene. ॥9॥
3.14.10: Everywhere the rivers became clear, together with the minds of beings; darkness (tamas) utterly faded, and even rajas (dust/passion) became free of rajas. ॥10॥
3.14.11: Creatures were filled with sattva (goodness); a rain of nectar fell; and the speech of every living being became wholly auspicious and pleasing. ॥11॥
3.14.12: Apsarases led by Rambhā, with auspicious articles in their hands, Vidyādharīs, Kinnarīs and celestial women by the thousands, ॥12॥
3.14.13: and the honoured women of the Gandharvas, serpents and Yakṣas, sweet-voiced, singing auspicious songs, came there in great numbers. ॥13॥
3.14.14: Marīci, Atri, Pulaha, Pulastya, Kratu, Aṅgiras, Vasiṣṭha, Kaśyapa, Agastya, Vibhāṇḍa, the son of Māṇḍavī, ॥14॥
3.14.15: Lomaśa, Romacaraṇa, Bharadvāja, then Gautama, Bhṛgu, Gālava, Garga, Jātūkarṇya, Parāśara, ॥15॥
3.14.16: Āpastamba, Yājñavalkya, Dakṣa, Vālmīki and Mudgala, Śātātapa, Likhita, Śilāda, Śaṅkha, Uñchabhuk, ॥16॥
3.14.17: Jamadagni, Saṃvarta, Mataṅga, Bharata, Aṃśumān, Vyāsa, Kātyāyana, Kutsa, Śaunaka, Suśruta, Śuka, ॥17॥
3.14.18: Ṛṣyaśṛṅga, then Durvāsas, Śuci, Nārada and Tumburu, Uttaṅka, Vāmadeva, Pavana, Asita and Devala, ॥18॥
3.14.19: Sālaṅkāyana and Hārīta, Viśvāmitra, then Bhārgava, Mṛkaṇḍa together with his son, Parvata and also Dāruka, ॥19॥
3.14.20: Dhaumya, Upamanyu, Vatsa and other sages, along with the sages' daughters, came together to the blessed hermitage of Viśvānara to perform rites for his well-being. ॥20॥
3.14.21: Brahmā accompanied by Bṛhaspati, the god whose mount is Garuḍa (Viṣṇu), and the bull-bannered Śiva together with Gaurī, attended by Nandin and Bhṛṅgin, ॥21॥
3.14.22: the gods headed by the great Indra, the Nāgas dwelling in Pātāla, and the great oceans with their rivers, bringing jewels in abundance, ॥22॥
3.14.23: and the immobile beings, assuming moving forms, came in thousands. At that great festival there was a moonlit radiance out of season. ॥23॥
3.14.24: Brahmā (Vidhi) himself, reverently, performed his birth rite (jātakarma). Having considered the Veda and his form, he declared: This one by name is Gṛhapati. ॥24॥
3.14.25: Thus he gave him the name, which is to be given on the eleventh day, following the procedure of the naming rite and reciting the Vedic text for that purpose. ॥25॥
3.14.26: And having greeted him with blessings spoken in the mantras of the four Vedas, the Grandsire of all, at the proper time, mounted his swan and departed. ॥26॥
3.14.27: Hara too, having performed the protective rite suited to a child, following worldly custom, mounted his vehicle and went with Hari to his own abode. ॥27॥
3.14.28: Oh, what beauty! Oh, what radiance! Oh, the marks on all his limbs! Oh, the good fortune of Śuciṣmatī — Hara himself has appeared as her son! ॥28॥
3.14.29: Or rather, what is so wonderful in this, among the devotees of Śarva? Rudra himself has appeared, because Rudra was worshipped by him. ॥29॥
3.14.30: Praising thus to one another, their hair bristling with joy, they all took leave of Viśvānara and went back as they had come. ॥30॥
3.14.31: Therefore those living in the householder stage long for a son: Through a son one conquers the worlds — this is the eternal Vedic teaching. ॥31॥
3.14.32: The house of a sonless man is empty; the earning of a sonless man is in vain; the austerity of a sonless man is cut off; one does not become purified while sonless. ॥32॥
3.14.33: There is no gain higher than a son, no happiness higher than a son, no friend higher than a son, anywhere, in the next world or here. ॥33॥
3.14.34: Then in his fourth month his father performed the niṣkramaṇa (first going out) from the house; the first feeding with grain at half a year, and the tonsure (cūḍā) at one year, were duly performed. ॥34॥
3.14.35: Then, having performed the ear-piercing under the asterism Śravaṇa, that knower of rites gave him the vow of initiation in the fifth year, for the increase of Brahmic splendour. ॥35॥
3.14.36: Then, after performing the upākarma, the wise one taught him the Vedas; within three years he duly studied the Vedas together with their limbs and their pada and krama recitations. ॥36॥
3.14.37: Capable as he was, displaying humility and other virtues, he acquired the entire body of knowledge from his teacher's mouth, the teacher being a mere witness. ॥37॥
3.14.38: Then, in his ninth year, Nārada came to see Gṛhapati, son of Viśvānara, who was devoted to serving his parents. ॥38॥
3.14.39: Reaching Viśvānara's hut, the curious divine sage, having duly received the guest-water and a seat, asked him there about his welfare. ॥39॥
3.14.40: Then, remembering the lotus-feet of Śiva, he told Viśvānara to his face all about his good fortune and about the destiny of the son. ॥40॥
3.14.41: Nandīśvara said: Addressed thus by the sage, that glorious boy, having obtained his parents' permission, bowed to Nārada with devotion and, humbly bending, sat down near him. ॥41॥
3.14.42: Nārada said: O Vaiśvānara, come here; sit on my lap, dear child. I shall examine your marks; show me your right hand. ॥42॥
3.14.43: Then the wise Nārada, having examined everything—the palate, tongue and the rest—spoke to Viśvānara, prompted by Śiva. ॥43॥
3.14.44: Nārada said: O sage Viśvānara, I tell you; listen attentively about your son's marks. This son bears auspicious marks on all his limbs; he is endowed with great characteristics. ॥44॥
3.14.45: But he who is endowed with all virtues, marked with all auspicious signs, with all his digits full and spotless — may Fate protect him, as it protects the moon. ॥45॥
3.14.46: Therefore this child must be protected with every effort; even a virtue turns into a fault when the Creator becomes adverse. ॥46॥
3.14.47: I fear that in his twelfth year there will be a danger from lightning and fire. Having said this, Nārada went back to the world of the gods as he had come. ॥47॥
3.14.iti: Thus ends the fourteenth adhyāya, named The incarnation as Gṛhapati, in the account of the Gṛhapati incarnation, in the third saṃhitā, the Śatarudra-saṃhitā, of the Śrī Śivamahāpurāṇa. ॥14॥
3.15.1: Nandīśvara said: Viśvānara and his wife, having heard what Nārada had said, took it to be a most dreadful stroke of a thunderbolt. ॥1॥
3.15.2: Crying out, alas, I am ruined, he beat his chest, and overwhelmed with grief for his son he fell into a deep swoon. ॥2॥
3.15.3: Śuciṣmatī too, stricken with sorrow, wept unbearably, with loud wails of alas, her senses utterly distraught. ॥3॥
3.15.4: Hearing this cry of anguish, Viśvānara too shook off his swoon and rose, crying aloud: What? What is it? What, what is this? Where is my Gṛhapati, my life-breath walking outside me, dwelling in my inner self, the lord of all my senses? ॥4॥
3.15.5: Then the boy Gṛhapati, born of a portion of Śaṅkara, seeing his parents overcome with great grief, smiled and spoke. ॥5॥
3.15.6: Gṛhapati said: O mother, O father, what has happened? Tell me the cause now. Why this excessive weeping? Whence such fear has come to you two? ॥6॥
3.15.7: Time itself cannot seize me, whose body is armoured by the dust of your feet — what then of the wretched, fickle, puny lightning? ॥7॥
3.15.8: Hear my vow, dear parents: if I am truly your son, I shall act in such a way that Death itself will be terrified. ॥8॥
3.15.9: Having worshipped Mṛtyuñjaya, the all-knowing giver of all to the good, I shall practise japa to Mahākāla — I tell you the truth, dear parents. ॥9॥
3.15.10: Nandīśvara said: Hearing his words, the afflicted brahmin couple, their anguish dispelled as if by floods of unseasonable showers of nectar, then said: ॥10॥
3.15.11: The brahmin couple said: Say it again, say it again. How was it, how? Tell us again: Time is not able to seize me — what is this wretched lightning? ॥11॥
3.15.12: You have spoken of a great means to end our anguish, namely the worship of the god called Mṛtyuñjaya. ॥12॥
3.15.13: And likewise taking refuge in Śambhu — there is nothing higher than that — who accomplishes what lies beyond the path of wishes, and who removes sins. ॥13॥
3.15.14: Have you not heard, dear son, how of old the destroyer of Tripura protected Śvetaketu when he was bound by the noose of Death? ॥14॥
3.15.15: Śiva made Śilāda's son Nandin, a mere eight years old and seized by death, his own attendant, a delight to the whole world. ॥15॥
3.15.16: Drinking the dreadful Hālāhala poison, born from the churning of the milk-ocean and like the fire of cosmic dissolution, he saved the three worlds. ॥16॥
3.15.17: He who slew the arrogant Jalandhara, who had seized the wealth of the three worlds, with the discus that arose from a line drawn by his beautiful toe. ॥17॥
3.15.18: He who of old, with the flames sprung from the fall of a single arrow, withered Tripura, deluded by its lordship over the three worlds, as the sun withers things. ॥18॥
3.15.19: With a mere glance he sent Kāma, mighty from conquering the three worlds, to the state of the bodiless, while Brahmā and the others looked on. ॥19॥
3.15.20: Go, son, for refuge to that Śiva, the sole creator of Brahmā and the rest, whose vehicle is the cloud, the imperishable, the protecting jewel of the universe. ॥20॥
3.15.21: Nandīśvara said: Having thus obtained his parents' permission, he bowed at their feet, circumambulated them, comforted them much, and set out. ॥21॥
3.15.22: He reached Kāśī, hard to attain even for Brahmā, Nārāyaṇa and others, which destroys the torment of the great cosmic dissolution and is protected by Viśveśa, ॥22॥
3.15.23: adorned at its neck-regions by the heavenly river Gaṅgā as by a necklace-string, and made resplendent by Hara's consort endowed with wondrous qualities. ॥23॥
3.15.24: Having arrived there, that best of brahmins first went to Maṇikarṇikā; bathing there according to rule, and seeing Lord Viśveśvara, ॥24॥
3.15.25: the wise boy, filled with great bliss, with joined palms and bowed head, prostrated before him who saves the life of the three worlds. ॥25॥
3.15.26: Gazing again and again at that liṅga, he rejoiced repeatedly in his heart: This is clearly rich with the very root of supreme bliss, there is no doubt. ॥26॥
3.15.27: Ah, there is none more blessed than I in the three worlds with their moving and unmoving beings, since today I have seen the glorious all-pervading Viśveśvara. ॥27॥
3.15.28: It was only for the dawning of my good fortune that the great sage Nārada came earlier and spoke as he did; therefore I have fulfilled my purpose. ॥28॥
3.15.29: Nandīśvara said: Having thus broken his fast with the nectar-juices of bliss, he then, on an auspicious day, installed a liṅga bestowing welfare on all, ॥29॥
3.15.30: and undertook severe observances, hard to perform for those of undisciplined mind. With a hundred and eight auspicious pots filled with Gaṅgā water, ॥30॥
3.15.31: purified by straining through cloth, he, pure in soul, bathed Śiva every day, and daily offered him a garland made of blue lotuses, ॥31॥
3.15.32: fashioned of one thousand and eight flowers. Once a fortnight, or once a month, he ate bulbs, roots and fruits. ॥32॥
3.15.33: For six months the steadfast one lived on withered leaves; for six months he subsisted on air; for six months he lived on drops of water. ॥33॥
3.15.34: Thus, O brahmins, O Nārada, two years passed for that great soul as he performed austerities with his mind fixed solely on Śiva. ॥34॥
3.15.35: In the twelfth year from his birth, as if to make true the words spoken by Nārada, the wielder of the thunderbolt (Indra) approached him, ॥35॥
3.15.36: and said: Ask a boon; I will give whatever is in your mind. I am Śatakratu, O brahmin; I am pleased with your auspicious vows. ॥36॥
3.15.37: Nandīśvara said: Hearing these words of the great Indra, the steadfast young son of the sage spoke sweetly, uttering sweet syllables: ॥37॥
3.15.38: Gṛhapati said: O Maghavan, enemy of Vṛtra, I know you as the bearer of the thunderbolt. I do not choose a boon from you; Śaṅkara is my giver of boons. ॥38॥
3.15.39: Indra said: Śaṅkara is not other than I; I am the god of gods, child. Give up your childishness and ask for a boon without delay. ॥39॥
3.15.40: Gṛhapati said: Go away, lover of Ahalyā, you wicked one, foe of the mountains, chastiser of Pāka. Plainly, I seek no god other than Paśupati. ॥40॥
3.15.41: Nandīśvara said: Having heard his words thus, Indra, his eyes reddened with anger, raised his terrible thunderbolt and frightened the boy. ॥41॥
3.15.42: Seeing the thunderbolt, covered with flashes of lightning, and remembering Nārada's words, the boy, overwhelmed with fear, fainted. ॥42॥
3.15.43: Then Śambhu, the lord of Gaurī, dispeller of darkness, appeared, saying, rise, rise, may good befall you, as though reviving him with his touches. ॥43॥
3.15.44: Opening his lotus-eyes, which had been as if closed like lotuses at the close of day, and rising, he saw before him Śambhu, more brilliant than a hundred suns. ॥44॥
3.15.45: Beholding the eye on his forehead, he saw him dark-throated, bearing the bull on his banner, with the Mountain's daughter seated on his left side, and the moon on his crest, ॥45॥
3.15.46: shining with matted locks, bearing the trident and the Ajagava bow as weapons, his body gleaming white like camphor, wrapped in an elephant's hide, ॥46॥
3.15.47: recognising Mahādeva from his guru's words and from scripture, his throat choked with tears of joy, his body clad as in a garment of bristling hair, ॥47॥
3.15.48: for a moment he stood still like a mountain, like a painted or artificial doll, utterly so, forgetting even himself. ॥48॥
3.15.49: When he was unable either to praise, or to bow, or to say anything at all, then Śaṅkara smiled and spoke. ॥49॥
3.15.50: Īśvara said: O child, O Gṛhapati. Ah, I know you are frightened of Śakra with the thunderbolt raised in his hand. Do not fear; I made a test of you. ॥50॥
3.15.51: Neither Śakra, nor the thunderbolt, nor even Death has power over my devotee. It was I myself, in the form of Indra, who frightened you. ॥51॥
3.15.52: I grant you a boon, good one: become the holder of Agni's position. You will be the giver of boons to all the gods. ॥52॥
3.15.53: O Agni, be the one who moves within all beings. As lord of a quarter, between Dharmarāja (Yama) and Indra, obtain your realm. ॥53॥
3.15.54: This liṅga established by you shall bear your name; known as Agnīśvara, it will increase all radiance. ॥54॥
3.15.55: For the devotees of Agnīśvara there is no fear from lightning or fire, no fear of weakness of digestion, and never untimely death. ॥55॥
3.15.56: Having worshipped in Kāśī Agnīśvara, the giver of all prosperity, one who by fate dies even elsewhere is honoured in the world of Fire. ॥56॥
3.15.57: Nandīśvara said: Having said this, and having brought his kinsmen, Śiva, while his parents looked on, consecrated Agni to the lordship of a quarter and entered into that liṅga. ॥57॥
3.15.58: Thus, dear one, I have described to you the incarnation as Agni, named Gṛhapati, of Śaṅkara, the supreme Self, the remover of people's afflictions. ॥58॥
3.15.59: The city of Agni (Citrahotra), Arciṣmatī, is delightful, bestowing happiness and excellent; those who are devoted to Jātavedas indeed dwell there. ॥59॥
3.15.60: Those of firm resolve and controlled senses who enter fire, or women endowed with courage — all of them become radiant as fire. ॥60॥
3.15.61: Brahmins devoted to the agnihotra, celibate students who have established the sacred fire, and likewise those who practise the five-fire austerity, dwell in the world of Agni, radiant as fire. ॥61॥
3.15.62: He who in the cold gives loads of firewood to dispel the cold, or who makes a fire-place for warmth, shall dwell near Agni. ॥62॥
3.15.63: He who, full of faith, performs the cremation rite for one without protector, or, if unable, urges another to do it, is honoured in the world of Agni. ॥63॥
3.15.64: Fire alone is the supreme bestower of the highest good for the twice-born. Guru, deity, vow, sacred ford — all is determined to be Fire. ॥64॥
3.15.65: All impure things become pure in an instant through contact with fire; therefore it is known as Pāvaka (the Purifier). ॥65॥
3.15.66: This Fire (Āśuśukṣaṇi) is indeed directly the inner Self, certainly; it digests morsels of flesh in the belly, but not the lump of flesh (embryo) in women's wombs. ॥66॥
3.15.67: This fiery form of Śambhu, visible and of the nature of burning, is creator, destroyer and protector; without it, what can be seen? ॥67॥
3.15.68: This Citrabhānu is directly the eye of the Lord of the three worlds. In a world blind and full of darkness, who but he is the illuminator? ॥68॥
3.15.69: Incense, lamps, food offerings, milk, curd, ghee and sugarcane products — this, when consumed by Fire, all the dwellers of heaven enjoy in heaven. ॥69॥
3.15.iti: Thus ends the fifteenth adhyāya, named The incarnation as Gṛhapati, in the third saṃhitā, the Śatarudra-saṃhitā, of the Śrī Śivamahāpurāṇa. ॥15॥
3.16.1: Nandīśvara said: O lord of sages, hear also of Śambhu's incarnation as Yakṣeśvara, which destroys the pride of the proud and increases the devotion of the good. ॥1॥
3.16.2: Long ago the mighty gods and Daityas churned the Ocean of Milk for the sake of nectar, joined together in an alliance for their own good purpose. ॥2॥
3.16.3: While the Ocean of Milk was first being churned for nectar by the gods and Dānavas, there arose from it a poison blazing like the fire of universal destruction. ॥3॥
3.16.4: Seeing it, all the gods and Daityas, overwhelmed with fear, fled swiftly, dear one, and went to Śambhu for refuge. ॥4॥
3.16.5: Seeing Śaṅkara, the crest-jewel of all gods, they all, together with Acyuta, bowed with heads lowered and praised him with devotion. ॥5॥
3.16.6: Then the blessed Śaṅkara, loving to his devotees, being pleased, drank the most terrible poison that tormented the hosts of gods and demons. ॥6॥
3.16.7: That terrible, virulent poison, once drunk, he held in his throat; the all-pervading Lord shone exceedingly by it and became Nīlakaṇṭha (the Blue-throated). ॥7॥
3.16.8: Then the hosts of gods and demons, all freed from the burning of the poison by Śiva's grace, churned it again. ॥8॥
3.16.9: Then, O sage, many jewels came forth from it, and also the nectar, the very object sought by gods and Dānavas, O sage. ॥9॥
3.16.10: By Hari's grace only the gods drank it, not the asuras. Then a very great conflict arose among them mutually. ॥10॥
3.16.11: Then, O sage, a hand-to-hand battle took place between the gods and Dānavas. There the Moon, afflicted by fear of Rāhu, fled. ॥11॥
3.16.12: Overwhelmed with fear, he went to Śambhu's abode for refuge, and bowing deeply, praised him, saying, protect me, protect me. ॥12॥
3.16.13: Then Śaṅkara, giver of fearlessness to the good and loving to his devotees, the Lord, bore upon his head the Moon who had come for refuge. ॥13॥
3.16.14: Then Rāhu arrived and, bowing deeply, reverently praised Śaṅkara, lord of all, with pleasing words. ॥14॥
3.16.15: Śambhu, understanding his wish, placed on his neck Rāhu's heads, called Ketu, which had earlier been severed by Acyuta. ॥15॥
3.16.16: Then in the battle all the asuras were defeated by the gods; all the gods, having drunk the nectar, became mighty and gained victory. ॥16॥
3.16.17: All of them, led by Viṣṇu, became exceedingly proud, deluded by Śiva's māyā, inwardly vaunting their own strength. ॥17॥
3.16.18: Then the god Śaṅkara, lord of all and destroyer of pride, becoming a Yakṣa, quickly went to where the gods were, O sage. ॥18॥
3.16.19: Seeing all the gods headed by Acyuta, with minds full of great pride, Maheśa, the lord of Yakṣas and destroyer of pride, spoke. ॥19॥
3.16.20: The lord of the yakṣas said: Why are you all, O gods, gathered here together? What is the whole matter? Tell me the reason, since I am asking. ॥20॥
3.16.21: The gods said: O great god, a great and most dreadful battle took place here. The asuras were destroyed, all of them; the survivors have fled away. ॥21॥
3.16.22: We are all great heroes, slayers of Daityas, exceedingly strong. What are those Daityas before us—always of petty strength? ॥22॥
3.16.23: Nandīśvara said: Hearing these words of the gods, full of pride, Mahādeva, destroyer of pride, in the form of a Yakṣa, spoke. ॥23॥
3.16.24: The lord of the yakṣas said: O all you gods, listen attentively to my words. I speak the truth, not falsehood—words that remove all pride. ॥24॥
3.16.25: Do not indulge in this pride; the creator and destroyer is another, the Lord. Having forgotten Maheśāna, you boast in vain of your strength. ॥25॥
3.16.26: If you have such pride, believing your own strength to be great, then cut this blade of grass set down by me with those weapons of yours, O gods. ॥26॥
3.16.27: Nandīśvara said: Having said this, he cast a single blade of grass before them. Then the Lord in Yakṣa form, refuge of the good, took away all their pride. ॥27॥
3.16.28: Then all the gods headed by Viṣṇu, thinking themselves heroes, exerted their prowess there and hurled their weapons. ॥28॥
3.16.29: Those weapons of the heaven-dwellers at once became futile there, through the power of Śiva, remover of their foolish pride. ॥29॥
3.16.30: Then there came a voice from the sky that dispelled the gods' astonishment: This Yakṣa, O gods, is Śaṅkara, remover of all pride. ॥30॥
3.16.31: He alone, the Supreme Lord, is creator, destroyer and sustainer. By his strength all beings are strong, not otherwise. ॥31॥
3.16.32: Deluded by the power of his māyā and through pride, even now they did not recognise their own Lord Śiva, the Lord whose body is consciousness. ॥32॥
3.16.33: Nandīśvara said: Hearing the heavenly voice, they understood, their pride gone; they bowed to Yakṣeśvara and praised that Lord. ॥33॥
3.16.34: The gods said: O God of gods, Mahādeva, remover of all pride, O Yakṣeśvara of great sport, your māyā is most wondrous, O Lord. ॥34॥
3.16.35: Deluded even now by the māyā of you who have taken the Yakṣa form, we spoke proudly before you, thinking ourselves separate from you. ॥35॥
3.16.36: Now, O Lord, knowledge has come by your grace alone: you alone are creator, destroyer and sustainer, none other, O Śaṅkara. ॥36॥
3.16.37: You alone are the initiator and withdrawer of all powers of all beings, the Lord of all, the Supreme Self, imperishable and non-dual. ॥37॥
3.16.38: In the form of Yakṣeśvara you have taken away the pride of all of us; we consider that a grace bestowed by you, the compassionate one. ॥38॥
3.16.39: Then that lord of Yakṣas, having favoured all the gods and enlightened them with various words, vanished right there. ॥39॥
3.16.40: Thus has been described Śambhu's incarnation named Yakṣeśvara, which brings happiness—giving joy to the good and, when pleased, granting fearlessness. ॥40॥
3.16.41: This stainless narrative removes all pride; it always grants deep peace to the virtuous and bestows worldly enjoyment and liberation upon men. ॥41॥
3.16.42: The wise man who listens to this with devotion, or causes it to be recited to others, obtains all his desires and thereafter attains the supreme goal. ॥42॥
3.16.iti: Thus ends the sixteenth adhyāya, named The incarnation as Yakṣeśvara, in the third saṃhitā, the Śatarudra-saṃhitā, of the Śrī Śivamahāpurāṇa. ॥16॥
3.17.1: Now hear of the first ten incarnations of Giriśa, headed by Mahākāla, which are served with devotion through the section of scripture concerned with worship (upāsanā-kāṇḍa). ॥1॥
3.17.2: Among them the first is Mahākāla, granter of enjoyment and liberation to the good. His Śakti there is Mahākālī, who grants the fruits desired by devotees. ॥2॥
3.17.3: The second is named Tāra, and likewise his Śakti is Tārā. Both grant enjoyment and liberation and give happiness to their own servants. ॥3॥
3.17.4: The third is proclaimed to be Bhuvaneśa, called Bāla; there Śivā is Bhuvaneśī, called Bālā, giver of happiness to the good. ॥4॥
3.17.5: The fourth is Śrīvidyeśa, called Ṣoḍaśa, and Śivā is Śrīvidyā Ṣoḍaśī; he gives happiness to devotees and grants the fruits of enjoyment and liberation. ॥5॥
3.17.6: The fifth is known as Bhairava, ever fulfilling the desires of devotees; there Girijā is Bhairavī, fulfilling the desires of true worshippers. ॥6॥
3.17.7: Śiva named Chinnamastaka is proclaimed the sixth; and Girijā is Chinnamastakā, granting the desires of devotees. ॥7॥
3.17.8: The seventh is Śambhu as Dhūmavān, granting the fruits of all desires; there Śivā is Dhūmavatī, fulfilling the desires of true worshippers. ॥8॥
3.17.9: The eighth incarnation of Śiva, giver of happiness, is Bagalāmukha; his Śakti there is Mahānandā, renowned as Bagalāmukhī. ॥9॥
3.17.10: The ninth incarnation of Śiva is proclaimed to be Mātaṅga; there Śarvāṇī is Mātaṅgī, granting the fruits of all desires. ॥10॥
3.17.11: The tenth is Śambhu as Kamala, granting the fruits of enjoyment and liberation; there Girijā is Kamalā, protector of her own devotees. ॥11॥
3.17.12: These ten incarnations of Śiva are givers of happiness, and always grant enjoyment and liberation to good devotees. ॥12॥
3.17.13: These are indeed the ten incarnations of the great-souled Śaṅkara, constantly giving various kinds of happiness to those who serve them without deviation. ॥13॥
3.17.14: O sage, this greatness of the ten incarnations has been described; it should be known as granting all desires and as contained in the Tantra scriptures and others. ॥14॥
3.17.15: O sage, wondrous is the glory of these primal Śaktis; it should be known as granting all desires and as contained in the Tantra scriptures and others. ॥15॥
3.17.16: In rites such as slaying enemies, each respective Śakti is held supreme; she always punishes the wicked and increases the brahminical splendour. ॥16॥
3.17.17: Thus, O brahmin, I have told you of the ten auspicious incarnations of Maheśa together with their Śaktis, headed by Mahākāla. ॥17॥
3.17.18: Whoever, intent on devotion, recites this pure narrative on all Śaiva festival days becomes exceedingly dear to Śambhu. ॥18॥
3.17.19: A brahmin would become endowed with brahminical lustre, a kṣatriya victorious, a vaiśya a lord of wealth, and a śūdra would attain happiness. ॥19॥
3.17.20: Followers of Śaṅkara who abide in their own dharma and listen to this account would be especially happy, and may they become devotees of Śiva. ॥20॥
3.17.iti: Thus ends the seventeenth adhyāya, named The ten incarnations of Śiva, in the third saṃhitā, the Śatarudra-saṃhitā, of the Śrī Śivamahāpurāṇa. ॥17॥
3.18.1: Nandīśvara said: Now listen to the eleven excellent incarnations of Śaṅkara, on hearing which one is not afflicted by the affliction that arises from untruth and the like. ॥1॥
3.18.2: Long ago all the gods, headed by Śakra, defeated by the Daityas, abandoned their own city Amarāvatī and fled in fear. ॥2॥
3.18.3: Oppressed by the Daityas, the gods went to Kaśyapa; joining their palms, with shoulders bowed, they prostrated before him in great distress. ॥3॥
3.18.4: Having praised him well and respectfully made their petition, all the gods reported everything to him: their own misery and their defeat. ॥4॥
3.18.5: Then, dear one, Kaśyapa, their father, whose mind was devoted to Śiva, hearing of the gods' misery, became sorrowful, though not excessively. ॥5॥
3.18.6: Then that sage, calm of mind, having comforted them and summoning his fortitude, went with great delight to Kāśī, the city of Viśveśvara, O sage. ॥6॥
3.18.7: Then, having bathed in the water of the Gaṅgā and performed the rite with reverence, he worshipped Viśveśvara, the Lord of all, the master, together with Ambā. ॥7॥
3.18.8: Having duly installed a Śiva-liṅga, he performed extensive austerity with great love, directed toward Śambhu, desiring the welfare of the gods. ॥8॥
3.18.9: A long time passed, O sage, while he practised austerity, steadfast, his mind attached to the lotus feet of Śiva. ॥9॥
3.18.10: Then Śambhu, friend of the afflicted and refuge of the virtuous, appeared to grant a boon to that seer whose mind was attached to his feet. ॥10॥
3.18.11: And Maheśvara, very pleased, affectionate to his devotees, said to Kaśyapa, the tiger among sages and his own devotee: Ask for a boon. ॥11॥
3.18.12: Having seen that Great Lord, Kaśyapa, the father of the gods, delighted and serene of mind, bowed with joined palms and praised him. ॥12॥
3.18.13: Kaśyapa said: O God of gods, Great Lord, affectionate to those who seek refuge, you are the Lord of all, the Supreme Self, reachable through meditation, non-dual and imperishable. ॥13॥
3.18.14: You, O Maheśvara, are the subduer of the mighty, the refuge of the virtuous, the friend of the afflicted, an ocean of compassion, whose mind is skilled in protecting devotees. ॥14॥
3.18.15: These gods are indeed yours, and especially your devotees. Today they have been defeated by the Daityas; protect them in their sorrow, O Lord. ॥15॥
3.18.16: Even the Lord of Ramā Viṣṇu is powerless; they the Daityas cause distress again and again. Therefore the gods have taken refuge in me, reporting that misery. ॥16॥
3.18.17: For that purpose, O Lord of the gods of gods, destroyer of the gods' sorrow, to fulfil that wish, I have undertaken steadfast austerity to win your favour. ॥17॥
3.18.18: I have taken refuge in you in every way, O Maheśvara. Fulfil my desire, O Master; destroy the sorrow of the gods. ॥18॥
3.18.19: And I am especially afflicted by the sorrows of my sons, O Lord of the gods. Make me happy, O Īśa; you are the helper of the heaven-dwellers. ॥19॥
3.18.20: O Lord, becoming my son — for the gods and Yakṣas have been defeated by the mighty Daityas — O Śambhu, be the giver of joy to the gods. ॥20॥
3.18.21: May you always be the helper of all the gods, O Great Lord, so that the affliction caused by the Daityas may not trouble the gods, O Lord. ॥21॥
3.18.22: Nandīśvara said: When he had spoken thus, Śaṅkara, the Lord of all, said, so be it, and the blessed Hara vanished right there as he looked on. ॥22॥
3.18.23: Kaśyapa too, greatly delighted, quickly went to his own abode and respectfully told the gods the whole account. ॥23॥
3.18.24: Then Śaṅkara, Śarva, to make his own word true, was born of Surabhī from Kaśyapa, assuming eleven forms. ॥24॥
3.18.25: Then there was a great festival; everything became full of auspiciousness (śivamaya). The gods were delighted, as was the sage Kaśyapa. ॥25॥
3.18.26: Kapālī, Piṅgala, Bhīma, Virūpākṣa, Vilohita, Śāstā, Ajapāt, Ahirbudhnya, Śambhu, Caṇḍa and likewise Bhava. ॥26॥
3.18.27: These eleven Rudras are known as the sons of Surabhī; they were born for the gods' purpose, are forms of Śiva, and are the abode of happiness. ॥27॥
3.18.28: Those heroic Rudras, sons of Kaśyapa, of great strength and valour, rendering help to the gods, slew the Daityas in battle. ॥28॥
3.18.29: By the grace of those Rudras, the gods, having conquered the Daityas and become fearless, all of them headed by Śakra, with minds at ease, ruled their own kingdom. ॥29॥
3.18.30: Even today those great Rudras, all of them forms of Śiva, shine forever in heaven for the protection of the gods. ॥30॥
3.18.31: Affectionate to their devotees, they made their dwelling in the city of Īśāna, in the north-east; skilled in various sports, they always delight there. ॥31॥
3.18.32: Their attendants, also Rudras, are declared to number in crores; they are stationed everywhere there, in the three worlds, according to their respective portions. ॥32॥
3.18.33: Thus, dear one, I have described to you the incarnations of Śaṅkara, the Rudras eleven in number, who bring happiness to all the worlds. ॥33॥
3.18.34: This pure narrative destroys all sins; it is blessed, brings fame and long life, and grants all desires. ॥34॥
3.18.35: Whoever, dear one, listens to this or recites it to others with a concentrated mind, enjoys every happiness here and thereafter attains liberation. ॥35॥
3.18.iti: Thus ends the eighteenth adhyāya, named The eleven incarnations, in the third saṃhitā, the Śatarudra-saṃhitā, of the Śrī Śivamahāpurāṇa. ॥18॥
3.19.1: Nandīśvara said: Now hear with delight, O great sage, another deed of Śambhu: how Śaṅkara became Durvāsas for the sake of dharma. ॥1॥
3.19.2: There was a son of Brahmā, an exceedingly great ascetic, a knower of brahman, a master, the wise husband of Anasūyā, faithful in carrying out Brahmā's command. ॥2॥
3.19.3: At the clear instruction of Brahmā, he, together with his wife and desiring a son, went to the mountain named Tryakṣakula to perform austerity. ॥3॥
3.19.4: Restraining his breath according to rule on the bank of the river Nirvindhyā, the sage, free from the pairs of opposites, practised a very great austerity for a hundred years. ॥4॥
3.19.5: He had his mind fixed on this: Whoever is the one Lord, changeless, the great master — may he grant me an excellent son. ॥5॥
3.19.6: Much time passed while he performed true austerity; then from him arose a bright, immense flame. ॥6॥
3.19.7: By it all the worlds were almost burnt; the chief sages, and likewise all the gods and seers, Vāsava and the rest, were tormented. ॥7॥
3.19.8: Then all the gods led by Vāsava, and the sages, O sage, sorely tormented by that flame, quickly went to the abode of Brahmā. ॥8॥
3.19.9: Bowing to and praising Brahmā, the gods told him of their distress; and Brahmā, dear one, went swiftly with the gods to Viṣṇu's world. ॥9॥
3.19.10: Going there, Brahmā with the gods bowed to and praised the Lord of Ramā, and recounted to Viṣṇu that boundless distress of theirs, O sage. ॥10॥
3.19.11: And Viṣṇu, with Brahmā and the gods, went quickly to Rudra's abode; arriving there and bowing to Hara, he praised the Supreme Lord. ॥11॥
3.19.12: Having praised him at length, Viṣṇu reported to Śarva their distress, arisen from the flame of Atri's supreme austerity. ॥12॥
3.19.13: Then Brahmā, Viṣṇu and Maheśvara, gathered there, consulted with one another, O sage, about the welfare of the worlds. ॥13॥
3.19.14: Then those three gods, Brahmā and the others, foremost among bestowers of boons, quickly went to his hermitage to grant a boon to that seer. ॥14॥
3.19.15: Seeing them marked with their own emblems, Atri, best of sages, bowed and reverently praised them with pleasing words. ॥15॥
3.19.16: Then that brahmin, son of Brahmā, humble in spirit and astonished, with joined palms spoke to them, who were called Brahmā, Viṣṇu and Hara. ॥16॥
3.19.17: Atri said: O Brahmā, O Hari, O Rudra, you are held to be worthy of worship by the three worlds — the sources and lords, the agents of creation, preservation and dissolution. ॥17॥
3.19.18: Only one Lord was meditated upon by me, together with my wife, for the sake of a son — whoever is renowned as the Lord of the worlds. ॥18॥
3.19.19: Why have you three gods, foremost of boon-givers, come? Dispel this doubt of mine, and then grant the desired boon. ॥19॥
3.19.20: Hearing his words, the three gods replied: Just as your resolve was made, so has it come to pass, O lord of sages. ॥20॥
3.19.21: We three are equal lords of the world, foremost of boon-givers; therefore three sons born of our portions will be born to you. ॥21॥
3.19.22: All of them will be famed in the world, enhancing the glory of their parents. Having said this, the three gods joyfully went to their own abodes. ॥22॥
3.19.23: Having received the boon, the sage, giver of the bliss of brahman, then joyfully returned to his hermitage with Anasūyā, well pleased, O sage. ॥23॥
3.19.24: Then Brahmā, Hari and Śambhu, well pleased, descended into that woman in the form of sons, displaying various divine sports. ॥24॥
3.19.25: From a portion of Brahmā the Moon was born in Anasūyā from the lord of sages; it was he who later, cast into the ocean by the gods, emerged from the ocean. ॥25॥
3.19.26: From a portion of Viṣṇu, Datta was born to Atri in that woman, by whom the supreme path of renunciation was promoted, O sage. ॥26॥
3.19.27: From a portion of Śiva, O best of sages, was born to Atri in that woman Durvāsas, the tiger among sages, promulgator of excellent dharma. ॥27॥
3.19.28: And Rudra, having become Durvāsas, increaser of brahminical splendour, full of compassion, tested the dharma of many. ॥28॥
3.19.29: There was a king Ambarīṣa born in the Solar dynasty; he Durvāsas tested him — hear of that, O lord of sages. ॥29॥
3.19.30: That Ambarīṣa, best of kings, lord of the earth with its seven continents, kept a firm rule regarding the Ekādaśī vow. ॥30॥
3.19.31: The king was firmly resolved: Having kept the Ekādaśī vow, I shall break the fast on Dvādaśī. ॥31॥
3.19.32: Knowing of his observance, Durvāsas, best of sages, born of Śaṅkara's portion, went to him with many disciples. ॥32॥
3.19.33: Knowing that only a little of Dvādaśī remained for breaking the fast, just as he resolved to eat, he invited the sage who had arrived. ॥33॥
3.19.34: Then Durvāsas went with his disciples to bathe, and there the sage delayed long in order to test the king. ॥34॥
3.19.35: Then the king, seeing the obstacle to his dharma, sipped water as prescribed by scripture and waited there, longing for his return. ॥35॥
3.19.36: Meanwhile the sage Durvāsas arrived there; knowing the king had taken food, he assumed a wrathful form for the sake of the test. ॥36॥
3.19.37: He became furious with that king, in order to test his dharma; and the sage born of Śaṅkara's portion spoke fierce words. ॥37॥
3.19.38: Durvāsā said: Having invited me, O king, without feeding me you have drunk water, O wretch. I shall show you its fruit, for I am the wielder of the rod over the wicked. ॥38॥
3.19.39: Having said this, his eyes red with anger, he made ready to burn the king; at once the Lord's discus stationed there rose up to protect him. ॥39॥
3.19.40: That Sudarśana discus blazed fiercely to burn the sage, not knowing him to be a form of Śiva, being deluded by Śiva's māyā. ॥40॥
3.19.41: Meanwhile a bodiless voice from the sky spoke to Ambarīṣa, the great-souled one, devoted to brāhmaṇas and a Vaiṣṇava. ॥41॥
3.19.42: The heavenly voice said: This discus Sudarśana was bestowed on Hari by Śambhu. O king, now make it calm, blazing as it is against Durvāsas. ॥42॥
3.19.43: This Durvāsas is Śiva himself; it was he who gave the discus to Hari. Do not regard him, O best of kings, as an ordinary sage. ॥43॥
3.19.44: This lord of sages has come to test your dharma. Quickly go to him for refuge; otherwise destruction will follow. ॥44॥
3.19.45: Nandīśvara said: Having said this, O lord of sages, the voice from the sky fell silent. And Ambarīṣa too reverently praised him, that portion of Hara. ॥45॥
3.19.46: Ambarīṣa said: If there is merit from what I have given and sacrificed, or if my own dharma has been well performed, if our family holds brāhmaṇas as its deity, then may Hari's weapon be pacified. ॥46॥
3.19.47: If the Lord, devoted to me and affectionate to devotees, is pleased with us, may this weapon Sudarśana be pacified completely. ॥47॥
3.19.48: Nandīśvara said: As he was praising thus in front of Rudra, the Śaiva discus Sudarśana became wholly calm; and he, of clear understanding, knowing him to be a portion of Śiva, ॥48॥
3.19.49: then King Ambarīṣa bowed to that sage, recognising him as an incarnation of Śiva who had come to test him. ॥49॥
3.19.50: Then that sage, born of a portion of Śaṅkara, became very pleased; having eaten and granted him the boon he desired, he went to his own abode. ॥50॥
3.19.51: O sage, the deed of Durvāsas in testing Ambarīṣa has been told. Now hear another of his deeds, O lord of sages. ॥51॥
3.19.52: Again he tested Dāśarathi Rāma by means of the vow—the rule that had been made by Kāla in the guise of a sage, O sage. ॥52॥
3.19.53: At that very time that sage forcibly made Saumitri Lakṣmaṇa be sent in; and Rāma, bound by his pledge, at once abandoned his brother, O sage. ॥53॥
3.19.54: That story is well known in the world and has been told in many ways by sages; therefore I have not narrated it at length, since it is fully known to the wise. ॥54॥
3.19.55: Seeing his very firm adherence to the vow, the sage Durvāsas was highly pleased, and with a gladdened heart he granted him a boon. ॥55॥
3.19.56: He also tested the vow of Śrī Kṛṣṇa. Hear that, O best of sages; I shall tell you that story. ॥56॥
3.19.57: At Brahmā's request Viṣṇu became the son of Vasudeva, to remove the burden of the earth and to protect the good. ॥57॥
3.19.58: He who bore the name Kṛṣṇa slew the wicked, greatly sinful villains who harmed brāhmaṇas, and protected all the good people and brāhmaṇas. ॥58॥
3.19.59: That Kṛṣṇa, son of Vasudeva, showed exceeding devotion to brāhmaṇas; daily he fed many brāhmaṇas with delicious food. ॥59॥
3.19.60: Kṛṣṇa gained fame as being especially devoted to brāhmaṇas. Wishing to see him, that sage went to Kṛṣṇa's presence, O sage. ॥60॥
3.19.61: He himself had Kṛṣṇa, together with Rukmiṇī, harnessed to the chariot; having yoked them as the draught animal, he sat in it, and Kṛṣṇa, well pleased, drew him. ॥61॥
3.19.62: The sage got down from the chariot and, seeing that supreme steadfastness, became very pleased with him and gave him the boon of an adamantine body. ॥62॥
3.19.63: Once, while bathing in the celestial river, he became naked; the playful Durvāsas, best of sages, was embarrassed, O sage. ॥63॥
3.19.64: Knowing this, Draupadī, who was bathing there, respectfully covered his shame by giving a torn-off piece of the hem of her own garment. ॥64॥
3.19.65: The sage took that cloth, which had come near him with the current, covered his private parts with it, and became pleased with her. ॥65॥
3.19.66: He gave Draupadī the boon of the endless lengthening of her garment's hem; and through that boon Draupadī later made the Pāṇḍavas happy. ॥66॥
3.19.67: Two certain kings, Haṃsa and Ḍimbha, wicked men who had insulted him—that lord had them destroyed by giving a command to Hari. ॥67॥
3.19.68: He especially established brahminical splendour on earth, and also the path of renunciation (saṃnyāsa) according to the order of scriptural rules. ॥68॥
3.19.69: He uplifted many by imparting good instruction, and by bestowing knowledge he especially made many liberated. ॥69॥
3.19.70: Thus Durvāsas performed many wondrous deeds, which are blessed, bring fame and long life, and fulfil every wish of the one who hears them. ॥70॥
3.19.71: Whoever hears this account of Durvāsas with devotion and joy, or whoever causes others to hear it, is happy here and in the hereafter. ॥71॥
3.19.iti: Thus ends the nineteenth adhyāya, named The life of Durvāsas, in the third saṃhitā, the Śatarudra-saṃhitā, of the Śrī Śivamahāpurāṇa. ॥19॥
3.20.1: Nandīśvara said: Hereafter, O sage, listen with affection to the story of Hanumān: how Hara quickly performed excellent sports in that form. ॥1॥
3.20.2: The Supreme Lord lovingly did great good for Rāma. O brahmin, hear that entire story, which brings every happiness. ॥2॥
3.20.3: Once Śambhu, the Lord who performs wondrous deeds, beheld the Mohinī form of Viṣṇu, for he would assume the play of qualities. ॥3॥
3.20.4: Śambhu made himself agitated, as though struck by the arrows of Kāma; the Lord caused his semen to fall for the sake of Rāma's task. ॥4॥
3.20.5: Those seven sages, prompted by his mind, respectfully placed that semen on a leaf for the sake of Rāma's task. ॥5॥
3.20.6: Those great sages deposited Śambhu's semen into Añjanī, daughter of Gautama, through her ear, for the sake of Rāma's task. ॥6॥
3.20.7: Then in due time Śambhu was born from her, bearing the name Hanumān, in a monkey's body, of great strength and valour. ॥7॥
3.20.8: That Hanumān, lord of monkeys, mighty even as a child, at dawn quickly swallowed the sun's orb, thinking it a small fruit. ॥8॥
3.20.9: At the gods' entreaty he released it; and, the gods knowing him to be mighty and an incarnation of Śiva, he received boons given by the chief gods. ॥9॥
3.20.10: Then, greatly delighted, Hanumān went to his mother and respectfully told her all that had happened. ॥10॥
3.20.11: Then by her command that steadfast monkey, going daily into the Sun's presence, learned all knowledge from the Sun without effort. ॥11॥
3.20.12: By the Sun's command, having obtained his mother's permission, that best of monkeys, a portion of Rudra, went to Sugrīva, who was born of the Sun's portion. ॥12॥
3.20.13: Sugrīva, spurned by his elder brother Vālin, who enjoyed his wife, lived on Mount Ṛṣyamūka together with that Hanumān. ॥13॥
3.20.14: Then that wise, excellent monkey became the minister of Sukaṇṭha (Sugrīva); born of Hara's portion, he did Sugrīva good in every way. ॥14॥
3.20.15: He brought about a happy friendship between him and Rāma, who had come there with his brother, grieving, his wife having been abducted. ॥15॥
3.20.16: And Rāma slew Vālin, elephant among monkeys, the sinful enjoyer of his brother's wife, who fancied himself a hero. ॥16॥
3.20.17: Then, dear one, by Rāma's command the wise Hanumān, lord of monkeys, undertook the search for Sītā with many monkeys. ॥17॥
3.20.18: Learning that Sītā had been taken to Laṅkā, the lord of monkeys swiftly leapt across that ocean, uncrossable by others, and went there. ॥18॥
3.20.19: There he performed wondrous deeds full of valour, and lovingly gave Sītā the excellent token of his master. ॥19॥
3.20.20: That heroic leader of monkeys quickly removed Sītā's grief by telling her the news of Rāma, which saved her life. ॥20॥
3.20.21: Taking her token, he set out back toward Rāma; having wrecked Rāvaṇa's garden, he killed many rākṣasas. ॥21॥
3.20.22: At that very time, having slain Rāvaṇa's son along with many rākṣasas, that fearless mighty one created great havoc there. ॥22॥
3.20.23: When, O sage, he was set on fire by the mighty Rāvaṇa, who had wrapped him tightly in oil-soaked cloths, ॥23॥
3.20.24: then that monkey, born of Mahādeva's portion, leaping again and again, burned all of Laṅkā, making that very fire his pretext. ॥24॥
3.20.25: Having burned Laṅkā, sparing Vibhīṣaṇa's house, that heroic elephant among monkeys then dropped into the ocean. ॥25॥
3.20.26: Extinguishing his tail there, he reached its far shore; unwearied, he who was born of Giriśa's portion went to Rāma's presence. ॥26॥
3.20.27: Without delay the swift Hanumān, best of monkeys, came near Rāma and gave him Sītā's crest-jewel. ॥27॥
3.20.28: Then by his command the mighty hero, gathering many great mountains with the monkeys, had a bridge built over the ocean. ॥28॥
3.20.29: Then Rāma, going there and wishing to cross, installed a Śiva-liṅga and duly worshipped it, desiring victory. ॥29॥
3.20.30: By his boon he obtained the excellent gift of victory, then crossed the ocean, surrounded Laṅkā with the monkeys, and fought the rākṣasas. ॥30॥
3.20.31: Then the hero Hanumān slew the asuras and protected Rāma's army; and he revived Lakṣmaṇa, wounded by the Śakti weapon, with the sañjīvinī herb. ॥31॥
3.20.32: He made Lakṣmaṇa, together with Rāma, happy in every way; that lord, born of Mahādeva, protected the whole army. ॥32॥
3.20.33: Tirelessly he destroyed Rāvaṇa with his whole retinue; that monkey of mighty grip made the gods happy. ॥33॥
3.20.34: Having slain the one named Mahīrāvaṇa, he brought Rāma with Lakṣmaṇa back from that place to their own camp and protected them. ॥34॥
3.20.35: The bull among monkeys swiftly accomplished Rāma's task in every way; he subdued the asuras and performed various sports. ॥35॥
3.20.36: The lord of monkeys established devotion to Rāma on earth, himself becoming the foremost devotee, bestower of happiness on Sītā and Rāma. ॥36॥
3.20.37: He is the giver of life to Lakṣmaṇa, the remover of the pride of all the gods, the blessed incarnation of Rudra, the uplifter of devotees. ॥37॥
3.20.38: That Hanumān, the great hero, ever doing Rāma's work, is known in the world as Rāma's messenger, slayer of demons, loving toward devotees. ॥38॥
3.20.39: Thus, dear one, I have told you the excellent story of Hanumān, which is blessed, brings fame and long life, and grants the fruit of all desires. ॥39॥
3.20.40: Whoever hears this with devotion, or attentively causes it to be heard, enjoys all desires here and at the end attains supreme liberation. ॥40॥
3.20.iti: Thus ends the twentieth adhyāya, named The incarnation as Hanumān and his deeds, in the third saṃhitā, the Śatarudra-saṃhitā, of the Śrī Śivamahāpurāṇa. ॥20॥
3.21.1: Nandīśvara said: Now, O sage, O son of the Self-born Brahmā, listen with delight to the supreme incarnation of the Lord Śaṅkara, which grants all desires to those who hear it. ॥1॥
3.21.2: Once, O tiger among sages, both Girijā and Śaṅkara, the supreme rulers, by their own will became desirous of sporting. ॥2॥
3.21.3: Making Bhairava the doorkeeper, they went inside, lovingly attended by various groups of companions, behaving in human fashion. ॥3॥
3.21.4: Having sported there for a long time, the two independent supreme lords, performers of various pastimes, became pleased, O sage. ॥4॥
3.21.5: Then the independent goddess Śivā, playfully assuming a frenzied form, came to the door in that form, having obtained the Lord's permission. ॥5॥
3.21.6: Then that Bhairava, looking at the goddess with the gaze one casts on a woman and infatuated by her form, forbade her to go out. ॥6॥
3.21.7: When she was gazed upon by Bhairava as a woman, O sage, the goddess Śivā became angry, and then Ambikā cursed him. ॥7॥
3.21.8: Śivā said: Since you look at me as a woman, O vilest of men, therefore, Bhairava, you shall become a human on earth. ॥8॥
3.21.9: Nandīśvara said: When Bhairava was thus cursed by Śivā, O sage, there was a great outcry of lamentation; he, through divine play, came to grief. ॥9॥
3.21.10: Then Śaṅkara, skilled in various ways of conciliation, quickly came to him, O lord of sages, and consoled Bhairava. ॥10॥
3.21.11: Then, because of that curse, Bhairava descended on earth, O sage, in a human womb, known by the name Vetāla, by Śaṅkara's will. ॥11॥
3.21.12: Out of affection for him, the all-pervading Śiva too descended on earth together with Śivā, engaged in noble play and adopting a worldly mode of life. ॥12॥
3.21.13: Śiva was named Maheśa and Girijā was Śāradā, O sage; the two, skilled in various pastimes, joyfully performed fine sport. ॥13॥
3.21.14: Thus, dear one, the excellent story of Maheśa has been told to you; it is blessed, bestows fame and long life, and grants the fruit of all desires. ॥14॥
3.21.15: Whoever hears this with devotion, or attentively causes it to be heard, enjoys all pleasures here and in the end attains liberation. ॥15॥
3.21.iti: Thus ends the twenty-first adhyāya, named The Maheśa incarnation, in the third saṃhitā, the Śatarudra-saṃhitā, of the Śrī Śivamahāpurāṇa. ॥21॥
3.22.1: Nandīśvara said: Listen, O wise son of Brahmā, O lord of sages, to the excellent incarnation of Śiva named Vṛṣeśa, full of noble sport, which took away Hari's pride. ॥1॥
3.22.2: Long ago all the gods and demons, tormented by fear of old age and death, made a pact with each other and became eager to obtain the jewels. ॥2॥
3.22.3: Then all the gods and demons, O delight of the sage, set about churning the Ocean of Milk, the finest of oceans. ॥3॥
3.22.4: All the gods and demons, smiling brightly, wondered, O brahmin: By what means could this churning of it be done, for the accomplishment of our purpose? ॥4॥
3.22.5: Then a voice from the sky, its sound deep as a thundercloud, spoke to the gods and the demons by the Lord's command, reassuring them. ॥5॥
3.22.6: The heavenly voice said: O gods and demons, churn the Ocean of Milk; strength and wisdom will surely be yours, there is no doubt. ॥6॥
3.22.7: Make Mandara the churning rod and Vāsuki the rope; uniting together, all of you, churn with diligence. ॥7॥
3.22.8: Nandīśvara said: Having heard that voice from the sky, all the gods and demons then made effort to carry it out, O best of sages. ॥8॥
3.22.9: Having made a firm pact, they all went to Mandara, the finest of mountains, gold-hued, straight, and adorned with many splendours. ॥9॥
3.22.10: Having fully propitiated that lord of the mountain and being permitted by him, the gods and demons, wishing to carry it to the ocean of milk, uprooted it by force. ॥10॥
3.22.11: Having uprooted it with their arms, they all went toward the Ocean of Milk, O sage; but, their strength spent, they became unable to carry it there. ॥11॥
3.22.12: Slipping from their arms, that exceedingly heavy Mount Mandara suddenly fell at once right upon the gods and demons. ॥12॥
3.22.13: Thus, their effort shattered, the gods and demons were crushed; then, regaining consciousness, they praised the Lord of the world. ॥13॥
3.22.14: By his will they all rose up again, lifted that mountain, carried it, and cast it into the water at the northern shore of the Ocean of Milk. ॥14॥
3.22.15: Then the hosts of gods and demons, making Vāsuki the rope and desiring to obtain the jewels, churned the Ocean of Milk. ॥15॥
3.22.16: As the Ocean of Milk was being churned, Śrī, the great sovereign of the heavenly world, daughter of Bhṛgu and beloved of Hari, arose from the ocean. ॥16॥
3.22.17: Then arose Dhanvantari, the moon, the great tree Pārijāta, the horse Uccaiḥśravas, and likewise the elephant Airāvata; ॥17॥
3.22.18: wine (Surā), Hari's bow, the conch, then the wish-yielding cows, the jewel called Kaustubha, and also the nectar. ॥18॥
3.22.19: And as it was churned again, the great poison Kālakūṭa was born, blazing like the fire at the end of an age, bringing terror to gods and demons. ॥19॥
3.22.20: At the time the nectar was born, from the drops that spilled outside arose many beautiful women of wondrous appearance, ॥20॥
3.22.21: with faces like the full autumn moon, radiant as lightning, the sun and fire, adorned with necklaces, armlets, bracelets and divine gems. ॥21॥
3.22.22: Sprinkling the ten directions with the nectar-water of their loveliness, with long glances and arched brows, they drove the world to madness. ॥22॥
3.22.23: They were born by the crore from the nectar, issued forth as embodiments of desire. Then arose the nectar that wards off old age and death. ॥23॥
3.22.24: Keśava took Lakṣmī, the conch, the Kaustubha and the sword; the Sun respectfully took the divine horse Uccaiḥśravas. ॥24॥
3.22.25: Śacī's husband, the lord of the immortals, eagerly took the Pārijāta, best of trees, and Airāvata, lord of elephants. ॥25॥
3.22.26: Śaṅkara Śambhu, affectionate to his devotees, of his own will held the Kālakūṭa in his throat and bore the moon, for the protection of the gods. ॥26॥
3.22.27: The demons, deluded by the Lord's command, took the lovely woman named Surā, O Vyāsa; and all people took Dhanvantari. ॥27॥
3.22.28: All the sages, lords among sages, took the wish-granting cow; and those bewitching women remained as common to all. ॥28॥
3.22.29: For the sake of the nectar a great war broke out between the gods and demons, each seeking victory, their minds agitated against one another. ॥29॥
3.22.30: And the nectar was seized by force by the demons led by Bali, O Vyāsa, radiant like the fire and sun at the end of an age, having conquered the gods. ॥30॥
3.22.31: The gods, Śakra and the rest, all distressed by Śiva's māyā and harassed by the demons' might, sought refuge in Śaṅkara, dear son. ॥31॥
3.22.32: Then, by Śiva's command, that nectar was carefully taken back from the demons by the Lord of Ramā, through māyā, in the form of a woman, O sage. ॥32॥
3.22.33: Hari, best of masters of illusion, assuming a woman's form as Mohinī and deluding all the demons, made those gods drink it. ॥33॥
3.22.34: The chief demons went near her and said: Serve this nectar; let there be no discrimination here among the rows. ॥34॥
3.22.35: Having said this, all those Daityas and Dānavas, deluded by Śiva's māyā, gave the nectar to Viṣṇu, who wore a deceptive form. ॥35॥
3.22.36: Meanwhile, the chief Dānavas, seeing the women born from the nectar, led them away to their own places as they pleased. ॥36॥
