3.22.37: Their cities were divine, a hundred times finer than heaven, well guarded by fearsome machines, and fashioned by the magic of Maya. ॥37॥
3.22.38: Having made all those cities secure, the demons, without having touched the women's breasts, went forth to battle, having indeed made a vow: ॥38॥
3.22.39: We shall not touch these women if we are defeated by the gods. Having said this, all those great heroic demons, eager for battle, ॥39॥
3.22.40: then roared lion-roars and blew their conches each separately, as though filling the sky and gratifying the clouds. ॥40॥
3.22.41: A terrifying battle took place between the gods and the asuras, known as the Devāsura war, unequalled and famous throughout the three worlds. ॥41॥
3.22.42: All the gods, protected by Viṣṇu, won victory; the daityas fled there, struck down by Viṣṇu together with the immortals. ॥42॥
3.22.43: The daityas, bewildered by the gods and by the great-souled Viṣṇu, those left over from the slaughter, entered Pātāla and its caverns. ॥43॥
3.22.44: Viṣṇu, the mighty one holding the discus in his hand, pursued them, going to the supreme Pātāla where they were staying as if utterly terrified. ॥44॥
3.22.45: Meanwhile Viṣṇu saw lovely women born from the nectar, with faces like the full moon, proud of their divine beauty. ॥45॥
3.22.46: Bewildered by the arrows of Kāma, he found delight right there, and he indeed took to sporting with those excellent women. ॥46॥
3.22.47: From them Viṣṇu begot sons of great valour, skilled in many kinds of warfare, making the whole earth tremble. ॥47॥
3.22.48: Then those sons of Hari, of great strength and valour, wrought great havoc, causing suffering in heaven and on earth. ॥48॥
3.22.49: Seeing the affliction of the worlds, the gods and sages then, bowing down to Brahmā, made a report about them to him. ॥49॥
3.22.50: Hearing that, Brahmā took them along and went to Mount Kailāsa; there, seeing the god Śiva, he bowed again and again. ॥50॥
3.22.51: With shoulders bowed and palms joined, he praised him with various hymns, saying: Victory, O god, O Mahādeva, O lord of all! ॥51॥
3.22.52: Brahmā said: O god of gods, O Mahādeva, O lord, protect all the worlds, afflicted by Viṣṇu's sons dwelling in Pātāla, who have become depraved. ॥52॥
3.22.53: O all-pervading one, Hari, his mind attached to the women born of the nectar, now stays in Pātāla and, being perverted, takes his pleasure there. ॥53॥
3.22.54: Nandīśvara said: Thus Śambhu was much praised by Brahmā together with the sages and gods, for the protection of the worlds and for bringing back Viṣṇu. ॥54॥
3.22.55: Then that blessed Śambhu, Maheśvara, ocean of compassion, understanding that affliction, took the form of a bull. ॥55॥
3.22.iti: Thus ends the twenty-second adhyāya, named The trouble caused by Viṣṇu and the bull incarnation, in the third saṃhitā, the Śatarudra-saṃhitā, of the Śrī Śivamahāpurāṇa. ॥22॥
3.23.1: Nandīśvara said: Then the bearer of Pināka, roaring in the form of a bull, entered the cavern there, uttering terrifying roars. ॥1॥
3.23.2: At his roars the cities and towns fell down, and then a trembling seized all the inhabitants of the cities. ॥2॥
3.23.3: Then the Bull confronted the sons of Hari, who had raised their bows for battle, mighty in strength and valour, their minds deluded by Śiva's māyā. ॥3॥
3.23.4: Then those sons of Hari became enraged, O best of sages; the heroes, roaring loudly, rushed towards Śaṅkara. ॥4॥
3.23.5: Rudra, bearing the form of a bull, grew angry at those sons of Hari as they came on, and tore the sons of Viṣṇu apart with his hooves and horns. ॥5॥
3.23.6: All those sons of Hari, their limbs torn apart by Rudra, quickly perished, lifeless and senseless. ॥6॥
3.23.7: When those sons had been slain, Viṣṇu, the foremost of the mighty, came out, roared loudly, and went swiftly up to Hara. ॥7॥
3.23.8: Seeing Rudra, the Bull who had slain Viṣṇu's sons, moving about, Keśava struck him with arrows and with divine missiles. ॥8॥
3.23.9: Then Mahādeva, enraged, in the form of a bull, mighty in his fury, the dweller in the mountains, swallowed those missiles of Viṣṇu. ॥9॥
3.23.10: Then that Maheśvara in the form of a bull, flying into a great rage, bellowed most terribly, shaking the three worlds, O sage. ॥10॥
3.23.11: Then, leaping up with force, he tore with hooves and horns at Viṣṇu, Hari, who was agitated with anger, deluded, and did not recognise his own Lord. ॥11॥
3.23.12: Then Hari, deluded by māyā, unable to bear that blow, quickly became weakened in spirit and pained in his limbs. ॥12॥
3.23.13: Hari, his pride gone, bewildered and dazed, recognised the Supreme Lord sporting in the form of a bull. ॥13॥
3.23.14: Then, having realised that the Lord of Gaurī had come in the form of a bull, he spoke in a deep voice, with bowed shoulders and joined palms. ॥14॥
3.23.15: Hari said: O God of gods, Mahādeva, ocean of compassion, O Lord, O Maheśāna, deluded by your māyā, my mind was utterly confused. ॥15॥
3.23.16: I have fought a battle with you, the Lord, my own master, O Lord. Showing compassion to me, O master, may that offence indeed be forgiven. ॥16॥
3.23.17: Nandīśvara said: Hearing those words spoken by Hari in humility, O sage, the blessed Śaṅkara, loving to his devotees, spoke to the Lord of Ramā. ॥17॥
3.23.18: O Viṣṇu, O you of great intellect, how did you not recognise me? You fought a battle; how today has all your knowledge been forgotten? ॥18॥
3.23.19: Why do you not know yourself, whose valour depends on me? You should take no delight here; turn back from this wrongful conduct. ॥19॥
3.23.20: How can knowledge remain when one is subject to desire, attached to women and given to pleasure? This is not fitting for you, O Lord of gods; remember your role as the deliverer of the world. ॥20॥
3.23.21: Hearing those words of Śambhu, which bestow true understanding, with reverence, Viṣṇu, ashamed in his own mind, spoke to Maheśvara. ॥21॥
3.23.22: Viṣṇu said: My discus is here; taking it with care, I shall go to that world of mine, obeying your command. ॥22॥
3.23.23: Nandīśvara said: Hearing Viṣṇu's words, Hara, the great Lord in the form of a bull, the protector of dharma, replied again to Hari. ॥23॥
3.23.24: No delay should be made; you must go quickly from here. By my command, O Hari, go to your world; let the discus remain right here. ॥24॥
3.23.25: For the sake of maintaining the lineage and the Ādityas, and also on account of my word of auspicious grace, I therefore give you another discus, more terrible. ॥25॥
3.23.26: Having said this, Hara fashioned a divine, supreme discus, blazing like the fire of time, destroyer of all the wicked. ॥26॥
3.23.27: He gave the discus, shining like ten thousand fierce suns, to the great-souled Viṣṇu, protector of all the immortals and chief sages. ॥27॥
3.23.28: Having received that other discus, Sudarśana, of supreme brilliance, Viṣṇu, the foremost of the wise, spoke there to the gods. ॥28॥
3.23.29: You, the best of all the gods, listen attentively to my words; it should be done accordingly and quickly; then you will have well-being. ॥29॥
3.23.30: In Pātāla there are divine, excellent women endowed with youth; whoever wishes to enjoy great sport with them, let him do so. ॥30॥
3.23.31: Hearing those words from Keśava, the heroic beings of divine birth became eager to enter Pātāla together with Viṣṇu. ॥31॥
3.23.32: Then, perceiving their intention, the blessed Hara in anger pronounced a terrible curse upon the eight classes of divine beings. ॥32॥
3.23.33: Hara said: Except for a tranquil sage, or the Dānavas, or one born of my portion, whoever enters this place shall meet death in an instant. ॥33॥
3.23.34: Hearing these terrible words, which further the welfare of humankind, the gods, rebuffed by Rudra, returned to their own homes. ॥34॥
3.23.35: Thus the supreme Viṣṇu, who had become attached to women, was admonished by Śiva and went to the heavenly world, O Vyāsa; and the world regained its well-being. ॥35॥
3.23.36: And the blessed Śaṅkara as Vṛṣeśvara, loving to his devotees, having thus accomplished the gods' task, went to his own lord of mountains. ॥36॥
3.23.37: Thus has been described the Vṛṣeśvara incarnation of Śaṅkara — Śarva, remover of Viṣṇu's delusion, bringer of happiness to the three worlds. ॥37॥
3.23.38: This narrative is purifying, supremely removing the oppression of enemies; it leads to heaven, brings fame and long life, and grants enjoyment and liberation to the good. ॥38॥
3.23.39: Whoever listens to this with devotion, or attentively causes it to be heard, and whoever reads it or teaches it to wise men — he, having enjoyed all desires, attains liberation at the end. ॥39॥
3.23.iti: Thus ends the twenty-third adhyāya, named The incarnation of Śiva called Vṛṣeśvara, in the third saṃhitā, the Śatarudra-saṃhitā, of the Śrī Śivamahāpurāṇa. ॥23॥
3.24.1: Nandīśvara said: O wise one, listen with great love to another incarnation of the great Lord, called Pippalāda. It is excellent and increases devotion. ॥1॥
3.24.2: The brāhmaṇa Dadhīci, best of sages, who was spoken of earlier, was a great Śaiva and very mighty, the son of Cyavana, born in the line of Bhṛgu. ॥2॥
3.24.3: In the battle with Kṣuva, he, with Maheśvara as his helper, defeated Viṣṇu together with the gods and then cursed him. ॥3॥
3.24.4: His wife, the highly fortunate Suvarcā by name, was a virtuous woman, supremely devoted to her husband. It was she who cursed the gods. ॥4॥
3.24.5: Therefore Mahādeva, who is skilled in many kinds of divine play, became manifest in her through him, radiant, under the name Pippalāda. ॥5॥
3.24.6: Sūta said: Hearing these wonderful words of Nandīśvara, Sanatkumāra, the foremost of sages, bowed his shoulders, joined his palms and spoke. ॥6॥
3.24.7: Sanatkumāra said: O Nandīśvara, greatly wise one, you bear the very form of Rudra himself. You are blessed, dear one, a true guru, for you have let me hear this wonderful story. ॥7॥
3.24.8: Long ago, dear son of Śilāda, I heard from Brahmā about Viṣṇu's defeat in the battle with Kṣuva, and about his curse as well. ॥8॥
3.24.9: Now I wish to hear about the curse that Suvarcā laid on the gods, and after that the auspicious story of Pippalāda. ॥9॥
3.24.10: Sūta said: Hearing these fine words of the son of Vidhi (Brahmā), the son of Śilāda, glad at heart, remembered Śiva's lotus feet and replied. ॥10॥
3.24.11: Nandīśvara said: Once, O lord of sages, all the gods, led by Vāsava (Indra), were defeated by the Daityas who were allies of the asura Vṛtra. ॥11॥
3.24.12: All the gods had deposited their own fine weapons in Dadhīca's hermitage, and so they were suddenly and swiftly defeated. ॥12॥
3.24.13: Then all the gods with Indra, and likewise the seers, as they were being slain, hurried to Brahmaloka and told of their calamity. ॥13॥
3.24.14: On hearing the gods' words, Brahmā, grandfather of the worlds, told them everything truly, including what Tvaṣṭṛ intended to do. ॥14॥
3.24.15: O gods, Tvaṣṭṛ produced him through austerity in order to kill you: Vṛtra by name, of great might, the mighty lord of all the Daityas. ॥15॥
3.24.16: So let an effort be made by which he may be killed. Listen, wise one, to the means for it; I tell it to you for the sake of dharma. ॥16॥
3.24.17: The great sage Dadhīci, an ascetic who has mastered his senses, long ago worshipped Śiva and obtained the boon that his bones would be as hard as the vajra. ॥17॥
3.24.18: Ask him for his bones; he will give them, no doubt. Make a staff-like vajra from them and slay Vṛtra, no doubt. ॥18॥
3.24.19: Nandīśvara said: Hearing Brahmā's words, Śakra, accompanied by his guru and the gods, came at once to Dadhīci's excellent hermitage. ॥19॥
3.24.20: Seeing the sage there with Suvarcā, Śakra, together with his guru and the gods, humbly bowed to him with reverence and joined palms. ॥20॥
3.24.21: Understanding their intention, the sage, best of the wise, sent his wife Suvarcā into the inner part of his hermitage. ॥21॥
3.24.22: Then the king of the gods, with the gods, intent on achieving his own purpose and following the science of statecraft, addressed the lord of sages. ॥22॥
3.24.23: Śakra said: All of us gods, and the seers too, have been harmed by Tvaṣṭṛ. We have come for refuge to you, the great Śaiva, the giver, who protects those who seek shelter. ॥23॥
3.24.24: O brāhmaṇa, give us your bones, which are made of great vajra. With your bone I will make my thunderbolt and kill the enemy of the gods. ॥24॥
3.24.25: Addressed thus by him, the sage, who delighted in helping others, meditated on Śiva, his own Lord, and gave up his body. ॥25॥
3.24.26: His bonds destroyed, the sage went at once to Brahmaloka. A rain of flowers fell there, and everyone was struck with wonder. ॥26॥
3.24.27: Then Śakra quickly summoned the cow Surabhi and had her lick the body clean. He directed Tvāṣṭra (Viśvakarman) to make weapons from those bones. ॥27॥
3.24.28: So commanded, Viśvakarman fashioned all the weapons from those bones, which were vajra-like and very hard through Śiva's power. ॥28॥
3.24.29: From the bones of his spine he made the vajra, an arrow and likewise the Brahmaśiras; from his other bones he made many other fine weapons. ॥29॥
3.24.30: O sage, Indra, strengthened by Śiva's power, raised that vajra and charged at Vṛtra in anger, as Rudra charged at Antaka (Death). ॥30॥
3.24.31: Then Śakra, fully armed, swiftly and with force cut off Vṛtra's head with that vajra, as one would a mountain peak. ॥31॥
3.24.32: Then, dear one, there was a great festival among the heaven-dwellers. The gods praised Śakra, and showers of flowers fell. ॥32॥
3.24.33: Thus, dear one, I have told you this story in passing. Now listen with great reverence as I tell of Śambhu's incarnation as Pippalāda. ॥33॥
3.24.34: Suvarcā, the devoted wife of the great-souled sage Dadhīca, went into her hermitage as he had commanded. ॥34॥
3.24.35: Having gone there, the ascetic woman, not seeing her husband, did all the household work as her husband had instructed, ॥35॥
3.24.36: and then came back there. O best of sages, seeing so much that was inauspicious, and those gods, Suvarcā was astonished. ॥36॥
3.24.37: Learning that all this was the doing of the gods, the virtuous Suvarcā, wife of the best of seers, became angry then; deeply enraged, she pronounced a curse on them. ॥37॥
3.24.38: She said: Ah! You gods are all most wicked, clever only at your own interests, foolish and greedy. Therefore, from this day on, by my word, may all of you, Indra included, become animals. ॥38॥
3.24.39: In this way the ascetic Suvarcā, the sage's beloved, laid a curse on all those gods, Śakra included. ॥39॥
3.24.40: Then that devoted, resolute wife wished to follow her husband to his world, and she built a funeral pyre with very pure firewood. ॥40॥
3.24.41: Then a voice from the sky, sent by Giriśa, comforting her and giving happiness, spoke to Suvarcā, the sage's beloved. ॥41॥
3.24.42: The heavenly voice said: Do not act rashly, O wise one; hear my supreme word. The sage's seed is in your womb; bring it forth with care. ॥42॥
3.24.43: After that, O lady, you may carry out the course you desire. A pregnant woman should not burn her body — this is Brahmā's injunction. ॥43॥
3.24.44: Nandīśvara said: Having said this, that heavenly voice fell silent, O lord of sages. Hearing it, the sage's wife was astonished for a moment. ॥44॥
3.24.45: That Suvarcā, the greatly chaste woman, longing for her husband's world, sat down and then tore open her belly with a stone. ॥45॥
3.24.46: From her womb came forth that embryo of the excellent sage, with a great divine body, radiant, illuminating the ten directions. ॥46॥
3.24.47: He was directly an incarnation of Rudra, born of the excellent energy of Dadhīci, manifested of himself, O dear one, capable of performing his own divine play. ॥47॥
3.24.48: Seeing that divine son of hers and his form, the sage's wife Suvarcā recognised in her mind that he was directly an incarnation of Rudra. ॥48॥
3.24.49: The greatly chaste woman was delighted; bowing at once, she praised him and installed that form in her heart, O lord of sages. ॥49॥
3.24.50: And the mother Suvarcā, of pure eyes, smiling, spoke with great affection to that son, longing for her husband's world. ॥50॥
3.24.51: Suvarcā said: O dear one, Supreme Lord, remain long near this aśvattha tree, O most fortunate one; may you be the giver of happiness to all. ॥51॥
3.24.52: Lovingly permit me now to go to my husband's world; staying there with my husband, I shall meditate on you, who bear the form of Rudra. ॥52॥
3.24.53: Nandīśvara said: Having thus spoken to her son, the chaste Suvarcā then followed her husband by means of supreme meditative absorption. ॥53॥
3.24.54: Thus that wife of Dadhīca, united with her husband, O sage, reached Śiva's world and joyfully served Śaṅkara. ॥54॥
3.24.55: Meanwhile the gods together with Indra, along with the sages, came there quickly, O dear one, delighted, as if they had been summoned. ॥55॥
3.24.56: Hari and Brahmā, with great joy, went with their own attendants to Śaṅkara, who had descended on earth in Suvarcā from Dadhīca. ॥56॥
3.24.57: Seeing there Rudra, who had descended and become the sage's son, all bowed and praised him with joined palms. ॥57॥
3.24.58: Then there was a great festival of the gods, O best of sages. Drums resounded there, and dancing women danced with joy. ॥58॥
3.24.59: The sons of the Gandharvas sang, and the Kinnaras, players of instruments, played; the immortals played music and showered flowers. ॥59॥
3.24.60: Having duly performed the sacraments for that resplendent son of Dadhīci, father of Pippalāda, all of them, Viṣṇu and the others, praised him again. ॥60॥
3.24.61: Brahmā, pleased in mind, gave him the name Pippalāda. Together with Hari and the gods he said: Be gracious, O Lord of the gods. ॥61॥
3.24.62: Having said this and taken leave of him, Brahmā, Viṣṇu and likewise the gods all went each to their own abode, having celebrated a great festival. ॥62॥
3.24.63: Then Rudra as Pippalāda, the great Lord, performed austerities at the root of the aśvattha tree for a very long time, desiring the welfare of the worlds. ॥63॥
3.24.64: Thus, while that Pippalāda, who conformed to the ways of the world, was performing intense austerities, a long time passed before him. ॥64॥
3.24.iti: Thus ends the twenty-fourth adhyāya, named The Pippalāda incarnation, in the third saṃhitā, the Śatarudra-saṃhitā, of the Śrī Śivamahāpurāṇa. ॥24॥
3.25.1: Nandīśvara said: Then, having established order in the world, out of a wish to establish dharma, the Lord performed a great sport. Ah, listen to it, O good sage. ॥1॥
3.25.2: Once, while going to bathe in the Puṣpabhadrā river, the lord of sages saw Padmā, a young woman who was a portion of Śivā and exceedingly charming. ॥2॥
3.25.3: Desiring to obtain her, he—a wanderer through the worlds, discerning in the truth of the world—went to the residence of her father, King Anaraṇya. ॥3॥
3.25.4: The king of men, seeing him, bowed, and, overcome with fear, offered madhuparka and the rest and worshipped him with devotion. ॥4॥
3.25.5: Having accepted everything with affection, the sage asked for the maiden. The king fell silent, unable to say anything. ॥5॥
3.25.6: The sage said to the king: Give me the maiden with devotion; otherwise I shall reduce everything to ashes, together with you. ॥6॥
3.25.7: Then all the king's people were overwhelmed by the splendour of Pippalāda, the son of Dadhīci, the great sage. ॥7॥
3.25.8: Then the king, greatly frightened and lamenting again and again, gave the adorned maiden Padmā to the aged sage. ॥8॥
3.25.9: Having married Padmā, the king's daughter, a portion of Śivā, the sage Pippalāda took her and joyfully went to his own hermitage. ॥9॥
3.25.10: Having gone there, that best of sages, greatly decrepit with age, an ascetic not given to excessive passion, dwelt with that woman. ॥10॥
3.25.11: Then that daughter of Anaraṇya served the sage with devotion in deed, mind and speech, as Lakṣmī serves Nārāyaṇa. ॥11॥
3.25.12: Thus Pippalāda, the best of sages, a portion of Śiva, having become young through his own sport, delighted with that young woman. ॥12॥
3.25.13: Ten great-souled sons, excellent ascetics, were born, all equal to their father the sage, increasing Padmā's happiness. ॥13॥
3.25.14: Thus Pippalāda, the best of sages, the lord who performs many sports, is indeed a sportive incarnation of Śaṅkara, the great Lord. ॥14॥
3.25.15: It was he, the compassionate one, by whom a boon was lovingly granted to the people, having seen in the world the affliction caused by Śani, which none could ward off: ॥15॥
3.25.16: Up to sixteen years from birth, that affliction shall not befall men, nor likewise Śiva's devotees; this word of mine is indeed true. ॥16॥
3.25.17: If Śani, disregarding my word, should ever afflict those men, then he would be reduced to ashes—there is no doubt. ॥17॥
3.25.18: Thus, dear one, out of fear of that, Śanaiścara, the foremost of planets, though malignant, never causes affliction to them. ॥18॥
3.25.19: Thus, O good sage, the excellent story of Pippalāda, who became a man in sport, has been told to you; it grants the fruit of all desires. ॥19॥
3.25.20: Gādhi, Kauśika, and the great sage Pippalāda—these three, when remembered, destroy the affliction caused by Śanaiścara. ॥20॥
3.25.21: Whatever man on earth reads or hears, with true devotion, the story of Pippalāda together with the story of Padmā— ॥21॥
3.25.22: —whoever reads or hears this excellent story for the destruction of Śani's affliction would obtain all desires. ॥22॥
3.25.23: Blessed is that best of sages Dadhīci, wise, a great devotee of Śiva, dear to the good; his son is Maheśāna himself, named Pippalāda, self-possessed. ॥23॥
3.25.24: This narrative, dear one, is sinless, leads to heaven, removes the defects of malefic planets, grants all desires, and increases devotion to Śiva. ॥24॥
3.25.iti: Thus ends the twenty-fifth adhyāya, named The deeds of the Pippalāda incarnation, in the third saṃhitā, the Śatarudra-saṃhitā, of the Śrī Śivamahāpurāṇa. ॥25॥
3.26.1: Nandīśvara said: Listen, dear one; I shall describe, O sage, the supremely blissful incarnation of Śiva, the Supreme Self, which is called Vaiśyanātha. ॥1॥
3.26.2: Long ago in Nandigrāma there lived a certain courtesan, renowned as Mahānandā, a devotee of Śiva and exceedingly beautiful. ॥2॥
3.26.3: She was endowed with great wealth, rich in fine riches, radiantly splendid, and full of the charm of adornment set off with many kinds of jewels. ॥3॥
3.26.4: She was skilled in all the arts of music and exceedingly captivating; queens and kings alike delighted in her singing. ॥4॥
3.26.5: That courtesan always joyfully worshipped Śaṅkara together with Ambā; she was devoted to repeating Śiva's name and wore ashes and rudrākṣa beads as ornaments. ॥5॥
3.26.6: Having worshipped Śiva every day and serving the Lord of the world, she danced with supreme devotion, singing Śiva's true glory. ॥6॥
3.26.7: Having adorned a monkey and also a cock with rudrākṣas, she would always make them dance with hand-claps and songs. ॥7॥
3.26.8: Seeing the two of them dancing, that courtesan, devoted to Śiva, would laugh aloud with affection, together with all her friends. ॥8॥
3.26.9: Decked with armlets and ear-ornaments made of rudrākṣas, the monkey, through her training, would dance before her like a child. ॥9॥
3.26.10: The cock, with a rudrākṣa tied to its crest, skilled in dancing, danced daily along with the monkey, bringing benefit to those who watched. ॥10॥
3.26.11: Thus, performing this entertainment with great care and always devoted to Śiva, that courtesan became filled with great bliss. ॥11॥
3.26.12: O best of sages, while that courtesan practised devotion to Śiva, a long time passed for her in supreme happiness. ॥12॥
3.26.13: One day Śiva himself, becoming a merchant, came to her house to test her disposition, auspicious and observing a vow. ॥13॥
3.26.14: His forehead shone with the tripuṇḍra, he wore rudrākṣa ornaments, was accomplished, devoted to repeating Śiva's name, had matted locks and bore the garb of a Śaiva. ॥14॥
3.26.15: Bearing a mass of ashes and on his forearm an excellent bracelet studded with great jewels, he, intent on a supreme sport, looked splendid. ॥15॥
3.26.16: When he arrived, the beautiful courtesan honoured the merchant well with great joy and respectfully seated him in her own place. ॥16॥
3.26.17: Seeing the excellent, most charming bracelet on his forearm, she conceived a longing for it and, greatly amazed, spoke to him. ॥17॥
3.26.18: Mahānandā said: This bracelet made of great jewels on your hand instantly steals my heart; it is fit to adorn a celestial woman. ॥18॥
3.26.19: Nandīśvara said: Seeing her thus longing for the hand-ornament rich with nine gems, the noble-minded merchant spoke with a smile. ॥19॥
3.26.20: The merchant lord said: If your heart longs for this excellent divine jewel, then take it yourself with pleasure; but what price will you give for it? ॥20॥
3.26.21: The courtesan said: We courtesans are women who act as we please, not devoted wives; the conduct fitting our class is free liaison—there is no doubt. ॥21॥
3.26.22: Since this hand-ornament captivates my whole mind, I shall be your wife for three days and nights. ॥22॥
3.26.23: The merchant said: So be it, if your word is true, O beloved of heroes; I give you the jewelled bracelet—be my wife for three nights. ॥23॥
3.26.24: In this transaction the moon and the sun are witnesses; saying the word true three times, touch my heart, O dear one. ॥24॥
3.26.25: The courtesan said: Becoming your wife for three days and nights, O lord, I shall live in shared dharma with you—this is true, true, without doubt. ॥25॥
3.26.26: Nandīśvara said: Having said this three times and made the moon and sun witnesses, Mahānandā gladly touched his heart. ॥26॥
3.26.27: Then the merchant, having given her the jewelled bracelet, placed a jewelled liṅga in her hand and said this: ॥27॥
3.26.28: The merchant lord said: This jewelled Śiva-liṅga is dear to me as my life; you must guard it, beloved, and keep it hidden with care. ॥28॥
3.26.29: Nandīśvara said: Saying, so be it, she took the jewelled liṅga, placed it in the middle of the dance pavilion, and entered the house. ॥29॥
3.26.30: United at night with that merchant who behaved as a lover, she slept happily on a couch adorned with soft bedding. ॥30॥
3.26.31: Then at midnight, O sage, by the will of the merchant-lord, a sound suddenly arose inside the dance pavilion. ॥31॥
3.26.32: A great blazing fire, aided by a strong wind, suddenly enveloped that very dance pavilion, dear one. ॥32॥
3.26.33: As the pavilion burned, the courtesan rose up hastily in alarm and freed the monkey there from its tether. ॥33॥
3.26.34: Freed from its bonds, the monkey, together with the cock, ran far away in fear, shaking off many sparks. ॥34॥
3.26.35: Seeing that liṅga burnt along with the pillar and broken to pieces, the courtesan and the merchant fell into boundless grief. ॥35॥
3.26.36: Seeing the liṅga, equal to his own self, burnt, the merchant-lord then, to learn her inner disposition, resolved upon death. ॥36॥
3.26.37: Sitting down in extreme sorrow, the merchant—Maheśāna of manifold sports, who had taken a human body in play—spoke to the grieving woman. ॥37॥
3.26.38: The merchant lord said: Now that the Śiva-liṅga, dear to me as life, is shattered and burnt, I tell you truly, without doubt—I cannot bear to live. ॥38॥
3.26.39: Good lady, have a pyre built for me quickly by your best servants; fixing my mind on Śiva, I shall enter the fire. ॥39॥
3.26.40: Even if Brahmā, Indra, Viṣṇu and the rest were to come together and stop me, still at this very moment, good lady, I shall enter the fire and give up my life. ॥40॥
3.26.41: Nandīśvara said: Knowing him to be so firmly resolved, she, deeply grieved, had her servants build a pyre outside her house. ॥41॥
3.26.42: Then that vaiśya, who was Śiva alone, steadfast, full of playful delight and wishing for her union with him, circumambulated the blazing fire and entered it while the people looked on. ॥42॥
3.26.43: Seeing his fate, that courtesan Mahānandā, a young woman, was utterly astonished and fell into remorse, O best of sages. ॥43॥
3.26.44: Then that grieving courtesan, remembering the spotless dharma, looked at all her kinsfolk and spoke piteous words. ॥44॥
3.26.45: Mahānandā said: When I took the jewelled bracelet, I made a true promise: for three days I am the acknowledged wife of this vaiśya. ॥45॥
3.26.46: Because of a deed done by me, this vaiśya, a keeper of Śiva's vow, has died. Therefore I will enter the fire together with him. ॥46॥
3.26.47: Truth-speaking teachers have said: She is one who follows her own dharma. When I do this out of love, let truth not perish in me. ॥47॥
3.26.48: The highest dharma rests on truth; by truth comes the supreme goal; by truth come heaven and liberation; on truth everything is established. ॥48॥
3.26.49: Nandīśvara said: Thus firmly resolved, though her kinsmen tried to stop her, the woman, fearing the breaking of truth, set her mind on giving up her life. ॥49॥
3.26.50: Having given all her possessions to eminent brāhmaṇas and meditated on Sadāśiva, she circled that fire three times and turned to enter it. ॥50॥
3.26.51: As she was falling into the blazing fire, her mind offered at his feet, Śiva, the Self of the universe, appeared and stopped her. ॥51॥
3.26.52: Beholding him, the God of all gods, three-eyed, crowned with the crescent moon, shining like millions of moons, suns and fires, she stood just as she was, as if stunned, as if afraid. ॥52॥
3.26.53: She was overwhelmed, terrified, trembling, stupefied, with tears streaming; comforting her and taking her hands, he spoke these words. ॥53॥
3.26.54: Śiva said: To test your truthfulness, your dharma, your steadfastness and your unwavering devotion to me, I came to you having become a vaiśya. ॥54॥
3.26.55: By my māyā I kindled the fire and your dancing hall was burnt; having made the jewelled liṅga burn, I entered the fire. ॥55॥
3.26.56: You, remembering truth, entered the fire along with me; therefore I shall grant you enjoyments hard even for the gods to attain. ॥56॥
3.26.57: Whatever you desire, O fair-hipped one, that indeed I give you. I am pleased by your devotion; there is nothing that cannot be given to you. ॥57॥
3.26.58: Nandīśvara said: When Śaṅkara, Gaurī's lord, loving to his devotees, had spoken thus, that courtesan Mahānandā replied to Śaṅkara. ॥58॥
3.26.59: The courtesan said: I have no desire for enjoyments on earth, in heaven or in the netherworld. I wish for nothing other than the touch of your lotus feet. ॥59॥
3.26.60: My servants and maidservants, and all my other kinsfolk, are all intent on seeing you and have entrusted their lives to you. ॥60॥
3.26.61: Lead all of them together with me to your own supreme abode and free us from the dreadful fear of rebirth. Salutations to you. ॥61॥
3.26.62: Nandīśvara said: Then Maheśvara, welcoming her words, led all of them together with her to his own supreme abode. ॥62॥
3.26.63: I have described to you the supreme Vaiśyanātha incarnation, which brought happiness to Mahānandā and ever grants bliss to devotees. ॥63॥
3.26.64: This story of Śiva's incarnation as the lord of the vaiśyas is supreme, purifying, divine and wonderful; it quickly bestows everything on the good, and brought great happiness to Mahānandā. ॥64॥
3.26.65: Whoever listens to this with devotion, or attentively recites it to others, does not fall from his own dharma and attains the supreme goal in the next world. ॥65॥
3.26.iti: Thus ends the twenty-sixth adhyāya, named The incarnation of Śiva called Vaiśyanātha, in the third saṃhitā, the Śatarudra-saṃhitā, of the Śrī Śivamahāpurāṇa. ॥26॥
3.27.1: Nandīśvara said: Listen, dear one: I shall describe the Dvijeśvara incarnation of Śiva, the Supreme Self, an incarnation accompanied by Śivā, which gives happiness to the good. ॥1॥
3.27.2: Bhadrāyu, the best of kings, who was described earlier, dear one, on whom Śiva bestowed grace in the form of Ṛṣabha — ॥2॥
3.27.3: to test his righteousness, he manifested again in the form of Dvijeśvara; that very story I now tell. ॥3॥
3.27.4: By the power of Ṛṣabha, the mighty Bhadrāyu, having conquered his enemies in battle, obtained the throne, dear one. ॥4॥
3.27.5: The daughter of Candrāṅgada, the fair child born of Sīmantinī, the very chaste Kīrtimālinī, became his wife, O brahmin. ॥5॥
3.27.6: Once, O sage, in springtime, that Bhadrāyu entered a dense forest with his beloved for recreation. ॥6॥
3.27.7: Then in that lovely forest the king sported together with his beloved, who protected those who came for refuge. ॥7॥
3.27.8: Then the Supreme Lord Śaṅkara, wishing to see the firmness of his righteousness, performed a sport right there together with Śivā. ॥8॥
3.27.9: Śivā and Śiva both, becoming a brahmin couple in that forest and creating an illusory tiger, appeared by their own play. ॥9॥
3.27.10: Then, not far from him, the two were running, overcome with fear, pursued by the tiger, weeping. ॥10॥
3.27.11: Then, dear one, King Bhadrāyu, the bull among kṣatriyas and refuge of all, saw the two stricken ones crying out. ॥11॥
3.27.12: Then, O tiger among sages, that brahmin couple of his own māyā, overcome with fear, spoke to the great king Bhadrāyu. ॥12॥
3.27.13: The brahmin couple said: Protect, protect us both, O great king, best of knowers of dharma. This tiger is coming to devour us, O great lord. ॥13॥
3.27.14: This savage beast, like Death itself, terrifying to all living beings — before it reaches and eats us, protect us, O knower of dharma. ॥14॥
3.27.15: Nandīśvara said: Hearing their cry thus, the lord of kings, the great hero, very quickly took up his bow — ॥15॥
3.27.16: at that moment the tiger, full of illusion, rushing up, seized the wife of that excellent brahmin in their midst. ॥16॥
3.27.17: As she wailed loudly—O lord, lord, O beloved, alas Śambhu! Alas, Guru of the world!—the dreadful tiger seized her in its jaws. ॥17॥
3.27.18: Meanwhile the king struck the tiger with sharp arrows, but it was not pained by them in the least, like a great mountain by rains. ॥18॥
3.27.19: That mighty tiger, only lightly hurt by the king, forcibly dragged the woman and swiftly went away. ॥19॥
3.27.20: Seeing his wife carried off by the tiger, the brahmin, greatly astonished, following the way of the world, wept bitterly again and again. ॥20॥
3.27.21: Having wept for a long time, that brahmin — the Lord disguised by māyā, the remover of pride — spoke to King Bhadrāyu. ॥21॥
3.27.22: The great brahmin said: O king, where are your great weapons? Where is your great protecting bow? Where is your strength equal to twelve thousand great elephants? ॥22॥
3.27.23: What use is your sword, your conch? What use your knowledge of mantra-weapons? What use the power of great weapons, what use your abundant might? ॥23॥
3.27.24: All that, and whatever else resides in you, has become fruitless, since you are unable to prevent the killing of forest-dwellers. ॥24॥
3.27.25: This is the highest duty of a kṣatriya: protection from injury. When that duty befitting your lineage is lost, what use is your life? ॥25॥
3.27.26: Kings who know dharma protect the afflicted who come for refuge, with their lives and wealth; without that they are like the dead. ॥26॥
3.27.27: For those who fail to protect the afflicted, death is better than life; for the wealthy who do not give, mendicancy is better than householder life. ॥27॥
3.27.28: The wise consider eating poison better, entering fire better, than failing to protect the wretched, the helpless and the distressed. ॥28॥
3.27.29: Nandīśvara said: Hearing his lament thus and the censure of his own valour, the king, out of grief, reflected within himself thus: ॥29॥
3.27.30: Alas! Today my manliness is lost through reversal of fate; today my fame too is lost, and a grievous sin has befallen me. ॥30॥
3.27.31: The duty befitting my lineage is lost for me, unfortunate and foolish; surely my prosperity, kingdom and life will come to ruin. ॥31॥
3.27.32: Today I shall free this brahmin, who has lost his wife and is tormented by grief, from his sorrow, even by giving up my dearest life. ॥32॥
3.27.33: Having thus resolved in his mind, Bhadrāyu, the best of kings, fell at his feet and spoke, consoling him. ॥33॥
3.27.34: Bhadrāyu said: Showing mercy to me, a mere kṣatriya bereft of vigour, O brahmin, abandon your grief, O most wise one; today I shall give you whatever you desire. ॥34॥
3.27.35: This kingdom, this queen, and this body of mine — all this is at your disposal. What boon do you desire? ॥35॥
3.27.36: The brahmin said: What use is a mirror to a blind man, or houses to one who lives on alms? What use is a book to a fool, what use wealth to one without a wife? ॥36॥
3.27.37: Therefore I, whose wife is taken away and who have never enjoyed pleasures, desire this chief queen of yours: let her be given to me. ॥37॥
3.27.38: Bhadrāyu said: I am a giver of wealth to the ends of the earth, of the kingdom, of elephants and horses, of my own body, of anything at all — but never of a wife. ॥38॥
3.27.39: The sin incurred by enjoying another's wife cannot be washed away even by hundreds of expiations. ॥39॥
3.27.40: The brahmin said: Let alone the dreadful slaying of a brahmin, or even drinking liquor — I shall destroy such sins by austerity; how much more the sin of adultery. ॥40॥
3.27.41: Therefore give me this wife of yours; I have no other desire. By failing to protect those stricken with fear, you will surely go to hell. ॥41॥
3.27.42: Nandīśvara said: Frightened by the brahmin's words, the king reflected: Failing to protect a suppliant is a great sin; giving away my wife is better than that. ॥42॥
3.27.43: So, having given my wife to this foremost brahmin and being freed from sin, I shall at once enter the fire, and my fame will become known. ॥43॥
3.27.44: Having resolved thus in his mind, he kindled a blazing fire, summoned that brahmin, and made the gift of his wife with the pouring of water. ॥44॥
3.27.45: Having bathed himself and become pure, bowing to the lords of the gods, he circumambulated that fire three times and, with concentrated mind, meditated on Śiva. ॥45॥
3.27.46: Then, as he was about to fall into the fire, his mind fixed on the Lord's feet, the Lord of the universe, who had appeared as the lord of brahmins, stopped him. ॥46॥
3.27.47: That Lord, five-faced, three-eyed, bearer of the Pināka bow, with the crescent moon as his crest-ornament, with a mass of long, tawny, radiant matted locks, with the splendour of ten million midday suns— ॥47॥
3.27.48: White as a lotus stalk, clad in an elephant hide, the crown of his head sprinkled by the waves of the Gaṅgā, his neck adorned with garlands of serpent-kings, resplendent with crown, girdle, armlets and bracelets— ॥48॥
3.27.49: —holding in his hands trident, sword, skull-staff, axe, shield, deer, the gesture of fearlessness, and the Pināka bow, mounted on the bull, adorned with a dark-blue throat—that Lord manifested before him, the king beheld. ॥49॥
3.27.50: Then showers of heavenly flowers quickly fell from the sky; divine instruments sounded, and goddesses danced and sang. ॥50॥
3.27.51: There came, being praised, Hari and Brahmā, and likewise the gods, Indra and the others, the sages headed by Nārada, and others too. ॥51॥
3.27.52: Then a great festival took place there, increasing devotion, while the king looked on, his joined palms bowed in devotion. ॥52॥
3.27.53: His heart expanding with the bliss of that vision, his body bathed in streaming tears, his hair standing on end, with faltering syllables and folded palms, he praised the Lord with words. ॥53॥
3.27.54: Then the blessed Supreme Lord, the treasure of compassion, thus praised by the king, being pleased, spoke to him, together with Pārvatī. ॥54॥
3.27.55: O king, I am fully pleased with your devotion, and even more by your righteousness. Ask a boon, for yourself together with your wife; I shall grant it, no doubt. ॥55॥
3.27.56: To test your disposition I came, having become a brahmin. She who was seized by the tiger is indeed the Goddess Śivā herself. ॥56॥
3.27.57: The tiger whose body was unharmed by your arrows was illusory. Wishing to see your steadfastness, I asked for your wife. ॥57॥
3.27.58: Nandīśvara said: Having heard these words of the Lord, King Bhadrāyu, bowing again and praising the Master, humbly spoke. ॥58॥
3.27.59: Bhadrāyu said: This alone is the boon, O Lord: that you, the Supreme Lord, have become visible to me, scorched as I am by the heat of worldly existence. ॥59॥
3.27.60: Yet since you grant a boon by your own grace, O Lord, O Master, I choose from you, the best of boon-givers, a supreme boon. ॥60॥
3.27.61: My father Vajrabāhu with his wife, O Maheśvara, and I with my wife, O Lord, may we be ever servants of your feet. ॥61॥
3.27.62: The merchant named Padmākara and his son called Sunaya—all these, O Maheśāna, make them always your attendants by your side. ॥62॥
3.27.63: Nandīśvara said: Then the queen, his wife Kīrtimālinī, enraptured, having propitiated Giriśa with devotion, asked for an excellent boon. ॥63॥
3.27.64: The queen said: Candrāṅgada is my father and Sīmantinī my mother; for the two of them, O Mahādeva, I joyfully ask nearness to you by your side. ॥64॥
3.27.65: Nandīśvara said: Saying, so be it, the Lord of Gaurī, pleased and loving to his devotees, granted the two of them the boons they desired and vanished in an instant. ॥65॥
3.27.66: Bhadrāyu too, having received the grace of the Trident-bearer with great joy, enjoyed many pleasures together with Kīrtimālinī. ॥66॥
3.27.67: Having ruled the kingdom for ten thousand years with unimpeded valour, he handed the kingdom over to his son and went to Śiva's presence. ॥67॥
3.27.68: Candrāṅgada too, the great king, and that queen Sīmantinī, having worshipped Giriśa with devotion, went to the abode of Śambhu. ॥68॥
3.27.69: Thus I have described to you, O lord, the supreme Dvijeśvara incarnation of Maheśvara, which bestowed supreme bliss on Bhadrāyu. ॥69॥
3.27.70: This supreme, purifying and most wondrous account of Śiva's incarnation named Dvijeśa, of pure fame—one who hears or recites it attains Śambhu's abode. ॥70॥
3.27.71: Whoever, with concentrated mind, listens to this daily or causes it to be heard does not fall from his own dharma, and attains the highest goal in the next world. ॥71॥
3.27.iti: Thus ends the twenty-seventh adhyāya, named The incarnation of Śiva called Dvijeśa, in the third saṃhitā, the Śatarudra-saṃhitā, of the Śrī Śivamahāpurāṇa. ॥27॥
3.28.1: Nandīśvara said: Listen, O wise one; I shall describe the incarnation of Śiva, the Supreme Self, which is supreme bliss and is called Yatinātha, O sage. ॥1॥
3.28.2: On the mountain called Arbudācala, near it, there lived Āhuka, born of the Bhilla race, O lord of sages. ॥2॥
3.28.3: His wife, named Āhukā, was indeed firm in her vows. Both of them were great Śaivas, worshippers of Śiva. ॥3॥
3.28.4: Once the Bhilla, ever devoted to Śiva, went very far away to get food for himself and his wife, O sage. ॥4॥
3.28.5: Meanwhile Śaṅkara, assuming the body of an ascetic, came in the evening to the Bhilla's house there in order to test him. ॥5॥
3.28.6: At that moment the master of the house came there, and the wise man worshipped the lord of ascetics with love. ॥6॥
3.28.7: To test his disposition, that Śaṅkara in ascetic form, the performer of great sport, as if afraid, spoke affectionately in a plaintive voice. ॥7॥
3.28.8: The lord of ascetics said: Give me a place to stay today; at dawn I shall certainly go, O Bhilla. May there be welfare for you always. ॥8॥
3.28.9: The Bhilla said: What you have said is right, master; but listen to my word to you. My place is very small; how can there be lodging for you? ॥9॥
3.28.10: Nandīśvara said: Thus addressed by him, the ascetic made up his mind to leave. Just then the Bhilla woman, having reflected, spoke these words to her husband. ॥10॥
3.28.11: The Bhilla woman said: Husband, give the ascetic a place; do not turn the guest away. Consider the duty of a householder; otherwise there will be ruin of dharma. ॥11॥
3.28.12: You stay comfortably inside the house with the ascetic; I shall stay outside, with the large weapons too. ॥12॥
3.28.13: Nandīśvara said: Hearing those auspicious, righteous words of his wife, the Bhilla woman, the Bhilla reflected in his mind: ॥13॥
3.28.14: Having put my wife outside, how can I stay in the house? Yet the ascetic's going elsewhere would bring unrighteousness upon me. ॥14॥
3.28.15: Neither of the two is at all proper for a householder. Whatever is to be will surely be; I must stay outside the house. ॥15॥
3.28.16: Then, having insisted thus and gladly placed the two inside the house, and having arranged his weapons, the Bhilla stayed outside the house. ॥16॥
3.28.17: In the night cruel, violent beasts attacked him, and he too made a great effort then, as far as his strength allowed. ॥17॥
3.28.18: Though striving thus and though strong, the Bhilla was forcibly devoured by the beasts, impelled by his past karma (prārabdha). ॥18॥
3.28.19: Rising at dawn, the ascetic, seeing that forest-dwelling Bhilla devoured by the beasts, became exceedingly grieved. ॥19॥
3.28.20: Seeing the ascetic grieved, the Bhilla woman, though grieving herself, suppressed her own sorrow through fortitude and spoke these words. ॥20॥
3.28.21: The Bhilla woman said: Why do you grieve? Good has now come about, O ascetic. He is blessed and has fulfilled his purpose, since such a death has befallen him. ॥21॥
3.28.22: And I shall follow him, becoming ashes in the fire, O ascetic. Have a pyre built gladly; this is the eternal dharma of women. ॥22॥
3.28.23: Hearing her words and thinking them beneficial, the ascetic himself built the pyre, and she entered it in accordance with her own dharma. ॥23॥
3.28.24: At that moment Śiva manifested in person before her. Hara, praising her lovingly, said: Blessed one, blessed one! ॥24॥
3.28.25: Hara said: Ask for a boon; I am pleased with your conduct, O sinless one. There is nothing that cannot be given to you; I am especially subject to you. ॥25॥
3.28.26: Nandīśvara said: Hearing Śambhu's words, which bestow supreme bliss, she attained great joy and lost all awareness of anything else. ॥26॥
3.28.27: Observing her state, Hara became very pleased, and the lord Śambhu again said to her: Ask for a boon. ॥27॥
3.28.28: Śiva said: This ascetic, who is my own form, will become a swan; in your next birth he will lovingly bring about the union of you two. ॥28॥
3.28.29: And the Bhilla will be the great son of Vīrasena, named Nala, in the excellent city of Niṣadha; there is no doubt. ॥29॥
3.28.30: You, O sinless one, will be the daughter of King Bhīma in the city of Vidarbha, renowned as Damayantī and endowed with virtues. ॥30॥
3.28.31: You two, having been united and having enjoyed abundant royal pleasures, will surely attain liberation, which is hard to attain even for the foremost yogins. ॥31॥
3.28.32: Nandīśvara said: Having said this, Śambhu himself then took the form of a liṅga. Because he did not swerve from dharma, he is remembered as Acaleśa. ॥32॥
3.28.33: That Bhilla Āhuka became the son of Vīrasena in the city of Niṣadha, dear one, the great king named Nala. ॥33॥
3.28.34: That great Bhilla woman Āhukā became the daughter of King Bhīma in the city of Vidarbha, famed as Damayantī. ॥34॥
3.28.35: And Śiva, who was called Yatinātha, became the swan and brought about the marriage of Damayantī with Nala. ॥35॥
3.28.36: Owing to the great merit of their former hospitality, Lord Śaṅkara, assuming the form of a swan, gave happiness to the two. ॥36॥
3.28.37: Śiva, the swan incarnation, skilled in various kinds of talk, bestowed supreme bliss on Damayantī and Nala. ॥37॥
3.28.38: This account of Śiva's incarnation of pure fame, named Yatīśa, and also of the one called Haṃsa, is supreme, purifying, most wonderful, and grants liberation. ॥38॥
3.28.39: Whoever hears or recites to others this auspicious account of the incarnations called Yatīśa and Brahmahaṃsa attains the supreme goal. ॥39॥
3.28.40: This faultless narrative grants the fruit of all desires; it leads to heaven, brings fame and long life, increases devotion, and is excellent. ॥40॥
3.28.41: Having heard this account of Śambhu in his two forms as the ascetic (yati) and the swan (haṃsa), one enjoys every happiness here in this world and at the end goes to Śiva's city. ॥41॥
3.28.iti: Thus ends the twenty-eighth adhyāya, named The deeds of the incarnations of Śiva called Yatinātha and Brahmahaṃsa, in the third saṃhitā, the Śatarudra-saṃhitā, of the Śrī Śivamahāpurāṇa. ॥28॥
3.29.1: Nandīśvara said: O Sanatkumāra, hear of Śambhu's supreme and excellent incarnation called Kṛṣṇadarśana, which granted knowledge to Nabhaga. ॥1॥
3.29.2: There were the sons of Śrāddhadeva, headed by Ikṣvāku; among them Nabhaga was the ninth, and Nābhāga is remembered as his son. ॥2॥
3.29.3: His son was Ambarīṣa; he became a devotee of Viṣṇu, upon whom Durvāsas became pleased because of his devotion to the brahmins. ॥3॥
3.29.4: Hear, O sage, the story of Nabhaga, who is declared to be Ambarīṣa's grandfather, to whom Śiva gave knowledge. ॥4॥
3.29.5: Nabhaga, the son of Manu, very intelligent and self-controlled, lived for a long time in the teacher's house for the sake of study. ॥5॥
3.29.6: At this time those sons headed by Ikṣvāku, without allotting any share to him, took their own shares in order. ॥6॥
3.29.7: Each taking his own share, those fortunate and wise ones enjoyed the excellent kingdom without distress, by their father's command. ॥7॥
3.29.8: Afterwards Nabhaga, the celibate student, having studied in order all the Vedas with their aṅgas and upāṅgas, came there from the teacher's place. ॥8॥
3.29.9: Seeing all his brothers had divided the property, Nabhaga, seeking his inheritance, spoke affectionately to them, headed by Ikṣvāku, O sage. ॥9॥
3.29.10: Nabhaga said: Brothers, leaving my inheritance unallotted, as things stood, you have all divided the property with great pleasure; give a share to me too, who have come for my own inheritance. ॥10॥
3.29.11: The brothers said: At that time you were forgotten by us; now we allot your father as your share. Take him, without doubt. ॥11॥
3.29.12: Hearing his brothers' words, Nabhaga, greatly astonished, then came near his father and spoke to him. ॥12॥
3.29.13: Nabhaga said: O father, all my brothers divided the property, leaving me out, while I had gone as a celibate student to the teacher's house for study. ॥13॥
3.29.14: Then, when I came and respectfully asked them to give me my inheritance, they named you as my share; for that reason I have come. ॥14॥
3.29.15: Nandīśvara said: Hearing his words, his father Śrāddhadeva, astonished, consoled him, who was devoted to truth and dharma, and spoke to him, O sage. ॥15॥
3.29.16: Manu said: Do not heed what they said, dear son, for it is deceitful. I am by no means a fine inheritance, a means of enjoyment. ॥16॥
3.29.17: Even so, I have been given by those deceivers as your inheritance. I will tell you a means of livelihood; listen truly. ॥17॥
3.29.18: The wise Āṅgirasa brahmins are performing a sattra today; in that rite they become confused on every sixth day. ॥18॥
3.29.19: Go there, Nabhaga, O great poet, and recite to them the two Vaiśvadeva hymns; then that sattra will become pure. ॥19॥
3.29.20: When that rite is completed, those brahmins, going to heaven, will be pleased and give you the wealth remaining from their sattra. ॥20॥
3.29.21: Nandīśvara said: Hearing his father's words, Nabhaga, steadfast in truth, went with great joy to where that excellent sattra was. ॥21॥
3.29.22: Then, O sage, in the rite of that day in the sattra, the wise son of Manu clearly recited the two Vaiśvadeva hymns. ॥22॥
3.29.23: When the rite was completed, those Āṅgirasa brahmins gave him each his own remainder of the sattra and went to heaven. ॥23॥
3.29.24: Then, knowing that he was about to accept that remainder of the excellent sattra, Giriśa, the bestower of good favour, at once appeared. ॥24॥
3.29.25: He appeared as a glorious man, beautiful in every limb, dark in appearance (Kṛṣṇadarśana), to test his disposition, to give him a share, and that supreme knowledge. ॥25॥
3.29.26: Then that Śaṅkara, Śambhu, the Lord who tests, approached from the north and spoke to Nabhaga, the son of Manu. ॥26॥
3.29.27: Īśvara said: Who are you, man, taking this wealth of mine left at the sacrificial site? By whom were you sent? Tell all of it truly before me. ॥27॥
3.29.28: Nandīśvara said: Hearing those words, dear one, Nabhaga, the wise son of Manu, humbly replied to the dark-looking man. ॥28॥
3.29.29: Nabhaga said: This wealth from the sacrifice was surely given to me by the sages. How can you, the dark-looking one, stop me as I take it? ॥29॥
3.29.30: Nandīśvara said: Hearing these truthful words spoken by Nabhaga, the dark-looking man, pleased at heart, replied. ॥30॥
3.29.31: The dark-looking man said: In this dispute between us, dear boy, your father is the authority. Go and ask him; he will truthfully state what is right. ॥31॥
3.29.32: Nandīśvara said: Hearing his words, Nabhaga, the wise son of Manu, went gladly to his father and asked him about what had been said, O sage. ॥32॥
3.29.33: Hearing what his son said, Manu Śrāddhadeva remembered Śiva's lotus feet, regained his recollection, and spoke to him. ॥33॥
3.29.34: Manu said: O son, hear my words: that man is the god Śiva. Everything belongs to him alone, especially what is obtained from a sacrifice. ॥34॥
3.29.35: What remains of a sacrifice is declared to be Rudra's share — this teaching of the wise arose somewhere by his will. ॥35॥
3.29.36: That god, the Lord, is entitled to everything, no doubt — how much more the remnant of the sacrifice. Others receive only by the will of that all-pervading one. ॥36॥
3.29.37: The Lord has come in that form to show you grace. Go there, Nabhaga, and sincerely make him pleased. ॥37॥
3.29.38: Beg forgiveness for your offence, bow deeply and offer praise. He alone is the Lord, master of all, lord of sacrifice, ruler of everything. ॥38॥
3.29.39: The gods headed by Viṣṇu and Brahmā, the Siddhas, and all the sages too, dear son, are capable in every act only by his grace. ॥39॥
3.29.40: Why say more, best of sons? Go there quickly, without delay, and in every way propitiate Mahādeva, the Lord of all. ॥40॥
3.29.41: Nandīśvara said: Having said this, Manu Śrāddhadeva quickly sent his son to Śambhu; and he too, approaching him, ॥41॥
3.29.42: Nabhaga, having quickly bowed, with joined palms and bowed head, the greatly wise one, very serene in mind, spoke with humility: ॥42॥
3.29.43: Nabhaga said: O Lord, everything that exists in the three worlds is indeed yours—so my father has surely said; how much more, then, what is left over from the sacrifice. ॥43॥
3.29.44: O Lord, the words I spoke out of ignorance were said in error. Please forgive my offence; I propitiate you with bowed head. ॥44॥
3.29.45: Having said this, Nabhaga, very humble in mind, with joined palms and bowing, praised that Great Lord Kṛṣṇadarśana. ॥45॥
3.29.46: Śrāddhadeva too, pure-souled and wise, bowing with joined palms, praised that Lord after saluting him, seeking forgiveness for his own offence. ॥46॥
3.29.47: Meanwhile, the gods headed by Viṣṇu and Brahmā, those headed by Vāsava (Indra), the Siddhas and the sages also assembled there. ॥47॥
3.29.48: Holding a great festival, all of them with palms well joined, bowing, praised him with devotion, each separately after prostrating deeply. ॥48॥
3.29.49: Then Rudra Kṛṣṇadarśana, pleased at heart, looking upon them with a compassionate glance, spoke lovingly and with a smile to Nabhaga. ॥49॥
3.29.50: The dark-looking man said: The righteous words your father spoke are indeed just so; and what you said was also true. You are virtuous; there is no doubt in this. ॥50॥
3.29.51: Therefore I am entirely well pleased with your good conduct; out of grace I give you knowledge, the eternal Brahman. ॥51॥
3.29.52: Become a great knower, together with the brahmins. O Nabhaga, quickly take all this wealth, given by me out of grace, now. ॥52॥
3.29.53: Enjoy here every happiness, untroubled, O great-minded one; and by my grace you, together with the brahmins, shall attain a good destiny. ॥53॥
3.29.54: Nandīśvara said: Having said this, dear one, the blessed Rudra Hara, lover of truth, vanished right there while they all looked on. ॥54॥
3.29.55: Viṣṇu, Brahmā, and all the gods and others, O best of sages, went happily each to his own abode, after joyfully bowing to that direction. ॥55॥
3.29.56: Śrāddhadeva too, with his son, went joyfully to his own place; having enjoyed abundant pleasures, at the end he went to Śiva's city. ॥56॥
3.29.57: Thus, O brahmin, I have narrated to you the incarnation of Śiva named Kṛṣṇadarśana, the giver of joy to Nabhaga. ॥57॥
3.29.58: This sinless narrative grants enjoyment and liberation to the good, and bestows the fruit of all desires on those who read or hear it. ॥58॥
3.29.59: The wise person who remembers this story morning and evening becomes a poet and knower of mantras, and at the end attains the supreme goal. ॥59॥
3.29.iti: Thus ends the twenty-ninth adhyāya, named The incarnation of Śiva called Kṛṣṇadarśana, in the dialogue of Nandīśvara and Sanatkumāra, in the third saṃhitā, the Śatarudra-saṃhitā, of the Śrī Śivamahāpurāṇa. ॥29॥
3.30.1: Nandīśvara said: O son of Brahmā, now listen to the incarnation of the Supreme Lord called Avadhūteśvara, which took away Śakra's pride. ॥1॥
3.30.2: Long ago, O sage, Śakra, together with his preceptor and accompanied by all the gods, went to Kailāsa to have the sight (darśana) of the Lord. ॥2॥
3.30.3: Then Śaṅkara, knowing of the coming of the two, the preceptor and Indra, and wishing to test the disposition of those two whose minds were devoted to seeing him, ॥3॥
3.30.4: the Lord, performer of many sports (līlā), took the form of an Avadhūta—naked, very terrifying, with a radiance like blazing fire. ॥4॥
3.30.5: Śambhu, the true refuge, in that Avadhūta form, stood blocking the path, with a hanging cloth, his form shining. ॥5॥
3.30.6: Then the two, the preceptor and Śakra, going toward Śiva's presence, saw in the middle of the path a terrifying man of wondrous form. ॥6॥
3.30.7: Then, O sage, Śakra, arrogant because of his authority, not recognising that man standing in his path as Śaṅkara, questioned him. ॥7॥
3.30.8: Śakra said: Who are you, naked Avadhūta? Where have you come from? What is your well-known name? Tell me truly, without delay. ॥8॥
3.30.9: Is Śambhu staying in his own abode, or has he now gone elsewhere? For I am going, with my preceptor and the gods, to see him. ॥9॥
3.30.10: Nandīśvara said: Questioned thus by Śakra, that man said nothing—he was Śaṅkara, the Lord, destroyer of pride, who had assumed a body in sport. ॥10॥
3.30.11: Śakra asked him again; that naked one did not speak—Śambhu, whose ways are unknown, the maker of great wonders. ॥11॥
3.30.12: Again Purandara, the overlord of the three worlds, the self-ruling king, asked; but that great yogin, the performer of great sport, remained silent. ॥12॥
3.30.13: Thus questioned again and again by Śakra, that naked Lord said nothing, wishing to destroy Śakra's arrogance. ॥13॥
3.30.14: Then the lord of the gods, proud of his sovereignty over the three worlds, became angry, and rebuking that bearer of matted locks, spoke these words out of anger. ॥14॥
3.30.15: Indra said: Fool, though being asked, you have given no answer. Therefore I will strike you with my thunderbolt. Who is there to protect you, wicked-minded one? ॥15॥
3.30.16: Having said this, the wielder of the thunderbolt, glaring at him in anger, raised his thunderbolt to slay that naked one. ॥16॥
3.30.17: Seeing Śakra with the thunderbolt in his hand, Sadāśiva Śaṅkara swiftly paralysed the fall of his thunderbolt. ॥17॥
3.30.18: Then that man, enraged, with dreadful eyes, terrifying, at once blazed up with his splendour as if burning everything. ॥18॥
3.30.19: The lord of Śacī, his might checked like a serpent held by a spell, burned inwardly with rage arising from the paralysis of his arm. ॥19॥
3.30.20: But Bṛhaspati, seeing that man blazing with his own splendour, recognised him in his mind and quickly bowed to Hara. ॥20॥
3.30.21: Then the noble-minded preceptor, with joined palms, bowing again on the ground like a staff, praised the Lord with devotion. ॥21॥
3.30.22: The guru said: O God of gods, Mahādeva, loving to those who seek refuge, be gracious, O lord of Gaurī, O lord of all; salutation to you. ॥22॥
3.30.23: All, even Brahmā, Viṣṇu and the others, deluded by your māyā, do not know you in truth; they know you only through your grace. ॥23॥
3.30.24: Nandīśvara said: Having thus praised Lord Śaṅkara, Bṛhaspati then made Purandara fall at the feet of that Lord. ॥24॥
3.30.25: Then, dear one, Bṛhaspati, the preceptor of the gods, noble-minded and wise, with joined palms, bowed in humility, said this: ॥25॥
3.30.26: Bṛhaspati said: O protector of the wretched, Mahādeva, lift up this one bowed at your feet, and me as well; therefore, do not show anger—show kindness. ॥26॥
3.30.27: Be pleased, Mahādeva, protect Indra who has sought refuge. This fire born from your forehead-eye is coming forth. ॥27॥
3.30.28: Nandīśvara said: Hearing these words of the preceptor, the Lord in the Avadhūta form, the ocean of compassion, the bestower of true protection, spoke, laughing. ॥28॥
3.30.29: The avadhūta said: How can I hold back the fiery energy that has come out of my eye in anger? How indeed does a snake put back on the slough it has cast off? ॥29॥
3.30.30: Nandīśvara said: Hearing these words of Śaṅkara, Bṛhaspati, his mind troubled with fear, spoke again with joined palms. ॥30॥
3.30.31: Bṛhaspati said: O God, O Lord, devotees are always to be shown compassion. O Śaṅkara, make true your own name Bhaktavatsala (loving to devotees). ॥31॥
3.30.32: O lord of gods, you should cast your extremely fierce energy elsewhere. Rescuer of all devotees, rescue Purandara. ॥32॥
3.30.33: Nandīśvara said: Thus addressed by the preceptor, Rudra, who bears the name Bhaktavatsala, the remover of the distress of those who bow, replied, pleased at heart, to the priest of the gods. ॥33॥
3.30.34: Rudra said: I am pleased with you, O preceptor of the gods; I grant you an excellent boon. Because you have given life to Indra, become renowned as Jīva. ॥34॥
3.30.35: This fire that has arisen from my forehead-eye, unbearable to the gods, I shall cast far away, so that it may not harm Indra. ॥35॥
3.30.36: Nandīśvara said: Having said this, he took in his hand that wondrous fire of his own energy, born from his forehead-eye, and hurled it into the salt ocean. ॥36॥
3.30.37: Then that energy of Śiva, born from his forehead-eye, cast into the salt ocean, immediately became a boy. ॥37॥
3.30.38: He became the lord of the asuras named Jalandhara, son of the Ocean. The Lord Maheśāna slew him at the request of the gods. ॥38॥
3.30.39: Having thus performed this noble deed in the form of the Avadhūta, Śaṅkara, the benefactor of the worlds, then vanished. ॥39॥
3.30.40: All the gods became happy and wholly free from fear; the preceptor and Śakra, released from fear, attained supreme happiness. ॥40॥
3.30.41: Having obtained the sight of him for whose sake they had set out, the two, Guru Bṛhaspati and Śakra Indra, their purpose fulfilled, went joyfully to their own abodes. ॥41॥
3.30.42: I have narrated to you the incarnation of the Supreme Lord named Avadhūteśvara, which bestows supreme bliss and metes out punishment to the wicked. ॥42॥
3.30.43: This narrative is sinless, conferring fame and heaven, divine, bestowing enjoyment and liberation, and granting the fruit of all desires. ॥43॥
3.30.44: Whoever listens to this daily, or with a composed mind causes it to be heard, enjoys every happiness here and at the end attains the state of Śiva. ॥44॥
3.30.iti: Thus ends the thirtieth adhyāya, named The deeds of the incarnation of Śiva called Avadhūteśvara, in the dialogue of Nandīśvara and Sanatkumāra, in the third saṃhitā, the Śatarudra-saṃhitā, of the Śrī Śivamahāpurāṇa. ॥30॥
3.31.1: Nandīśvara said: Now, O best of sages, I shall tell you of an incarnation of Śambhu; listen, O brahmin. Out of compassion for his devotee, it dispelled a woman's doubt. ॥1॥
3.31.2: In the land of Vidarbha there was a king named Satyaratha. He was righteous at heart, devoted to truth, and dear to the great devotees of Śiva. ॥2॥
3.31.3: O sage, while that king ruled the earth with good dharma, a long time passed happily for him through his practice of Śiva's dharma. ॥3॥
3.31.4: Then once a great battle took place between that king and the Śālvas, who besieged his city with many troops, arrogant in their strength. ॥4॥
3.31.5: That king of Vidarbha fought a fierce battle with them; his great army was destroyed, and by the working of fate he was slain by the Śālvas. ॥5॥
3.31.6: When that king was killed in battle by the Śālvas, the surviving soldiers, overwhelmed with fear, fled along with the ministers. ॥6॥
3.31.7: Then, O sage, his chief queen, who was pregnant, escaped with great effort at night from her own city, which was besieged by the enemies. ॥7॥
3.31.8: Having left, that queen, burning with grief, slowly went far toward the eastern direction, remembering the lotus feet of the Lord. ॥8॥
3.31.9: Then at dawn, having travelled a long way through Śaṅkara's compassion, the queen saw a clear lake. ॥9॥
3.31.10: Arriving there, the king's beloved, delicate and distressed, took shelter under a shady tree on the lakeshore in order to rest. ॥10॥
3.31.11: There, by the power of destiny, at an auspicious hour endowed with good qualities, the queen gave birth to a divine son marked with all the auspicious signs. ॥11॥
3.31.12: Then, by fate, his mother, the king's wife, being very thirsty, went down into the lake to drink and was seized in the water by a crocodile. ॥12॥
3.31.13: That son, just born, sorely afflicted by hunger and thirst, wept on the lakeshore, having lost both father and mother. ॥13॥
3.31.14: O sage, as the newborn son was crying in that forest, Maheśa, the indwelling controller and protector, was filled with compassion. ॥14॥
3.31.15: Prompted in her mind by the Lord, the remover of fear, a certain woman who lived by begging, wandering about, suddenly arrived there. ॥15॥
3.31.16: That widow, carrying her own one-year-old child, saw there a lone, helpless infant crying. ॥16॥
3.31.17: O sage, seeing that child there in the deserted forest, the brahmin woman was greatly astonished and pondered much in her heart. ॥17॥
3.31.18: Ah, what a great wonder I have now seen—altogether inconceivable by the mind and indescribable in words! ॥18॥
3.31.19: This infant, with his navel cord still uncut, lies alone on the ground, motherless and crying—the best of the radiant ones. ॥19॥
3.31.20: None of his relatives, father or others, are here to help. What could have been the cause? Ah, great is the power of fate! ॥20॥
3.31.21: I do not know whose son he is, and no one here knows him, from whom I might ask about his birth. Yet compassion has arisen in me. ॥21॥
3.31.22: I wish to raise this child like a son of my own body, but I dare not touch him without knowing his family, birth, and so on. ॥22॥
3.31.23: Nandīśvara said: While that excellent brahmin woman was reflecting thus, Śaṅkara, who loves his devotees, showed great compassion. ॥23॥
3.31.24: Maheśvara of great sport assumed the form of a mendicant—he who always grants happiness to his devotees in every way, and is himself ever free of limiting attributes. ॥24॥
3.31.25: That mendicant, the Supreme Lord, suddenly came to where the doubting brahmin woman was, wishing to know the truth. ॥25॥
3.31.26: That Lord in the form of an excellent mendicant, whose ways are unknowable, the treasure of compassion, smiled and spoke to the brahmin woman. ॥26॥
3.31.27: The best of mendicants said: Do not harbour doubt in your mind, O brahmin lady; do not be troubled. Protect this very pure child lovingly as your own little son. ॥27॥
3.31.28: Through this infant you will before long attain the highest good. Nourish this greatly radiant child in every way. ॥28॥
3.31.29: Nandīśvara said: When he, Śambhu, the treasure of compassion in the form of a mendicant, had spoken thus, the brahmin woman questioned him lovingly and respectfully. ॥29॥
3.31.30: The brahmin woman said: By your command I will protect this child like my own son and nourish him—there is no doubt about this. Through my good fortune you have come here. ॥30॥
3.31.31: Even so, I wish to know in particular and truly: who is he, whose son is he, and who are you who have come here? ॥31॥
3.31.32: O lord, best of mendicants, again and again an insight comes to me: you are Śiva, the ocean of compassion, and this infant was formerly your devotee. ॥32॥
3.31.33: Through some fault in his past actions he has come to this state. Having undergone it, he will attain the highest good by your grace. ॥33॥
3.31.34: It is by your māyā alone that I, having strayed from my path and been bewildered, have come here—sent by you for the sake of protecting him. ॥34॥
3.31.35: Nandīśvara said: To the brahmin woman, who had gained understanding through seeing him and who wished to know in detail, Śiva in the body of a mendicant spoke. ॥35॥
3.31.36: The best of mendicants said: Listen gladly, O brahmin's wife, to the past doings of this child. All of it, including what concerns his other life, will be told truly and with great affection, O sinless one. ॥36॥
3.31.37: This is the son of the wise king of Vidarbha, Satyaratha, a devotee of Śiva, devoted to his own dharma. ॥37॥
3.31.38: Listen: King Satyaratha was slain by enemies in battle with the Śālvas. His wife, greatly distressed, quickly left her home at night. ॥38॥
3.31.39: Arriving here at dawn, she gave birth to this son; then, going down into the lake out of thirst, she was by fate seized by a crocodile. ॥39॥
3.31.40: Nandīśvara said: Thus he related to her everything: the child's birth, his father's death in battle, and his mother's death by the crocodile. ॥40॥
3.31.41: Then that Brahmin woman, greatly astonished, O lord of sages, again questioned that mendicant, the wise one who had the form of a perfected being. ॥41॥
3.31.42: The brahmin woman said: O mendicant, why was that king, this child's father, slain in the very midst of his excellent enjoyments by the Śālvas, his own enemies, with but little effort? ॥42॥
3.31.43: Why was this infant's mother swiftly devoured by a crocodile, so that he has become helpless and kinless from his very birth? ॥43॥
3.31.44: Why is my own son here also so very poor, a beggar? How may happiness come to these two sons? Tell me, O mendicant. ॥44॥
3.31.45: Nandīśvara said: Having heard these words of the Brahmin's wife, that mendicant, the Supreme Lord, pleased at heart and smiling, spoke to her. ॥45॥
3.31.46: The best of mendicants said: O wife of the Brahmin, I shall answer all your questions in detail. Listen attentively to this excellent account. ॥46॥
3.31.47: That king of Vidarbha, father of this boy, was in his former birth a Pāṇḍya, the best of kings. ॥47॥
3.31.48: That Śaiva king, protecting the whole earth righteously, delighted his subjects and destroyed all calamities. ॥48॥
3.31.49: Once, on the thirteenth lunar day, fasting and observing the day-and-night vow, he was worshipping Śiva, the Lord of all, at the pradoṣa twilight hour. ॥49॥
3.31.50: While he, absorbed, was worshipping Śambhu Giriśa at pradoṣa, a great and terrible noise arose throughout the city. ॥50॥
3.31.51: Hearing that sound, the king abandoned the worship of Śiva and, fearing an enemy attack, went out of the palace. ॥51॥
3.31.52: At that very moment his very mighty minister, having captured an enemy feudal lord, came to the king. ॥52॥
3.31.53: Seeing that enemy lord, the king, overwhelmed by great anger, without considering righteousness, had his head cut off. ॥53॥
3.31.54: Without completing that worship of the Lord, the king, impure, his judgement lost, ate his meal at night with great relish, his auspiciousness destroyed. ॥54॥
3.31.55: In this birth he became king in Vidarbha, a keeper of Śiva's vow; but because of the interruption of Śiva's worship he was slain by enemies in the midst of his enjoyments. ॥55॥
3.31.56: He who was his father in the former life is, in this birth, his son—this very one, deprived of sovereignty because of the breach in Śiva's worship. ॥56॥
3.31.57: His mother, in her former life, did away with her co-wife by deceit; because of that sin she was devoured by a crocodile in this life. ॥57॥
3.31.58: This history of theirs has been told to you. Those who do not worship Śiva with devotion fall into poverty. ॥58॥
3.31.59: This son of yours was, in his former birth, an excellent Brahmin; he spent his life accepting gifts, not in sacrifices and other good deeds. ॥59॥
3.31.60: Therefore your son has fallen into poverty, O Brahmin lady. To remove that fault, go to Śaṅkara for refuge. ॥60॥
3.31.61: Let these two boys perform the worship of Śiva; after their investiture with the sacred thread, Śiva will surely bring about their welfare. ॥61॥
3.31.62: Nandīśvara said: Having thus instructed her, Śiva, who had taken the body of the excellent mendicant and who is loving to his devotees, revealed his supreme true form. ॥62॥
3.31.63: Then that Brahmin woman, recognising him as Lord Śaṅkara, bowed down deeply and praised him with love, in a voice choked with emotion. ॥63॥
3.31.64: Then Lord Śambhu, who had assumed the mendicant's body, swiftly vanished right there as the Brahmin's wife looked on. ॥64॥
3.31.65: When that mendicant had gone, the Brahmin woman, reassured, took that infant and went home together with her own son. ॥65॥
3.31.66: Making her dwelling in the charming village called Ekacakra, she raised her own son and the prince with good food. ॥66॥
3.31.67: The two, having had their sacraments and sacred-thread ceremony performed by Brahmins, grew up in their home, devoted to the worship of Śiva. ॥67॥
3.31.68: Dear one, by the instruction of the sage Śāṇḍilya, the two, steadfast in their observances, kept the auspicious vow and worshipped Śambhu at pradoṣa. ॥68॥
3.31.69: Once the prince, having gone to bathe in the river without the Brahmin's son, found an excellent pot of treasure. ॥69॥
3.31.70: Thus, as the prince and the Brahmin boy worshipped Śambhu, four months passed for them in happiness. ॥70॥
3.31.71: As they continued to worship Śambhu with supreme joy, a year passed for them in that very home. ॥71॥
3.31.72: When the year had passed, O sage, the prince, having gone to the edge of the forest with the Brahmin boy, by the grace of the all-pervading Śiva— ॥72॥
3.31.73: —married the Gandharva's daughter who had unexpectedly come there and was given to him by her father, and ruled a kingdom free of enemies. ॥73॥
3.31.74: The Brahmin woman who had earlier nourished him like her own son became his mother, and the Brahmin's son his brother. ॥74॥
3.31.75: Having thus worshipped the Lord of gods, he, named Dharmagupta, enjoyed royal pleasures with that queen in the land of Vidarbha. ॥75॥
3.31.76: Thus I have now described to you Śiva's incarnation as the excellent mendicant, which bestowed happiness on the boy-king named Dharmagupta. ॥76॥
3.31.77: This narrative is sinless, holy, purifying and great; it is a means to dharma, wealth, desire and liberation, and grants all wishes. ॥77॥
3.31.78: Whoever with a focused mind constantly hears this or causes it to be heard, enjoys all desires here and at the end goes to the city of Śiva. ॥78॥
3.31.iti: Thus ends the thirty-first adhyāya, named The deeds of the incarnation of Śiva called Bhikṣuvarya, in the third saṃhitā, the Śatarudra-saṃhitā, of the Śrī Śivamahāpurāṇa. ॥31॥
3.32.1: Listen, dear one; I shall tell you of the Sureśvara incarnation of Śiva, the Supreme Self, which brought welfare to Dhaumya's elder brother. ॥1॥
3.32.2: The wise Upamanyu, son of Vyāghrapāda, dear to the virtuous, already perfected through a former birth, had attained the state of a sage's boy. ॥2॥
3.32.3: While still a mere child he lived with his mother in his maternal uncle's house; Upamanyu, son of Vyāghrapāda, was poor by the will of fate. ॥3॥
3.32.4: Once, at his uncle's hermitage, he drank a very little milk; then, longing for milk, he lovingly begged his mother again and again. ॥4॥
3.32.5: Hearing her son's words, his mother, an ascetic woman, went inside and then devised a good expedient. ॥5॥
3.32.6: Grinding seeds gathered by gleaning and stirring them with water, she coaxed her son and gave him artificial milk. ॥6॥
3.32.7: Having drunk the artificial milk given by his mother, the boy said to her, this is not milk, and wept again. ॥7॥
3.32.8: Hearing her son's weeping, she, lovely as a lotus, grieved, wiped her son's eyes with her hands and spoke to him. ॥8॥
3.32.9: The mother said: Where could milk come from for us, who always dwell in the forest? Without Śambhu's grace there can be no obtaining of milk. ॥9॥
3.32.10: Whatever was done in a former birth with Śiva as its aim, O son, that alone is surely obtained; there is no need for doubt here. ॥10॥
3.32.11: Hearing these words of his mother, that boy, son of Vyāghrapāda, loving to his mother and free of sorrow, replied to her. ॥11॥
3.32.12: Enough of this grief, mother. If Śambhu, Śaṅkara, exists, give up your sorrow, O fortunate one; all will be well. ॥12॥
3.32.13: Hear my words today, mother: if Mahādeva exists anywhere, then sooner or later I will obtain an ocean of milk. ॥13॥
3.32.14: Nandīśvara said: Having said this, the child joyfully declared, may Śiva be mine, took leave of her, bowed deeply, and set about performing austerity. ॥14॥
3.32.15: Going to the Himālaya mountain, living on air, concentrated, he made a shrine of eight bricks and a liṅga of clay. ॥15॥
3.32.16: Invoking there Śiva together with Ambā with devotion through the five-syllable mantra, the child worshipped him with forest leaves, flowers and the like. ॥16॥
3.32.17: Meditating on that Śiva with Ambā, repeating the five-syllable mantra and worshipping for a long time, he practised supreme austerity. ॥17॥
3.32.18: By the austerity of that boy, the great-souled Upamanyu, the world of moving and unmoving beings was set ablaze, O sage. ॥18॥
3.32.19: Meanwhile the Lord Śambhu, entreated by Viṣṇu and the others, took the form of Śakra (Indra) to test his devotion. ॥19॥
3.32.20: Śivā took the form of Śacī, all the gaṇas became gods, Nandī became the elephant Airāvata, and everything else was transformed accordingly. ॥20॥
3.32.21: Then Śiva with Ambā, in the form of Śakra and with his gaṇas, went swiftly to Upamanyu's hermitage to bestow grace. ॥21॥
3.32.22: To test his devotion, Hara, bearing Śakra's form, spoke to that boy in a deep voice, O lord of sages. ॥22॥
3.32.23: The lord of the gods said: I am pleased with you by this austerity, O you of good vows; ask a boon. I will grant all the desires you wish; there is no doubt about this. ॥23॥
3.32.24: Thus addressed by Śambhu in Śakra's form, he said with joined palms: I choose devotion to Śiva. ॥24॥
3.32.25: Hearing that, Hari (Indra) said: Do you not know me, the lord of the gods, Śakra, ruler of the three worlds, saluted by all the gods? ॥25॥
3.32.26: Become my devotee, O brahmin sage; worship me alone always. I will give you every good thing; and abandon Rudra, who is without attributes. ॥26॥
3.32.27: Enough of the attributeless Rudra. What purpose of yours will he serve—he who is outside the race of gods and has become a piśāca? ॥27॥
3.32.28: Nandīśvara said: Hearing that, the sage's son, repeating the five-syllable mantra and regarding him as one come to obstruct his dharma, spoke to him. ॥28॥
