3.32.29: Upamanyu said: All this has been said by you, intent on reviling Bhava; incidentally you have spoken of the attributelessness and the piśāca-nature of the God of gods. ॥29॥
3.32.30: You do not know Rudra, the lord of the lords of all gods, the begetter of Brahmā, Viṣṇu and Maheśa, beyond Prakṛti. ॥30॥
3.32.31: He whom the knowers of Brahman call being and non-being, manifest and unmanifest, eternal, one and many—from him I choose a boon. ॥31॥
3.32.32: He whom the knowers of truth declare to be supreme, free from mere argumentation, bestower of the goal of Sāṅkhya and Yoga—from him I choose a boon. ॥32॥
3.32.33: There is no reality higher than Śambhu, the cause of all causes, the all-pervading one beyond the guṇas, who is foremost among the gods Brahmā, Viṣṇu and the rest. ॥33॥
3.32.34: I do not choose a boon from you, nor from Viṣṇu or Brahmā, nor from any other immortal; may Śaṅkara be my boon-giver. ॥34॥
3.32.35: What use is saying much here? I state the truth, my own conviction: I plainly ask of no god or other being apart from Paśupati. ॥35॥
3.32.36: Hear my conviction, O foe of the mountains (Indra); this I have inferred today: if I have heard reviling of Bhava, it is due to sin committed in another birth. ॥36॥
3.32.37: Having heard reviling of Bhava, one should at that very moment give up one's own body; having quickly slain that reviler, he goes to Śiva's world. ॥37॥
3.32.38: Let this desire of mine for milk rest for now, O vilest of gods; having slain you with Śiva's weapon, I shall abandon this body. ॥38॥
3.32.39: Nandīśvara said: Having spoken thus, Upamanyu, himself resolved to die and giving up even his desire for milk, made ready to slay Śakra. ॥39॥
3.32.40: Then, taking ash from its receptacle, consecrated with the Aghora-weapon mantra, and hurling it at Śakra, the sage roared. ॥40॥
3.32.41: Remembering the two feet of his beloved deity and ready to burn his own body, Upamanyu stood holding the fiery (āgneyī) yogic concentration (dhāraṇā). ॥41॥
3.32.42: When the brahmin had thus resolved, the Lord, who had taken Indra's form, restrained that yogin's concentration with a gentle (saumya) one. ॥42॥
3.32.43: At the command of Śiva, Nandī's lord, Nandī, dear to Śaṅkara, caught in mid-course the Aghora weapon released and hurled by him. ॥43॥
3.32.44: Assuming his own form, the Lord, the Supreme Ruler, showed the brahmin his form crowned with the crescent moon. ॥44॥
3.32.45: And that Lord showed him a thousand oceans of milk, likewise an ocean of curd and the rest, and an ocean of foods to chew and to eat. ॥45॥
3.32.46: Thus Śambhu was seen with the Goddess upon the bull, surrounded by the lords of the gaṇas and by divine weapons, the trident and others. ॥46॥
3.32.47: Drums sounded in heaven, a shower of flowers fell, and the ten directions were filled with gods headed by Viṣṇu, Brahmā and Indra. ॥47॥
3.32.48: Then Upamanyu, engulfed by the waves of an ocean of bliss, fell flat on the ground like a staff, with a mind bowed in devotion. ॥48॥
3.32.49: At that moment Lord Bhava, smiling, called him, saying, come, come, kissed him on the head and granted boons. ॥49॥
3.32.50: Śiva said: Dear Upamanyu, I am pleased by your excellent conduct. You are a steadfast devotee, O brahmin sage; you have just been tested by me. ॥50॥
3.32.51: Enjoy foods and pleasures as you wish with your kinsmen at all times. Be happy, ever free from sorrow, devoted to me. ॥51॥
3.32.52: O greatly fortunate Upamanyu, this Pārvatī is indeed your mother. Today you have been made our son by me, and granted eternal youth. ॥52॥
3.32.53: Oceans of milk, curd, ghee and honey by the thousands, and likewise all the oceans of foods and other things— ॥53॥
3.32.54: —are given to you by me with love; accept them, O great sage. Immortality too is granted, and eternal leadership of the gaṇas. ॥54॥
3.32.55: I, Mahādeva, am your father; your mother is Jagadambikā. Choose, with great joy, other boons that your heart desires. ॥55॥
3.32.56: Be ageless and deathless, free from sorrow, famous, of excellent splendour, endowed with divine knowledge, a great master. ॥56॥
3.32.57: Then Śambhu, gracious at heart, remembering his great austerity, gave ten more divine boons to the sage Upamanyu: ॥57॥
3.32.58: He gave him the Pāśupata vow, knowledge, the yoga of the vow in its true essence, eloquence in exposition, skill, and his own state. ॥58॥
3.32.59: Having given thus, Mahādeva took him in both hands, kissed him on the head, and told the Goddess: This is your son. ॥59॥
3.32.60: And the Goddess, hearing this with love, placed her lotus hand upon his head and bestowed on him the imperishable state of Kumāra. ॥60॥
3.32.61: She also gave him the Milk Ocean in embodied form—the ocean that yields the sweetness of milk—bringing it near, solidified and imperishable. ॥61॥
3.32.62: With a fully satisfied mind she gave him yogic sovereignty, constant contentment, imperishable knowledge of Brahman, and supreme prosperity. ॥62॥
3.32.63: He too, having obtained divine boons and perpetual youth from that Śiva and from Śivā, was overjoyed. ॥63॥
3.32.64: Then, glad at heart, bowing low with folded hands, he lovingly asked a boon of Maheśvara, the God of gods. ॥64॥
3.32.65: Upamanyu said: Be gracious, O Lord of the God of gods; be gracious, O Supreme Lord. Grant me supreme, divine, unwavering devotion to you. ॥65॥
3.32.66: O Mahādeva, grant me always faith in those connected with you, supreme servitude to you, love, and your presence at all times. ॥66॥
3.32.67: Nandīśvara said: Having spoken thus, Upamanyu, best of the twice-born, glad at heart, praised Mahādeva in a voice choked with joy. ॥67॥
3.32.68: Thus addressed by him, Śiva, the Lord, the ruler of all, pleased at heart, replied to Upamanyu while everyone listened. ॥68॥
3.32.69: Śiva said: Dear Upamanyu, you are blessed, and especially my devotee. Everything you have chosen has been granted to you by me, O sinless one. ॥69॥
3.32.70: Be ageless and deathless, ever free from sorrow, worshipped by all, unchanging, the foremost of devotees. ॥70॥
3.32.71: Your kinsmen, family and lineage will always be imperishable, O best of the twice-born, and your devotion to me eternal. ॥71॥
3.32.72: And I shall always be present in your hermitage, O sage. Stay as you please, dear child; you will feel no longing. ॥72॥
3.32.73: Nandīśvara said: Having spoken thus and given him excellent boons, the blessed Lord, together with Ambā and his gaṇas, vanished at once right there. ॥73॥
3.32.74: Upamanyu, glad at heart, having obtained excellent boons from Śambhu, went to his mother's dwelling and related everything to his mother. ॥74॥
3.32.75: Hearing that, his mother attained great joy. He too became worshipped by all and always enjoyed abundant happiness. ॥75॥
3.32.76: Thus, dear one, I have described to you the Sureśvara incarnation of Śiva, the Supreme Self, which ever gives happiness to the good. ॥76॥
3.32.77: This pure narrative grants the fruit of all desires; it leads to heaven, fame and long life, and bestows enjoyment and liberation on the good. ॥77॥
3.32.78: Whoever listens to this with devotion, or with a collected mind causes it to be heard, having enjoyed every happiness here, attains in the end the goal of Śiva. ॥78॥
3.32.iti: Thus ends the thirty-second adhyāya, named The deeds of the incarnation of Śiva called Sureśvara, in the third saṃhitā, the Śatarudra-saṃhitā, of the Śrī Śivamahāpurāṇa. ॥32॥
3.33.1: Nandīśvara said: O Sanatkumāra, listen with great delight to the most purifying incarnation, named Jaṭila, of Śiva, the Supreme Self, the all-pervading Lord. ॥1॥
3.33.2: Formerly Satī, the daughter of Dakṣa, disrespected by her own father, gave up her body at her father's sacrifice and was born of Menā from Himālaya, the mountain. ॥2॥
3.33.3: Going into a dense forest, Śivā, accompanied by her two female friends, performed very pure austerity, desiring Śaṅkara as her husband. ॥3॥
3.33.4: To test that austerity thoroughly, Śiva, skilled in many sports, sent the seven sages to Pārvatī's place of austerity. ॥4॥
3.33.5: Those sages went there and carefully put her to the test, but despite great effort they were not able to shake her. ॥5॥
3.33.6: Coming there to Śiva, they bowed to him, reported that account, and, having received his permission, respectfully went to heaven. ॥6॥
3.33.7: When those sages had gone to their own abode, Śaṅkara himself, the Lord, the cause of creation, wished to test Śivā's conduct. ॥7॥
3.33.8: Greatly pleased, this Lord, in order to fulfil the desire of the ascetic maiden, then took the most wondrous form of a celibate student. ॥8॥
3.33.9: Very old, bearing the body of a brahmin, blazing with his own splendour, delighted in mind, carrying a staff and an umbrella, he was exceedingly radiant. ॥9॥
3.33.10: Having thus assumed the matted-haired form, Śambhu, Śaṅkara, affectionate to his devotees, full of great love, went to Girijā's forest. ॥10॥
3.33.11: There he saw the goddess seated on an altar, surrounded by her friends, pure within, auspicious like a digit of the moon. ॥11॥
3.33.12: Having looked at that goddess, Śambhu, bearing the form of a celibate student, affectionate to his devotees and eager, approached her lovingly. ॥12॥
3.33.13: Then, seeing the brahmin who had arrived, wondrous in splendour, hairy on his limbs, calm, furnished with a staff and a hide, ॥13॥
3.33.14: observing celibacy, old, matted-haired, carrying a water-pot, she worshipped him with supreme love, with all the articles of worship. ॥14॥
3.33.15: Then the goddess Pārvatī, with supreme joy, respectfully asked that celibate student, whom she had worshipped, about his welfare. ॥15॥
3.33.16: Who indeed are you, in the form of a celibate student, and from where have you come? You illumine this forest. Tell me, O best of the knowers of the Veda. ॥16॥
3.33.17: Nandīśvara said: Thus asked by Pārvatī, that twice-born celibate student replied quickly and affectionately, in order to test Śivā's disposition. ॥17॥
3.33.18: The brahmacārī said: I am a twice-born celibate student who goes wherever he wishes; an ascetic, a giver of happiness to others, a benefactor, no doubt. ॥18॥
3.33.19: Nandīśvara said: Having said this, that celibate student, Śaṅkara, affectionate to his devotees, stood nearby, concealing his own form. ॥19॥
3.33.20: The brahmacārī said: What shall I say, O great goddess? There is nothing fit to be said. A great and perverse affair, causing great harm, is to be seen. ॥20॥
3.33.21: In fresh youth, which is the means of fine enjoyments and the cause of happiness, you are practising austerity in vain, forgoing great comforts and fine pleasures. ॥21॥
3.33.22: Who are you? Whose daughter are you? Why do you perform, in a lonely forest, austerity hard to undertake even for sages of controlled mind? ॥22॥
3.33.23: Nandīśvara said: Hearing his words, the Supreme Goddess laughed and lovingly spoke to the excellent celibate student. ॥23॥
3.33.24: Pārvatī said: Listen, O brahmin, O celibate student, O sage, to my whole story. My present birth is in Bhārata-varṣa, in the house of Himavat. ॥24॥
3.33.25: Formerly I was born in Dakṣa's house as Satī, the beloved of Śaṅkara; I gave up my body through yoga because of my father, who reviled my husband. ॥25॥
3.33.26: In this birth, O brahmin, Śiva was obtained through great merit; but he abandoned me, reduced Manmatha to ashes, and went away. ॥26॥
3.33.27: When Śaṅkara had departed, ashamed out of distress, I came here from my father's house to practise austerity, bound by the words of my preceptor. ॥27॥
3.33.28: With mind, speech and action, directly, in the sense of a husband, Śaṅkara has been chosen by me; I speak the truth, not falsehood. ॥28॥
3.33.29: I know it is a thing hard to obtain—how could it be attained by me? Even so, out of my mind's longing, I am now performing austerity. ॥29॥
3.33.30: Setting aside the gods headed by Indra, and even Viṣṇu and Brahmā, I truly wish to obtain the Pināka-bearer as my husband. ॥30॥
3.33.31: Nandīśvara said: Having heard these resolute words of Pārvatī, O sage, that Jaṭila, Rudra, laughing, spoke. ॥31॥
3.33.32: The matted-haired ascetic said: O goddess, daughter of Himācala, what notion have you adopted, that for Rudra's sake, abandoning the gods, you perform such vast austerity? ॥32॥
3.33.33: I know that Rudra; listen, I shall tell you. That Rudra has a bull on his banner, is of deformed nature, and wears matted locks. ॥33॥
3.33.34: He is always solitary, perpetually so, and above all dispassionate. Therefore you ought not to join your mind to that Rudra. ॥34॥
3.33.35: Everything—form and the rest—of yours and Hara's is opposed, O goddess. This does not please me; but do as you wish. ॥35॥
3.33.36: Nandīśvara said: Having said this, Rudra, in the form of a celibate student, again reviled himself in many ways in her presence, in order to test her. ॥36॥
3.33.37: Hearing that unbearable speech of the brahmin, the goddess Pārvatī, greatly enraged, replied to him who was bent on reviling Śiva. ॥37॥
3.33.38: So far I had thought that someone blessed had come; but now everything is known: you appear merely as one who must not be slain. ॥38॥
3.33.39: You are some rogue who has come in the guise of a celibate student. You have reviled Śiva, you fool, and my wrath has arisen. ॥39॥
3.33.40: You do not know Śiva; indeed you are turned away from Śiva. Since I have worshipped you, I am therefore filled with remorse. ॥40॥
3.33.41: The man who here reviles Śiva without knowing the truth: the merit he has accumulated since birth turns to ashes. ॥41॥
3.33.42: Having touched one hostile to Śiva, one should perform expiation. ॥42॥
3.33.43: O you wicked one, you said that you know Śaṅkara. Certainly you have not understood him: Śiva alone is the supreme Lord. ॥43॥
3.33.44: However Rudra may be, assuming many forms through māyā, to me he is the giver of what I desire most, changeless, and dear to the good. ॥44॥
3.33.45: Nandīśvara said: Having said this to him, the goddess Śivā expounded the truth of Śiva, in which Rudra is declared, as Brahman, to be beyond attributes and imperishable. ॥45॥
3.33.46: Hearing those words of the goddess, that brahmin, the brahmacārin, had just begun to speak again, ॥46॥
3.33.47: when Girijā, whose mind was devoted to Śiva and who was averse to the reviling of Śiva, quickly spoke to her friend Vijayā. ॥47॥
3.33.48: Girijā said: O friend, this vilest of brahmins must be stopped with effort; he is intent on speaking again and will revile Śiva. ॥48॥
3.33.49: Sin falls not only on the one who reviles Śiva; whoever hears that reviling also becomes a sharer in sin here. ॥49॥
3.33.50: One who reviles Śiva is by all means to be slain by Śiva's servants; if he is a brahmin, he is to be shunned, and one should leave that place quickly. ॥50॥
3.33.51: This wicked one will revile Śiva again. Being a brahmin he cannot be slain, so he must be shunned and by all means not be looked upon. ॥51॥
3.33.52: Leaving this place quickly, we shall go elsewhere without delay, so that there may be no further conversation with this ignorant man. ॥52॥
3.33.53: Nandīśvara said: Just as Umā, having said this, lifted her foot to go, O sage, at that very moment Śiva himself, in person, caught hold of her garment. ॥53॥
3.33.54: Assuming his divine form exactly as Śivā meditated on it, and revealing it to Śivā, Śiva spoke to her as she stood with face cast down. ॥54॥
3.33.55: Śiva said: Where are you going, leaving me? You are not to be abandoned by me, O Śivā. You have been tested by me; you are my firm devotee, O sinless one. ॥55॥
3.33.56: Wishing to know your disposition, I came near you in the form of a brahmacārin and spoke words of various kinds. ॥56॥
3.33.57: I am deeply pleased, O Śivā, especially by your devotion. Name the boon your heart desires; there is nothing that cannot be given to you. ॥57॥
3.33.58: From today, O you full of love, I have been made your servant by your austerities. Because of your beauty a single moment seems like an age. ॥58॥
3.33.59: Let shyness be abandoned by you; you are my eternal wife. Come, beloved; with you I go quickly to my own mountain. ॥59॥
3.33.60: When the Lord of gods had spoken thus, Śivā attained great joy, and at once cast off all the suffering of her austerities. ॥60॥
3.33.61: Then, delighted at seeing that divine form of Śiva, Śivā, her face lowered in shyness, lovingly replied to the Lord. ॥61॥
3.33.62: Śivā said: If you are pleased, O Lord of gods, and show grace to me, become my husband, O Lord of gods. Thus was Śiva addressed by Śivā. ॥62॥
3.33.63: Nandīśvara said: Taking her hand according to rite, he went with her to Kailāsa; and Girijā, having gained him as husband, accomplished the task of the gods. ॥63॥
3.33.64: Thus, dear one, I have told you of Śiva's incarnation in the form of a brahmacārin, the tester of Śivā's devotion. ॥64॥
3.33.65: This pure and supreme narrative has been told by me. Whoever listens to it with love becomes happy and attains the highest goal. ॥65॥
3.33.iti: Thus ends the thirty-third adhyāya, named The incarnation of Śiva as the celibate student, in the third saṃhitā, the Śatarudra-saṃhitā, of the Śrī Śivamahāpurāṇa. ॥33॥
3.34.1: Nandīśvara said: O omniscient Sanatkumāra, hear of the incarnation of the all-pervading Śiva, the supreme Self, called Sunartaka-naṭa (the excellent dancer-actor). ॥1॥
3.34.2: When the goddess Kālikā, Pārvatī the daughter of Himavat, went to the forest and performed very pure austerities to attain Śiva, ॥2॥
3.34.3: then, O sage, Śiva became pleased with her fine austerity; to test her conduct thoroughly and to grant a boon, he went joyfully to her. ॥3॥
3.34.4: With a delighted heart he revealed his own form to her, and Śaṅkara said to that Śivā, O sage: Ask for a boon. ॥4॥
3.34.5: Hearing Śambhu's words and seeing his supreme form, Śivā rejoiced exceedingly; bowing deeply to him, she spoke. ॥5॥
3.34.6: Pārvatī said: If you are pleased, O lord of gods, and if a boon is to be given to me, then become my husband, O Īśāna; show compassion towards me. ॥6॥
3.34.7: With your permission I shall go properly to my father's house; you, O lord, O master, should then come to my father's presence. ॥7॥
3.34.8: Then, as a mendicant, ask for me, proclaiming my father's auspicious fame; and lovingly make his whole householder's life fruitful. ॥8॥
3.34.9: Then, O lord, O Maheśāna, you should perform the marriage according to the prescribed rite, for the accomplishment of the gods' purpose. ॥9॥
3.34.10: Fulfil my desire, O all-pervading one; you are ever free from change, and you are indeed named the one loving to devotees; I am always your devotee. ॥10॥
3.34.11: Nandīśvara said: Thus addressed by her, Śambhu, the great lord loving to devotees, said, so be it, vanished, and went to his own mountain. ॥11॥
3.34.12: Pārvatī too then, with delight, accompanied by her two friends, went to her father's house, having made her beauty fruitful. ॥12॥
3.34.13: Hearing of Pārvatī's arrival, that Himācala, with Menā and accompanied by his household, joyfully went to see his daughter. ॥13॥
3.34.14: Seeing her with a radiant face, the two brought her home and, overjoyed, lovingly had a great festival held. ॥14॥
3.34.15: Menā and likewise the best of mountains gave wealth to brāhmaṇas and others, and respectfully had auspicious rites performed with the sound of the Vedas. ॥15॥
3.34.16: Then Menā joyfully stayed in the courtyard with her daughter, while Himavat, the mountain, went to bathe in the Gaṅgā. ॥16॥
3.34.17: Meanwhile Śambhu, fond of sport and loving to devotees, became an excellent dancer-actor and came into Menakā's presence. ॥17॥
3.34.18: Holding a horn in his left hand and a ḍamaru in his right, with a patched cloak on his back, wearing red garments, skilled in dance and song, ॥18॥
3.34.19: then he, in the form of an actor, joyfully performed in Menakā's courtyard various dances and very charming songs. ॥19॥
3.34.20: There he sounded the horn and the ḍamaru with a fine tone, and lovingly performed various charming grand displays. ॥20॥
3.34.21: All the townspeople, men and women alike, even children and the old, certainly came there at once to see him. ॥21॥
3.34.22: Hearing that fine song and seeing the charming dance, all were suddenly entranced, and Menā too then, O sage. ॥22॥
3.34.23: Then Menā, her heart delighted by his performance, quickly went with love to give him jewels placed in golden vessels. ॥23॥
3.34.24: He did not accept them, saying, I desire as alms that Śivā; and, out of playfulness, he set about dancing and singing again. ॥24॥
3.34.25: Hearing his words, Menā, greatly astonished, became very angry; she rebuked the mendicant and wished to drive him out. ॥25॥
3.34.26: Meanwhile the king of mountains came there from the Gaṅgā and saw before him the mendicant in human form standing in the courtyard. ॥26॥
3.34.27: Hearing all that had happened from Menā's mouth, he became very angry and ordered his attendants to throw the mendicant out. ॥27॥
3.34.28: But no one could put him out, O best of sages, for he was blazing with great radiance and untouchable like a mighty fire. ॥28॥
3.34.29: Then, dear one, that mendicant, skilled in many sports, showed the mountain his own infinite power. ॥29॥
3.34.30: The mountain saw him there at once bearing the form of Viṣṇu, then the form of Brahmā, and then in a moment the form of the Sun. ॥30॥
3.34.31: Then, dear one, he saw him in the most wondrous form of Rudra, with Pārvatī, lovely, smiling, and radiant. ॥31॥
3.34.32: Thus he saw there his very many forms; at once he became greatly astonished and was flooded with supreme bliss. ॥32॥
3.34.33: Then that best of mendicants, the creator of all, begged from him and from her (Menā) that Durgā as alms, and accepted nothing else. ॥33॥
3.34.34: Then the Supreme Lord in the guise of a mendicant vanished and, prompted by Durgā's words, quickly went to his own abode. ॥34॥
3.34.35: Then true understanding arose in Menā and the lord of mountains as well: The all-pervading Śiva has deceived us and gone to his abode. ॥35॥
3.34.36: To him this our daughter Pārvatī, the great ascetic, should be given. Reflecting thus, supreme devotion to Śiva arose in the two of them. ॥36॥
3.34.37: Thereafter Rudra, having performed great sports that bring joy to devotees, lovingly married Pārvatī according to the prescribed rite. ॥37॥
3.34.38: Thus, dear one, I have told you of Śiva's incarnation named Sunartaka-naṭa, which fulfilled Śivā's words. ॥38॥
3.34.39: This sinless, supreme narrative has been told by me. Whoever listens to it with devotion becomes happy and attains the highest goal. ॥39॥
3.34.iti: Thus ends the thirty-fourth adhyāya, named The incarnation of Śiva called Sunartaka Naṭa, in the third saṃhitā, the Śatarudra-saṃhitā, of the Śrī Śivamahāpurāṇa. ॥34॥
3.35.1: Nandīśvara said: O all-knowing Sanatkumāra, hear of the incarnation of Śiva, the Supreme Self and all-pervading Lord, that is called the Brahmin in the guise of a holy man (sādhu-veṣa-dvija). ॥1॥
3.35.2: Knowing the supremely great devotion of Menā and Himālaya to Śiva, all the gods became anxious, and they consulted together earnestly. ॥2॥
3.35.3: If the mountain, with single-minded devotion, gives his daughter to Śambhu, he will surely attain at once the state of liberation (nirvāṇa) in Śiva. ॥3॥
3.35.4: If he, the repository of endless gems, goes to liberation, then the earth's name Ratnagarbhā (womb of gems) will surely become false. ॥4॥
3.35.5: Abandoning his immobile state and assuming a divine form, he, having given his daughter to the Trident-bearer, will go to Śiva's world. ॥5॥
3.35.6: Attaining likeness of form with Mahādeva by Śambhu's grace, and enjoying great pleasures there, he will then attain liberation. ॥6॥
3.35.7: Having thus considered, O sage, all the gods, intent on securing their own interest, went to the house of their preceptor (Bṛhaspati), and on arriving made their petition to him. ॥7॥
3.35.8: The gods said: O preceptor, go to Himālaya's house to accomplish our purpose; by speaking ill of Maheśa, turn the mountain away from his devotion. ॥8॥
3.35.9: O preceptor, by giving his daughter to Śiva with his own faith, that mountain would gain liberation; rather let him remain right here on the earth. ॥9॥
3.35.10: Hearing these words of the gods, and after reflecting, he spoke to them. ॥10॥
3.35.11: The guru said: O gods, let someone among you go to the mountain and accomplish what you desire; I am unable to do it. ॥11॥
3.35.12: Or else, O gods, go with Vāsava (Indra) to Brahmā's world; tell him your situation, and he will do your task. ॥12॥
3.35.13: Nandīśvara said: Hearing that, the gods deliberated and went to Brahmā's (Vidhi's) assembly, and laid the whole matter before Brahmā. ॥13॥
3.35.14: Having heard their words and pondered them well, Brahmā said to them: I will not utter censure of him, which always brings sorrow and destroys happiness. ॥14॥
3.35.15: O gods, go to Kailāsa and please Śaṅkara; send that god himself to Himālaya's house. ॥15॥
3.35.16: Let him go to the lord of mountains and censure himself; for censuring another is held to lead to ruin, while self-censure leads to glory. ॥16॥
3.35.17: Nandīśvara said: Then all the gods went quickly to Kailāsa, bowed devoutly to Śiva, and together recounted the whole matter. ॥17॥
3.35.18: Hearing the gods' words, Maheśvara accepted their request; smiling and reassuring them, he sent the gods off. ॥18॥
3.35.19: Then the blessed Śambhu, Maheśa, loving to his devotees, the lord of Māyā who is free of change, wished to go to the mountain's abode. ॥19॥
3.35.20: Carrying a staff and an umbrella, clad in splendid garments, bearing a bright tilaka mark, with a crystal rosary in his hand and a śālagrāma stone at his neck, ॥20॥
3.35.21: devoutly repeating the name of Hari, the Brahmin in the guise of a holy man went swiftly to Himācala, who was surrounded by his kinsfolk. ॥21॥
3.35.22: Seeing him, Himālaya rose up together with his attendants, and bowed down on the ground like a staff, with all eight limbs, according to rule. ॥22॥
3.35.23: Then the lord of mountains asked that Brahmin: Who are you? That foremost of Brahmins, the yogī, at once replied to the mountain with great courtesy. ॥23॥
3.35.24: Sādhudvija said: O mountain, I am called Sādhudvija; I am a Vaiṣṇava who sees the highest truth, devoted to helping others, all-knowing, and able to go everywhere through the power of my guru. ॥24॥
3.35.25: O best of mountains, I came to know your intention by my own insight while in my own place. Hear it: out of affection, I speak to you, casting aside deceit. ॥25॥
3.35.26: You wish to give your own daughter, this lovely girl equal to Padmā (Lakṣmī), to Śaṅkara, whose family and conduct are unknown. ॥26॥
3.35.27: This intention of yours, O king of mountains, is neither proper nor auspicious. Understand this, O best of the wise, born of Nārāyaṇa's line. ॥27॥
3.35.28: Consider your status as lord of mountains: he has not a single kinsman. Ask your own relatives carefully, and Menā, your beloved wife. ॥28॥
3.35.29: Ask all of them carefully, Menā and the rest, except Pārvatī; for, O mountain, to a sick man medicine is never pleasing—unwholesome food always is. ॥29॥
3.35.30: He is not a recipient suited to you in the act of giving Pārvatī; people of standing will smile merely on hearing of it. ॥30॥
3.35.31: He has no shelter, is ever unattached, ill-formed, without qualities, changeless; he dwells in cremation grounds, is frightful, handles snakes, and is naked (sky-clad). ॥31॥
3.35.32: His ornament is ash; his head is encircled by great serpents; he has fallen away from every stage of life (āśrama), and his ways are always unknown. ॥32॥
3.35.33: Brahmā said: Having spoken these and similar words—true, yet intent on censuring Śiva—Śiva, the performer of many sports, quickly returned to his own abode. ॥33॥
3.35.34: Hearing the Brahmin's words, the minds of the two, Himālaya and Menā, became contrary and inclined to mischief: What indeed shall we do? ॥34॥
3.35.35: Then Rudra, bestowing a great favour that brought joy to his devotees, married Girijā and accomplished the gods' purpose. ॥35॥
3.35.36: Thus, dear one, O lord, I have told you of Śiva's incarnation named the Brahmin in the guise of a holy man, who accomplished the gods' task. ॥36॥
3.35.37: This narrative is sinless, leads to heaven, grants long life, and is excellent; whoever reads or hears it becomes happy and attains the highest goal. ॥37॥
3.35.iti: Thus ends the thirty-fifth adhyāya, named The incarnation of Śiva as Sādhudvija, in the third saṃhitā, the Śatarudra-saṃhitā, of the Śrī Śivamahāpurāṇa. ॥35॥
3.36.1: Nandīśvara said: O Sanatkumāra, all-knowing one, hear of the supreme incarnation, named Aśvatthāman, of Śiva, the all-pervading Lord and Supreme Self. ॥1॥
3.36.2: O sage, from a portion of Bṛhaspati, the divine sage of great intellect, Droṇa, self-possessed and not born from a womb, was born of Bharadvāja. ॥2॥
3.36.3: He was the best of bowmen, a hero, a brahmin seer, knower of all the scriptures, of great fame and great splendour, foremost among those who know all weapons. ॥3॥
3.36.4: The wise know Droṇa as expert in the science of archery and in the Veda, the most excellent, of wondrous deeds, the one who increased the glory of his own family. ॥4॥
3.36.5: O brahmin, by his own strength he became the preceptor of the Kauravas, famed among the six great chariot-warriors in the Kaurava camp. ॥5॥
3.36.6: To aid the Kauravas, Droṇācārya, best of brahmins, performed extensive austerity directed to Śiva, for the sake of a son. ॥6॥
3.36.7: Then, pleased, the blessed Śaṅkara, loving to his devotees, appeared before Droṇa, O best of sages. ॥7॥
3.36.8: Seeing him, the brahmin Droṇa quickly bowed to him and praised him, his heart greatly delighted, bending low with palms joined. ॥8॥
3.36.9: Pleased by his praise and austerity, the Lord Śaṅkara, loving to devotees, said to Droṇa: Ask for a boon. ॥9॥
3.36.10: Hearing Śambhu's words, Droṇa, bowing deeply, then said: Grant me a son born of a portion of yourself, invincible to all, of great strength. ॥10॥
3.36.11: Hearing Droṇa's words, Śambhu said, so be it, and, dear one, the playful bestower of happiness vanished, O sage. ॥11॥
3.36.12: Droṇa went to his own abode, greatly delighted and free of anxiety, and joyfully told his wife all that had happened. ॥12॥
3.36.13: Then, at the proper time, Rudra, the Lord who ends all, was born through a portion of himself as Droṇa's son, mighty in strength. ॥13॥
3.36.14: He became famous on earth as Aśvatthāman, O sage — a great hero with lotus-petal eyes, the destroyer of the enemy's side. ॥14॥
3.36.15: Renowned in the Bhārata war, that mighty one, having received his father's command, became a helper of the Kauravas. ॥15॥
3.36.16: Relying on that great hero, the very mighty Kauravas, Bhīṣma and the others, became invincible even to the gods. ॥16॥
3.36.17: Out of fear of him, all the Pāṇḍavas, though great heroes and all skilled, were unable to conquer the Kauravas and were dispirited. ॥17॥
3.36.18: On Kṛṣṇa's advice Arjuna performed a most severe austerity to Śambhu, and having obtained a weapon through Śambhu's boon, he then conquered them. ॥18॥
3.36.19: Aśvatthāman, the great hero born of a portion of Mahādeva, O sage, nevertheless, under the sway of devotion to him, displayed his own prowess. ॥19॥
3.36.20: He, whose strength could not be checked by the enemy, the great heroes Kṛṣṇa and others, destroyed the sons of the Pāṇḍavas, even though they had been carefully trained. ॥20॥
3.36.21: Seeing that Arjuna, distraught with grief for his sons, rushing at him in a chariot with Acyuta, he fled. ॥21॥
3.36.22: He released at him the weapon called Brahmaśiras; then a fierce blaze arose in every direction. ॥22॥
3.36.23: Perceiving danger to his life, Arjuna, afflicted, exhausted, his vigour gone and in great fear, spoke to Kṛṣṇa. ॥23॥
3.36.24: Arjuna said: O Kṛṣṇa, Kṛṣṇa, I do not know what this is or from where it comes; this utterly unbearable blaze advances facing every side. ॥24॥
3.36.25: Nandīśvara said: Hearing these words of Arjuna, Kṛṣṇa, the best of Śaivas, meditated on Śiva together with his consort and respectfully replied to Arjuna. ॥25॥
3.36.26: Śrī Kṛṣṇa said: Know this to be the most dreadful Brahmā-weapon of Droṇa's son. There is no other weapon whatever that can counter it. ॥26॥
3.36.27: Quickly remember Śiva, Śambhu, your own Lord, protector of devotees, by whom his own supreme weapon, accomplishing every purpose, was given to you. ॥27॥
3.36.28: With the blaze of that Śaiva weapon, destroy this surging blaze of the weapon. Having said this, Kṛṣṇa himself meditated on Śiva for that purpose. ॥28॥
3.36.29: Hearing Kṛṣṇa's words, Pārtha remembered Śiva in his heart, touched water, bowed to him, and quickly discharged the weapon, O sage. ॥29॥
3.36.30: Although the Brahmaśiras weapon is unfailing and cannot be countered, it was instantly pacified by the blaze of the Śaiva weapon, O great sage. ॥30॥
3.36.31: Do not think this a marvel in the case of Śiva, who is full of every wonder — the Unborn who by his own power creates, protects and destroys the entire universe. ॥31॥
3.36.32: Then Aśvatthāman, born of Śiva's portion, knowing this event to be Śiva's doing, was not in the least distressed, his mind content with Śiva's will, O sage. ॥32॥
3.36.33: Then Drauṇi set his mind on destroying the child in Uttarā's womb, so as to make this whole world bereft of Pāṇḍavas. ॥33॥
3.36.34: That great lord hurled, aiming at Uttarā's womb, the Brahmā-weapon of great radiance, which other weapons could not check. ॥34॥
3.36.35: Then Uttarā, daughter-in-law of Jiṣṇu (Arjuna), her mind distraught, being burned by that weapon, praised Kṛṣṇa, the lord of Lakṣmī. ॥35॥
3.36.36: Then Kṛṣṇa, having meditated on Śiva, praised him in his heart and bowed, understood that Drauṇi's weapon was meant to make this world free of Pāṇḍavas. ॥36॥
3.36.37: By Śiva's command he made her protection with that radiant weapon Sudarśana, which had been given to him by the lord for his own protection. ॥37॥
3.36.38: Knowing the true nature of the deed performed by Kṛṣṇa, the foremost of Śaivas, at Śaṅkara's command, Aśvatthāman gradually became downcast. ॥38॥
3.36.39: Then Kṛṣṇa, king among Śaivas, pleased at heart, made all the Pāṇḍavas fall at his feet to gratify him. ॥39॥
3.36.40: Then Drauṇi Aśvatthāman, gracious at heart, showed them favour and lovingly gave various boons to the Pāṇḍavas and to Kṛṣṇa as well. ॥40॥
3.36.41: Thus, dear one, O best of sages, the Lord Maheśvara performed a supreme divine play, having descended upon the earth in the form of Drauṇi, the son of Droṇa. ॥41॥
3.36.42: Aśvatthāmā, the incarnation of Śiva, of great strength and valour, the giver of happiness to the three worlds, still dwells even today on the bank of the Jāhnavī Gaṅgā. ॥42॥
3.36.43: Thus the Aśvatthāmā incarnation of Lord Śaṅkara has been described to you; it brings about all accomplishments and also grants devotees the fruits they desire. ॥43॥
3.36.44: Whoever listens to this with devotion, or recites it with a concentrated mind, would attain the accomplishment he desires, and at the end would go to Śiva's city. ॥44॥
3.36.iti: Thus ends the thirty-sixth adhyāya, named The incarnation of Śiva as Aśvatthāman, in the third saṃhitā, the Śatarudra-saṃhitā, of the Śrī Śivamahāpurāṇa. ॥36॥
3.37.1: Nandīśvara said: Listen, O wise one, to the incarnation of the Pināka-bearer Śiva called Kirāta, in which he killed the demon Mūka and, being pleased, gave a boon to Arjuna. ॥1॥
3.37.2: Those excellent Pāṇḍavas, defeated by Suyodhana, went with that virtuous Draupadī to the forest called Dvaita. ॥2॥
3.37.3: There, relying on the vessel given by Sūrya, the Pāṇḍavas then passed their time in comfort, it is said. ॥3॥
3.37.4: O chief of brahmins, Durvāsas, foremost of sages, was sent by that Suyodhana with a deceitful purpose, respectfully, to the presence of the Pāṇḍavas. ॥4॥
3.37.5: Having arrived there with his own disciples, numbering ten thousand, he gladly asked them for food as his heart desired. ॥5॥
3.37.6: Having agreed, those Pāṇḍavas then sent the ascetic sages headed by Durvāsas off to bathe. ॥6॥
3.37.7: Then, O lord of sages, all those Pāṇḍavas, distressed for lack of food, resolved in their minds to give up their lives. ॥7॥
3.37.8: Remembered by Draupadī, Kṛṣṇa came at that very moment; and by eating a leaf of vegetable he brought about their satisfaction. ॥8॥
3.37.9: Then Durvāsas, knowing his disciples to be satiated, went away again; and the Pāṇḍavas were then freed from hardship by the grace of Kṛṣṇa. ॥9॥
3.37.10: Then those Pāṇḍavas asked Kṛṣṇa: What will happen? A powerful enemy has arisen. Tell us what should be done, O lord. ॥10॥
3.37.11: Nandīśvara said: Thus asked then by those Pāṇḍavas, O sage, Śrī Kṛṣṇa, remembering the lotus feet of Śiva, said this to the Pāṇḍavas. ॥11॥
3.37.12: Śrī Kṛṣṇa said: Listen, excellent Pāṇḍavas, to my story, especially as it concerns the service of Śiva; having heard it, you must act accordingly. ॥12॥
3.37.13: Having gone to Dvārakā with the desire to conquer my enemies, and having reflected on the teachings of the great-souled Upamanyu, ॥13॥
3.37.14: I worshipped Śambhu, the supreme Lord, well served for seven months on Baṭuka, the best of mountains, and he became pleased. ॥14॥
3.37.15: The Lord of the universe, standing before me in person, granted me my desired wishes; by his power I obtained supreme capability in all things. ॥15॥
3.37.16: Even now that god, giver of the fruits of enjoyment and liberation, is served by me. You too should serve that Śambhu, who brings all happiness. ॥16॥
3.37.17: Nandīśvara said: Having said this and consoled the Pāṇḍavas, Kṛṣṇa vanished and quickly went to Dvārakā, remembering the lotus feet of Śiva. ॥17॥
3.37.18: Then the Pāṇḍavas promptly sent a Bhilla as spy to examine the qualities of that Duryodhana. ॥18॥
3.37.19: He too, having learned all that was there—the flourishing of Duryodhana's qualities—and that it was sound, returned to his masters. ॥19॥
3.37.20: Hearing what he said, O lord of sages, they became sorrowful; and the Pāṇḍavas, deeply distressed, spoke to one another: ॥20॥
3.37.21: What should we do now, where should we go regarding war? Though all capable, we are bound by the noose of truth, our promise. ॥21॥
3.37.22: Nandīśvara said: At that time Vyāsa came, his forehead adorned with ash, wearing rudrākṣa ornaments, and adorned with matted locks. ॥22॥
3.37.23: Muttering the five-syllable mantra, overflowing with love for Śiva, himself a mass of radiance, like another Dharma incarnate. ॥23॥
3.37.24: Seeing him, they were delighted, rose and stood before him, and then offered him a seat beautified with kuśa grass and deerskin. ॥24॥
3.37.25: Joyful, they worshipped Vyāsa seated there, and having offered various praises, said: We are blessed. ॥25॥
3.37.26: The austerities well performed and the various gifts—all that has borne fruit; we are satisfied by the sight of you, O lord. ॥26॥
3.37.27: By your sight, O grandfather, sorrow has gone far away—great sorrow that was inflicted on us by the wicked, whose deeds are cruel. ॥27॥
3.37.28: When the sight of the illustrious occurs, sorrow will surely depart. If at any time it does not depart in such a case, this conclusion has been reached: ॥28॥
3.37.29: When the hermitage of the great, who are capable in every undertaking, has been reached, if sorrow still does not go, then fate alone is the cause here. ॥29॥
3.37.30: Poverty, the cause of sorrow, will certainly go. This nature of the great is held to be like the wish-fulfilling tree. ॥30॥
3.37.31: Counting only their qualities, by the very nature of the great one, it is solely through the power of one's refuge that, for a man, O lord, arise ॥31॥
3.37.32: smallness and greatness; no deliberation is needed on this. This is the nature of the noblest, that they protect the wretched. ॥32॥
3.37.33: The mark of a poor man is considered in the world most conducive to welfare: before him lies supreme effort and the service of good people. ॥33॥
3.37.34: Beyond this lies fortune; let no blame be assigned. For this reason, O master, when you have been seen, auspiciousness comes then. ॥34॥
3.37.35: By your mere arrival our minds are gladdened. Give us instruction by which our sorrow may quickly be destroyed. ॥35॥
3.37.36: Nandīśvara said: Hearing these words of the Pāṇḍavas, the great sage Vyāsa, his mind pleased, said this: ॥36॥
3.37.37: O Pāṇḍavas, you ought not to grieve. You are blessed, you have fulfilled your duty; truth has not been violated by you. ॥37॥
3.37.38: This is the most beautiful nature of good people: even at the end of life they never abandon dharma. Here, truth is the vessel of fruitful reward. ॥38॥
3.37.39: To us, you and they are alike; nevertheless, partiality toward the most righteous is approved by the wise. ॥39॥
3.37.40: First of all, by the wicked and blind Dhṛtarāṣṭra dharma was himself abandoned out of greed, and your kingdom was seized. ॥40॥
3.37.41: You, and they too, are indeed his sons; there is no doubt. Since your father has passed away, you children are to be treated with compassion by that great-souled one. ॥41॥
3.37.42: But afterwards his son was never restrained by him. Had he been restrained, no calamity would have arisen, nor what was then done in this way. ॥42॥
3.37.43: What has happened after that has happened; it could not be otherwise. This one is wicked, while you are most righteous and truthful. ॥43॥
3.37.44: Therefore, in the end, misfortune will surely come to him alone; whatever seed is sown, its sprout appears here. ॥44॥
3.37.45: Therefore you should by no means grieve. Good will surely come to you; there need be no doubt about this. ॥45॥
3.37.46: Nandīśvara said: When he had spoken thus, all the Pāṇḍavas, gladdened by Vyāsa, led by Yudhiṣṭhira, spoke these words again. ॥46॥
3.37.47: The Pāṇḍavas said: You have spoken the truth, O lord. The wicked, evil-souled ones inflict sorrow on us incessantly, again and again, even in the forest. ॥47॥
3.37.48: So destroy our misfortune today; grant us something auspicious, O mighty one. Kṛṣṇa told us before that Śaṅkara is always to be worshipped. ॥48॥
3.37.49: But we were negligent, and that advice was neglected. Let that divine path now be taught to us again. ॥49॥
3.37.50: Nandīśvara said: Hearing these words, Vyāsa, filled with joy, spoke lovingly to the Pāṇḍavas, having remembered the lotus-feet of Śiva. ॥50॥
3.37.51: Vyāsa said: Listen to my words today, O Pāṇḍavas of righteous mind. Kṛṣṇa indeed spoke the truth; Śiva is served by me as well. ॥51॥
3.37.52: Let him be served by you with love; there will always be incomparable happiness. All sorrow arises precisely from not serving Śiva. ॥52॥
3.37.53: Nandīśvara said: Then, having considered among those five who was suited for the worship of Śiva, Vyāsa, the best of sages, named Arjuna as the fit one; ॥53॥
3.37.54: and having thus considered a place for austerity, that most excellent sage then spoke this again to the Pāṇḍavas, who were firmly devoted to dharma. ॥54॥
3.37.55: Vyāsa said: Listen, all you Pāṇḍavas; I shall tell you what is always beneficial: seeing Śiva as everything, the Supreme, the supreme Brahman, the goal of the virtuous. ॥55॥
3.37.56: Whatever world is seen, from Brahmā up to the end of the triple parārdha, all that is Śiva's form; and that again is to be worshipped and meditated upon. ॥56॥
3.37.57: This Śaṅkara, destroyer of all sorrows, is to be served by all. Śiva becomes fully pleased in a short time through devotion. ॥57॥
3.37.58: For Maheśa, when well pleased, grants everything to his devotees; he bestows enjoyment and liberation, here and hereafter—this is firmly established. ॥58॥
3.37.59: Therefore Śambhu should always be served by those who desire the fruits of enjoyment and liberation. Śaṅkara is the Supreme Person himself, destroyer of the wicked, the goal of the virtuous. ॥59॥
3.37.60: But first one should, with a firm mind, recite the Śakra-vidyā (lore of Indra). For an eminent kṣatriya this alone is prescribed. ॥60॥
3.37.61: Therefore Arjuna, steadfast, should first recite the Śakra-vidyā. Indra will first test him, and then he will be satisfied. ॥61॥
3.37.62: Well pleased, he will always remove obstacles, and further he will bestow the excellent mantra of Śiva himself. ॥62॥
3.37.63: Nandīśvara said: Having said this, he summoned Arjuna and taught him the Upendra-vidyā. Having bathed and faced east, Arjuna of intense mind received it. ॥63॥
3.37.64: The best of sages also gave him the procedure for worshipping the earthen liṅga; and Vyāsa, of noble mind, spoke to Dhanañjaya in turn. ॥64॥
3.37.65: Vyāsa said: Go now from here, Pārtha, to the beautiful Indrakīla, and staying near the Jāhnavī (Gaṅgā), perform austerity properly. ॥65॥
3.37.66: And may this invisible lore always be beneficial to you. Thus he gave him a blessing; then the sage spoke to the others. ॥66॥
3.37.67: Let all of you, best of kings, remain steadfast in dharma. The highest success will come in every way; there need be no doubt about this. ॥67॥
3.37.68: Nandīśvara said: Having thus given his blessing to the Pāṇḍavas, Vyāsa, lord of sages, remembered Śiva's lotus-feet and vanished in an instant. ॥68॥
3.37.iti: Thus ends the thirty-seventh adhyāya, named Vyāsa's instruction to Arjuna, in the course of the account of the Kirāta incarnation, in the third saṃhitā, the Śatarudra-saṃhitā, of the Śrī Śivamahāpurāṇa. ॥37॥
3.38.1: Nandīśvara said: Then Arjuna too was seen there, shining, bearing incomparable radiance through the mantra, which has the form of Śiva. ॥1॥
3.38.2: All the Pāṇḍavas, seeing Arjuna, reached certainty: Victory is surely ours, since his radiance is so great. ॥2॥
3.38.3: This task is to be accomplished by you and never by anyone else; so it appears from Vyāsa's words. Make your life fruitful. ॥3॥
3.38.4: Having said this to Arjuna, they, distressed by the anxiety of separation, though unwilling, respectfully sent him off from that very place. ॥4॥
3.38.5: Draupadī, the devoted wife, filled with grief, holding back the tears in her eyes, then spoke auspicious words as she sent him off. ॥5॥
3.38.6: Draupadī said: O prince, what Vyāsa has instructed must be done by you with effort. May your path bring auspiciousness; may Śaṅkara grant you well-being. ॥6॥
3.38.7: Having respectfully sent Arjuna off, they all stayed there, overcome by extreme sorrow, the five of them together. ॥7॥
3.38.8: Staying there, they said—listen, O best of sages—even in sorrow, the company of a dear one does not lead to sorrow. ॥8॥
3.38.9: In separation from him, one's sorrow becomes constantly twofold; then how could even one who holds firm have fortitude here? ॥9॥
3.38.10: Nandīśvara said: While the Pāṇḍavas were thus grieving, the lord of sages, Vyāsa, the ocean of compassion and best of seers, arrived. ॥10॥
3.38.11: Then the Pāṇḍavas, filled with sorrow, bowed to him, worshipped him respectfully, offered him a seat, and with joined palms spoke these words. ॥11॥
3.38.12: The Pāṇḍavas said: Listen, O most excellent one; we are burned by sorrow, O lord. Having obtained your sight today, O sage, we attain joy. ॥12॥
3.38.13: Stay right here for some time to destroy our sorrow, O lord; through seeing you, O brahmin seer, all sorrow dissolves. ॥13॥
3.38.14: Nandīśvara said: Thus addressed, that best of sages stayed for their comfort, and then with various stories he drove away their sorrow. ॥14॥
3.38.15: While the conversation was being carried on by Vyāsa, O good sage, Dharmarāja, humble in spirit, bowed deeply and said this: ॥15॥
3.38.16: Yama said: Listen, O best of sages: I regard your presence as the pacification of my sorrow. I ask you, O greatly wise one; please tell me, O lord. ॥16॥
3.38.17: Has anyone in the past met with such sorrow? We alone have met with supreme sorrow, no one else. ॥17॥
3.38.18: Vyāsa said: Formerly, to the king named Nala, lord of Niṣadha, that great soul, there came sorrow greater than your sorrow. ॥18॥
3.38.19: King Hariścandra met with even greater sorrow; it is especially indescribable, and likewise brings grief to others who hear it. ॥19॥
3.38.20: Likewise, O Pāṇḍava, know the sorrow of Rāma too, hearing which women and men would fall into still greater bewilderment. ॥20॥
3.38.21: Therefore I cannot describe it again. Regarding the body as a heap of sorrow, you should now give up attachment to it. ॥21॥
3.38.22: Whoever has taken on this body is pervaded by sorrow, no doubt. First, birth in the mother's womb is a cause of sorrow. ॥22॥
3.38.23: In childhood too there is great sorrow, which follows from childish play; and after that, in youth, one enjoys pleasures that are sorrow in form. ॥23॥
3.38.24: With the coming and going of days and the many burdens of duties, life wastes away constantly, yet one does not realise it. ॥24॥
3.38.25: And at the end comes death, the greatest sorrow beyond this; and then the torments of various hells are suffered by ignorant men. ॥25॥
3.38.26: Therefore this world is unreal; you, however, practise what is true. A man should act in such a way that Śambhu is pleased. ॥26॥
3.38.27: Nandīśvara said: Thus, with various conversations and along the paths of their hopes, all the brothers then passed the time. ॥27॥
3.38.28: Arjuna too, firm in his vow, went on himself through difficult mountains, and, having obtained a Yakṣa as guide, with his help slaying robbers many times, ॥28॥
3.38.29: joyful in mind, went to the excellent mountain. Having gone there, near the Gaṅgā, he came to a beautiful spot, ॥29॥
3.38.30: an Aśoka grove, where it was as if the highest heaven stood. There he stayed, having bathed and bowed to his excellent teacher. ॥30॥
3.38.31: He himself adopted the dress and the rest just as he had been instructed. First withdrawing his senses, he became settled in mind. ॥31॥
3.38.32: Then, having made a beautiful, well-proportioned earthen liṅga, he meditated before it on the supreme mass of radiance. ॥32॥
3.38.33: Bathing well at the three times of day, he then performed various worship and repeatedly adored Hara there. ॥33॥
3.38.34: A radiance issued from his very head. Seeing that, the spies of Indra were seized with fear: When did this one enter here? ॥34॥
3.38.35: Then, having reflected thus, they said, this must be told to Indra (Viḍaujas), and went swiftly to Śakra's presence. ॥35॥
3.38.36: The spies said: Whether a god, or a sage, or the Sun, or Fire—someone is practising austerity in the forest, O lord of gods; we do not know who he is. ॥36॥
3.38.37: Scorched by his radiance, we have come into your presence. This account has been reported; let whatever is proper be done. ॥37॥
3.38.38: Nandīśvara said: Thus addressed by the spies, and understanding fully what his son intended, he dismissed the mountain-guardians and resolved to go there. ॥38॥
3.38.39: The lord of Śacī, becoming an old brahmin celibate, went there, O chief of brahmins, to test him. ॥39॥
3.38.40: Seeing him arrived, the Pāṇḍava then worshipped him, and standing before him, having praised him, said: Tell me now, from where have you come? ॥40॥
3.38.41: Addressed thus by him, the lord of the gods, out of affection and to test his steadfastness, then spoke to the Pāṇḍava words that concealed a test. ॥41॥
3.38.42: The brahmin said: Dear one, why are you now performing austerity at so young an age? Is this austerity of yours wholly for liberation or for victory? ॥42॥
3.38.43: Nandīśvara said: Questioned thus by him, Arjuna then again related everything. Hearing that, the brahmin then spoke again. ॥43॥
3.38.44: The brahmin said: O hero, austerity that is performed in accordance with kṣatriya duty to obtain happiness is not fitting; austerity is performed for liberation, O best of the Kurus. ॥44॥
3.38.45: Indra indeed is a giver of happiness, but he cannot be a giver of liberation. Therefore, O excellent one, you should by all means perform true austerity. ॥45॥
3.38.46: Nandīśvara said: Hearing these words, Arjuna then became angry; yet, humble of spirit and firm in his vows, he disregarded it and replied. ॥46॥
3.38.47: Arjuna said: It is for the kingdom and not for liberation — why do you say this? Such austerity is being performed solely at the word of Vyāsa. ॥47॥
3.38.48: Go away from here, celibate student. You wish to make me fall. What purpose do you, a celibate, have here? ॥48॥
3.38.49: Nandīśvara said: Addressed thus, he was pleased and revealed his own beautiful, wondrous form, endowed with his own insignia. ॥49॥
3.38.50: Seeing the form of Śakra, Arjuna then felt ashamed; Indra, having comforted him, spoke words again. ॥50॥
3.38.51: Indra said: Choose a boon, O dear Dhanañjaya of great intellect, whatever your heart desires; nothing exists that cannot be given to you. ॥51॥
3.38.52: Hearing Śakra's words, Arjuna then replied: Grant me victory in every way, dear one, for I am afflicted by enemies. ॥52॥
3.38.53: Śakra said: Your enemies, led by Duryodhana, are very mighty; Droṇa, Bhīṣma and Karṇa — all of them are surely hard to conquer. ॥53॥
3.38.54: Aśvatthāmā, Droṇa's son, a portion of Rudra, is extremely invincible. They would be wholly beyond my power; hear what is for your own good. ॥54॥
3.38.55: O hero, no one now is able to bring about this victory. Śiva, the most excellent, is there; therefore now undertake the japa of Śambhu. ॥55॥
3.38.56: Śaṅkara is the lord of all worlds, master of the moving and the unmoving, self-ruling; he is able to do everything and bestows the fruits of enjoyment and liberation. ॥56॥
3.38.57: I believe that I, Brahmā and the others, Viṣṇu the bestower of all boons, and all others who seek victory — all of them are worshippers of Śiva. ॥57॥
3.38.58: From today, abandoning that mantra, worship Śiva with devotion, by the rite of the earthen liṅga and by meditation on Śiva, ॥58॥
3.38.59: and with many offerings, with your whole being, O Bhārata; then your success will be unshakable today — there need be no deliberation about this. ॥59॥
3.38.60: Nandīśvara said: Having said this, he summoned all his attendants and said: You must always remain vigilant in protecting him. ॥60॥
3.38.61: Having instructed his attendants about Arjuna's protection and so on, Indra, his heart full of affection, again spoke to the one with the monkey banner. ॥61॥
3.38.62: Indra said: You must never rule the kingdom carelessly. May this knowledge be for your welfare, good one, O scorcher of foes. ॥62॥
3.38.63: Steadfastness must be maintained by the practitioner; Śiva is the protector in every way. He will give you prosperity and the fruit you seek; there is no doubt of this. ॥63॥
3.38.64: Nandīśvara said: Having thus given the boon to the Bhārata, the lord of the gods, remembering the lotus feet of Śiva, went to his own abode. ॥64॥
3.38.65: Arjuna too, the great hero, having bowed deeply to the lord of the gods, with self-control performed austerity of that kind directed toward Śiva. ॥65॥
3.38.iti: Thus ends the thirty-eighth adhyāya, named Arjuna's austerity, in the course of the account of the Kirāta incarnation, in the third saṃhitā, the Śatarudra-saṃhitā, of the Śrī Śivamahāpurāṇa. ॥38॥
3.39.1: Nandīśvara said: Having bathed according to rule, and likewise performed nyāsa and the rest according to rule, he performed with true devotion the meditation on Śiva exactly as Vyāsa had taught it. ॥1॥
3.39.2: Standing on the sole of one foot like an eminent sage, fixing his single-pointed gaze on the sun, he remained repeating the mantra. ॥2॥
3.39.3: He performed austerity with great delight, remembering Śiva in his mind and repeating Śambhu's five-syllabled mantra, the highest of all. ॥3॥
3.39.4: Such was the radiance of his austerity that the gods were amazed. They went again to Śiva and, composed, spoke to him. ॥4॥
3.39.5: The gods said: O Lord of all, a single man has undertaken austerity for your sake. Whatever this man desires, why do you not grant it, O Lord? ॥5॥
3.39.6: Nandīśvara said: Having said this, the gods then offered various hymns of praise, and fixing their eyes on his feet they stood there with steady minds. ॥6॥
3.39.7: Śiva, the great Lord of noble mind, hearing their words, laughed heartily and, pleased at heart, spoke to the gods. ॥7॥
3.39.8: Śiva said: Go to your own abodes, all you gods; this is true, without doubt. I shall accomplish your purpose in every way; there is no doubt about it. ॥8॥
3.39.9: Nandīśvara said: Hearing Śambhu's words, the gods attained supreme certainty, and all of them turned back and went to their own abodes. ॥9॥
3.39.10: Meanwhile a demon named Mūka arrived, having assumed the form of a boar, sent by the wicked one— ॥10॥
3.39.11: by the deceitful Duryodhana, O best of brahmins, against Arjuna; he came then by the path where Arjuna was staying, ॥11॥
3.39.12: breaking the peaks of the mountain and many trees, making various noises, rushing with great speed. ॥12॥
3.39.13: Arjuna too, seeing that demon named Mūka, remembered the lotus feet of Śiva and became intent on reflection. ॥13॥
3.39.14: Arjuna said: Who is this, and from where does he come? He appears to be of cruel deeds. Surely he is coming to do me harm, without doubt. ॥14॥
3.39.15: So my mind tells me: he is surely an enemy, no doubt. Many Daityas and Dānavas were slain by me before. ॥15॥
3.39.16: Someone of theirs is coming to take revenge again; or else some friend devoted to Duryodhana's welfare. ॥16॥
3.39.17: He at whose sight one's own mind becomes serene is surely a well-wisher; he at whose sight that same mind becomes agitated is surely an enemy. ॥17॥
3.39.18: Conduct reveals one's family, the body reveals one's food, speech reveals one's learning, and the eye reveals affection. ॥18॥
3.39.19: By appearance, gait, gesture and speech, and by changes in the eyes and face, the hidden mind is known. ॥19॥
3.39.20: The wise have declared the eye to be of four kinds—bright, tender, oblique and reddish—each with its own distinct meaning. ॥20॥
3.39.21: Bright on meeting a friend, tender on seeing a son, oblique in union with a beloved woman, and red on seeing an enemy. ॥21॥
3.39.22: In his presence all my senses are disturbed. This must be an enemy; he is to be killed, no doubt. ॥22॥
3.39.23: And my guru's instruction stands for me today: One who causes pain is to be killed by you by all means, O king; no hesitation should be had here. ॥23॥
3.39.24: And my weapons are for this very purpose, no doubt. Reflecting thus, he stood right there, fitting an arrow to his bow. ॥24॥
3.39.25: Meanwhile, to protect Arjuna and to test his devotion, Śaṅkara, who is affectionate to his devotees, ॥25॥
3.39.26: assumed the most wondrous form of a skilled Bhilla hunter together with his gaṇas, and quickly arrived there to destroy that demon. ॥26॥
3.39.27: Hara then, with his garment girded up and his hair tied with creepers, with white stripes on his body, himself bearing bow and arrows, ॥27॥
3.39.28: carrying a quiver of arrows on his back, went forth. His gaṇas too became hunters likewise, and Śiva became the king of the Bhillas. ॥28॥
3.39.29: Making various cries, the leader of the host set out; then the sound pursued the boar in all ten directions. ॥29॥
3.39.30: Arjuna was then disturbed by the sound of the forest-dweller, and by those sounds the mountains and everything else were all shaken. ॥30॥
3.39.31: Arjuna thought: Ah, what could this be? Yet Śiva is the bestower of good here. I have heard this before, and Kṛṣṇa too has told it again, ॥31॥
3.39.32: and Vyāsa told it as well; and the gods too, remembering, have said again: Śiva is declared the bestower of good, and Śiva likewise the giver of happiness. ॥32॥
3.39.33: He himself is called the giver of liberation because he grants liberation, no doubt. By remembering his name, welfare surely arises for people. ॥33॥
3.39.34: For those who worship him with their whole being, sorrow does not arise even in a dream; if it ever does arise, then it springs from past karma. ॥34॥
3.39.35: What is destined, even if great, should be known as surely small, no doubt; or else it should be understood especially as the fault of prārabdha karma. ॥35॥
3.39.36: Or else Śaṅkara, having carried the devotee through what must be experienced, whether much or little, may at times remove it by his will, no doubt. ॥36॥
3.39.37: He can turn poison into nectar, or nectar into poison. Whatever he wishes, he does; he is all-powerful—what can restrain him? ॥37॥
3.39.38: Even as this is pondered thus, it is understood by other devotees of old and by devotees yet to come: having always brought the mind here to Śiva, one should keep it steady. ॥38॥
3.39.39: Whether fortune departs or remains, whether death is near and before one, whether people blame or praise—and likewise the ending of sorrow— ॥39॥
3.39.40: all this arises from merit and sin. Śaṅkara is always the giver of happiness; and sometimes Śiva gives sorrow in order to test his devotee. ॥40॥
3.39.41: And in the end he is declared to be the giver of happiness, because of his compassion; there is no doubt. Just as gold, when refined, attains purity, so too does the devotee through hardship. ॥41॥
3.39.42: Thus indeed I heard it formerly from the mouth of the sage. Therefore, by worshipping him alone, I shall obtain supreme happiness. ॥42॥
3.39.43: While he was reflecting in this way, just then the boar arrived within range of an arrow's release. ॥43॥
3.39.44: Śiva too came, following closely behind the boar. Then, between the two of them, that boar appeared like a wondrous peak. ॥44॥
3.39.45: His greatness has been proclaimed: Śiva, Śaṅkara who is affectionate to his devotees, moved even more swiftly for the protection of Arjuna. ॥45॥
3.39.46: At that moment the two of them released their arrows: Śiva's arrow struck at the tail, and Arjuna's at the mouth. ॥46॥
3.39.47: Śiva's arrow, having entered through the tail and swiftly emerged from the mouth, vanished into the ground; Arjuna's went out through its tail. ॥47॥
3.39.48: And Arjuna's arrow fell to the side. At that instant the boar-demon fell dead upon the ground. ॥48॥
3.39.49: The gods attained supreme joy and showered flowers; crying victory, they offered praises, bowing again and again. ॥49॥
3.39.50: Śiva was pleased at heart and Arjuna attained happiness; then the two of them saw the cruel form of the demon. ॥50॥
3.39.51: Arjuna in particular spoke with a joyful heart: Ah! This is a mighty demon, and his form is most wondrous. ॥51॥
3.39.52: Having assumed this form, he came to kill me; I have been well protected by Śiva. The Lord has granted me understanding this very day; there is no doubt. ॥52॥
3.39.53: Having reflected thus, Arjuna there chanted Śiva, Śiva, bowed once more to Śiva, and praised him again and again. ॥53॥
3.39.iti: Thus ends the thirty-ninth adhyāya, named The slaying of the demon Mūka, in the account of the Kirāta incarnation, in the third saṃhitā, the Śatarudra-saṃhitā, of the Śrī Śivamahāpurāṇa. ॥39॥
3.40.1: Nandīśvara said: O Sanatkumāra, knower of all, hear the sport (līlā) of the Supreme Self, filled with affection for his devotees and interwoven with the testing of Arjuna's firmness. ॥1॥
3.40.2: Then Śiva too quickly sent his own servant for the arrow; and at that time Arjuna also came there for it. ॥2॥
3.40.3: At one and the same moment both his attendant (gaṇa) and Arjuna arrived for the arrow; Arjuna, rebuking him, then took up his own arrow. ॥3॥
3.40.4: The attendant said to him there: Why is the arrow being taken? The arrow is ours indeed; let it go, O best of sages. ॥4॥
3.40.5: O best of sages, thus addressed by that attendant of the Bhilla, Arjuna remembered Śaṅkara and spoke these words to him. ॥5॥
3.40.6: Arjuna said: What are you saying without knowing? You are a fool, forest-dweller. The arrow was released by me today; how then is it yours? ॥6॥
3.40.7: Its lined shape and feathers, and it is marked with my very name—how has it become yours? Your nature is hard to give up. ॥7॥
3.40.8: Nandīśvara said: Having heard these words of his, that lord of attendants, in the form of a Bhilla, laughed and addressed Arjuna, who was in the guise of a sage. ॥8॥
3.40.9: Listen, you ascetic. No austerity is being performed by you. You are an ascetic only by your garb, not in truth; you act deceitfully. ॥9॥
3.40.10: How can a man who is an ascetic speak falsely? And know that I am not alone: I serve the lord of an army. ॥10॥
3.40.11: That master of mine dwells accompanied by many forest Bhillas, and he is fully able to bestow both hostility and favour. ॥11॥
3.40.12: This arrow, which has just now been taken by you, is his; this arrow will never remain by your side. ॥12॥
3.40.13: Why, O ascetic, do you wish to throw away the fruit of your austerity? Through theft, deceit, harassing others, arrogance and breaking the truth— ॥13॥
3.40.14: —austerity wanes; this is what I have heard. Therefore, how will there be any fruit of your austerity today? ॥14॥
3.40.15: Therefore, if you do not let go of the arrow, you will be ungrateful; for surely it was my own master who released the arrow for your sake. ॥15॥
3.40.16: The enemy was slain by him, and your life was protected by the arrow; so you are utterly ungrateful, and likewise one who makes his austerity inauspicious. ॥16॥
3.40.17: You do not speak the truth; how then do you hope for success? If you need the arrow, let my master be asked for it. ॥17॥
3.40.18: He himself is able then to give many such arrows. My king is present here today; why then is he not asked by you in this way? ॥18॥
3.40.19: Casting aside the favour done to you, you seek to do harm. What you are doing right now is not proper; give up this rashness. ॥19॥
3.40.20: Nandīśvara said: Having heard these words of his, Arjuna, son of Pṛthā, grew angry, yet remembering Śiva he then spoke measured words. ॥20॥
3.40.21: Arjuna said: Listen, Bhilla, I shall speak: your speech is not true. As your birth is, so do I know you to be, forest-dweller. ॥21॥
3.40.22: I am a king; you are a thief. How can there be fighting between us? I must fight with the mighty, never with the base. ॥22॥
3.40.23: So too your master will be just like you. We are called givers; you forest-dwellers are thieves. ॥23॥
3.40.24: How should the Bhilla king be begged by me now in this way? Why do you yourself not ask me for the arrow, forest-dweller? ॥24॥
3.40.25: If asked, I would give you arrows, for surely I have many; but a king will not yield to seizure—so it must be. ॥25॥
3.40.26: Why indeed should I hand over arrows thus, forest-dweller? If your lord has any design against me, why does he not come now? ॥26॥
3.40.27: Let your master rather come; why does he merely talk now? Having come and fought with me, and having defeated me in battle, ॥27॥
3.40.28: let your Bhilla master, the lord of the army, take this arrow and go happily to his own abode. Why is there delay? ॥28॥
3.40.29: Nandīśvara said: Having heard these words of Arjuna, who had obtained true strength through the grace of Maheśvara, the Bhilla then spoke. ॥29॥
3.40.30: The Bhilla said: You are ignorant; you are no sage. Why do you seek death? Give up the arrow and remain at ease; otherwise you will suffer distress. ॥30॥
3.40.31: Nandīśvara said: Thus addressed by that Bhilla attendant, who shone with the true power of Śiva, the Pāṇḍava remembered Śaṅkara and spoke to him. ॥31॥
3.40.32: Arjuna said: Listen truly to my words, Bhilla, forest-dweller: when your master comes, then I shall show him the result. ॥32॥
3.40.33: Fighting with you is not fitting; I shall fight with your master. A fight between a lion and a jackal is to be known as laughable. ॥33॥
3.40.34: You have heard my words today; you will see great might. Go to your master, Bhilla, and do as you wish. ॥34॥
3.40.35: Nandīśvara said: Thus addressed by Pārtha, O sage, the Bhilla went to where the Kirāta, the lord of the army, the incarnation of Śiva, was staying. ॥35॥
3.40.36: Then he reported all of Arjuna's words in detail to the lord of the Bhillas, that Supreme Self in the form of a Bhilla. ॥36॥
3.40.37: Hearing those words, that lord of the Kirātas, Śaṅkara bearing the form of a Bhilla, was delighted and came with his own army. ॥37॥
3.40.38: Then Arjuna the Pāṇḍava, seeing the Kirāta's army, took up his bow with arrows and came forward to face it. ॥38॥
3.40.39: Then the Kirāta again sent that messenger, and through his mouth spoke these words to the great-souled Bhārata. ॥39॥
3.40.40: The Kirāta said: Look at the army, O ascetic. Release the arrow and go now. Why do you wish for death at this moment for so trifling a matter? ॥40॥
3.40.41: Your brothers will be stricken with grief, and after that your wife as well; and the earth will today slip from your hand. This is my view. ॥41॥
3.40.42: Nandīśvara said: Thus spoke the supreme Lord Śambhu, who had assumed a form in order to test Pārtha's firmness and, in every way, for the protection of Arjuna. ॥42॥
3.40.43: Thus addressed, that attendant of Śaṅkara then came and reported to Arjuna the whole matter in detail. ॥43॥
3.40.44: Hearing that, Pārtha spoke again to the messenger who had come: Tell the commander of the army that the opposite will happen. ॥44॥
3.40.45: If I give you my arrow, I shall become a disgrace to my lineage; there is no doubt. ॥45॥
3.40.46: Then my brothers would surely be stricken with grief, and my learning would be fruitless. Therefore come to fight, certainly. ॥46॥
3.40.47: Never have I heard of a lion afraid of a jackal; likewise a king never fears a forest-dweller. ॥47॥
3.40.48: Nandīśvara said: Thus addressed by the Pāṇḍava, he went back to his master and reported everything, especially what Arjuna had said. ॥48॥
3.40.49: Then Mahādeva too, called the Kirāta, with his host, having heard that, came at that time against Arjuna accompanied by his army. ॥49॥
3.40.iti: Thus ends the fortieth adhyāya, named The dialogue of the Bhilla and Arjuna, in the account of the Kirāta incarnation, in the third saṃhitā, the Śatarudra-saṃhitā, of the Śrī Śivamahāpurāṇa. ॥40॥
3.41.1: Then, seeing him arrive, Arjuna meditated on Śiva, went there, and fought a very fierce battle with him. ॥1॥
3.41.2: With the gaṇas he harassed him with various sharp weapons. Then Pārtha, afflicted by them, remembered his lord Śiva. ॥2॥
3.41.3: Then Arjuna cut down their volley of arrows; and whatever weapon was hurled by them, he cut that too, and then he contemplated Śarva. ॥3॥
3.41.4: Afflicted by him, those gaṇas fled in the ten directions; and the gaṇa-chiefs, being held back, did not come back to their master. ॥4॥
3.41.5: Śiva and Arjuna fought each other with many kinds of weapons, both possessed of great strength and valour. ॥5॥
3.41.6: Śiva too, surely feeling compassion in his mind, approached Arjuna; and Arjuna then dealt a firm blow there. ॥6॥
3.41.7: Then Śiva cut off Arjuna's weapons and all his armour; only his body remained. ॥7॥
3.41.8: Then Arjuna, remembering Śiva, engaged in wrestling with that commander of the host; though distressed by fear, he remained steadfast. ॥8॥
3.41.9: By that fight the whole earth with its oceans trembled. The gods fell into distress, wondering: What will happen now? ॥9॥
3.41.10: Meanwhile the god Śiva rose into the sky and fought from there; and Arjuna did likewise. ॥10॥
3.41.11: Leaping up again and again, the two, the god and the prince, fought; and the gods were struck with wonder on seeing that marvellous combat. ॥11॥
3.41.12: Then Arjuna, perceiving his chance and remembering the lotus-feet of Śiva, having gained true strength through that meditation, seized him by the feet. ॥12॥
3.41.13: Holding his feet, Arjuna then whirled him round; and Mahādeva, loving to his devotees and their helper, laughed. ॥13॥
3.41.14: O sage, this deed was done by Śiva alone, out of his submission to his devotees, in order to grant him the status of his own servant; it could not be otherwise. ॥14॥
3.41.15: Afterwards, laughing, Śaṅkara, out of submission to his devotee, suddenly revealed there his wondrous, auspicious form, ॥15॥
3.41.16: as described in the Vedas, the śāstras and the Purāṇa, O best of persons, the form taught by Vyāsa for meditation upon him, which bestows all accomplishments. ॥16॥
3.41.17: Seeing that beautiful form of Śiva, attained before in meditation, Arjuna was exceedingly amazed and was himself ashamed. ॥17॥
3.41.18: Ah! This is Śiva, Śiva himself, whom I chose as my lord — the Lord of the three worlds in person. Alas, what have I now done! ॥18॥
3.41.19: Powerful is the Lord's māyā, deluding even the masters of illusion. What has the Lord done, concealing his form? I have truly been deceived. ॥19॥
3.41.20: Having reflected thus in his mind, with joined palms and bowed head, he lovingly bowed to the Lord; then, dejected in mind, he spoke. ॥20॥
3.41.21: Arjuna said: O God of gods, Mahādeva, mine of compassion, Śaṅkara, Lord of all — please forgive my offence. ॥21॥
3.41.22: What have you done, concealing your form? I have now been deceived by you. Shame on me, who fought with you, my master, O Lord! ॥22॥
3.41.23: Nandīśvara said: Speaking thus, the Pāṇḍava was filled with remorse and quickly fell at the feet of Śaṅkara, the great Lord. ॥23॥
3.41.24: Then the Lord, pleased at heart, Maheśa, loving to his devotees, consoled Arjuna again and again and replied to him thus. ॥24॥
3.41.25: Śaṅkara said: Do not grieve, Pārtha; you are my devotee in a special way. I did this today to test you; cast off your sorrow. ॥25॥
3.41.26: Nandīśvara said: Having said this, the Lord raised Arjuna with his own hands and, with the gaṇas extolling the master's virtues, freed him from his shame. ॥26॥
3.41.27: Again Śiva, Śaṅkara, loving to his devotees, spoke to Arjuna the Pāṇḍava, esteemed by heroes, delighting him in every way with affection. ॥27॥
3.41.28: Śiva said: O Pārtha, best of the Pāṇḍavas, I am pleased; choose a boon. Your blows and strikes today I have honoured as worship. ॥28॥
3.41.29: It was done today by my own will; there is no offence on your part now. There is nothing that cannot be given to you; whatever you desire, choose that. ॥29॥
3.41.30: This has been done for your good, to establish your fame and kingdom over your enemies. Do not grieve over this; give up all your despondency. ॥30॥
3.41.31: Nandīśvara said: Thus addressed by the Lord Śaṅkara, Arjuna, standing attentively, spoke to Śaṅkara with devotion. ॥31॥
3.41.32: Arjuna said: O good Lord, what more is to be desired from you, Śambhu, who love your devotees? Your glory is what I should describe, O God; you are compassionate, O Sadāśiva. ॥32॥
3.41.33: Having said this, the Pāṇḍava then offered to Śaṅkara, the great Lord, a hymn of praise, true devotion in accord with the Veda. ॥33॥
3.41.34: Arjuna said: Salutation to you, God of gods; salutation to the dweller on Kailāsa. O Sadāśiva, salutation to you; salutation to you, the five-faced one. ॥34॥
3.41.35: Salutation to you, wearer of matted locks; salutation be to you, the three-eyed. Salutation to the one of gracious form and to the thousand-faced. ॥35॥
3.41.36: O blue-throated one, salutation be to you; salutation indeed to Sadyojāta. O bull-bannered one, salutation be to you, who have Girijā on your left side. ॥36॥
3.41.37: O ten-armed one, salutation to you; salutation to you, the Supreme Self. Salutation to you who hold the ḍamaru and the skull in your hands, who wear a garland of skulls. ॥37॥
3.41.38: To you whose body is like pure crystal and pure camphor, who hold Pināka in hand, bearer of the excellent trident — salutation. ॥38॥
3.41.39: Salutation to you who wear a tiger-skin as upper garment and an elephant-hide as clothing, whose limbs are adorned with serpents; O bearer of the Gaṅgā, salutation be to you. ॥39॥
3.41.40: Salutation be to you of beautiful feet, of reddish soles, to be served by Nandin and the other gaṇas, and lord of the gaṇas — salutation to you. ॥40॥
3.41.41: Salutation to you who have the form of Gaṇeśa and who are attended by Kārttikeya; to you who give devotion to the devotees and who give liberation, salutation, salutation. ॥41॥
3.41.42: Salutation be to you who are without attributes; salutation, salutation to you who have attributes; to the formless and to the one with form, to the one with parts and to the partless. ॥42॥
3.41.43: Salutation to you who took the form of a Kirāta (hunter), who bestow grace on me, who are fond of battle with heroes, and who enact many kinds of divine play. ॥43॥
3.41.44: Whatever form is seen is regarded as your own radiance. You, whose nature is consciousness, delight in the three worlds through both immanence and distinction. ॥44॥
3.41.45: There is no counting your qualities, just as there is none here for the particles of earth's dust, for the stars in the sky, or for the drops of rain-water. ॥45॥
3.41.46: Even the Vedas are not able to count your qualities; how then, O Lord, can I, of dull intellect, describe them? ॥46॥
3.41.47: You are that which you are; salutation be to you. Please show me compassion here. I am your servant, O Maheśāna; you are my master, O Maheśvara. ॥47॥
3.41.48: Nandīśvara said: Hearing these words of his, the Lord Śaṅkara, becoming even more pleased, smiling, spoke again to Arjuna. ॥48॥
3.41.49: Śaṅkara said: What is the use of saying much? Listen to my word: quickly choose a boon, son, and I shall give you all of it. ॥49॥
3.41.50: Nandīśvara said: Thus addressed by him, Arjuna prostrated before Sadāśiva and, with joined palms, bowing, spoke with love in a voice choked with emotion. ॥50॥
3.41.51: Arjuna said: What shall I say? You abide as the inner controller of all. Nevertheless, O all-pervading one, may what I describe today be heard by you. ॥51॥
3.41.52: The distress caused by enemies is gone through the sight of you. Act so that I may attain success both in this world and the supreme one. ॥52॥
3.41.53: Nandīśvara said: Having said this and bowed to Śaṅkara, who is affectionate to his devotees, Arjuna stood there with bent shoulders and joined palms. ॥53॥
3.41.54: Śiva, the master, knowing the Pāṇḍava Arjuna to be thus, the best of his own devotees, became greatly pleased. ॥54॥
3.41.55: Maheśāna gave him his own Pāśupata missile, ever invincible by all, and spoke these words. ॥55॥
3.41.56: Śiva said: My own great missile has been given by me; you will be invincible. With it, achieve the task of conquering all your enemies. ॥56॥
3.41.57: I shall also tell Kṛṣṇa; he will give you help. He is indeed my very self, my devotee, who accomplishes my work. ॥57॥
3.41.58: Through my power, O Bhārata, make your kingdom free of thorns (enemies), and always, together with your brother, have the various kinds of dharma performed. ॥58॥
3.41.59: Nandīśvara said: Having said this and placed his own hand on his head, Śaṅkara, worshipped by Arjuna, quickly vanished. ॥59॥
3.41.60: Then Arjuna, delighted at heart, having obtained the missile and the boon from the Lord, went to his principal hermitage, remembering with devotion Śiva, his guru. ॥60॥
3.41.61: All his brothers were delighted, like bodies to which the life-breath has returned; meeting him, they attained happiness, and so did Draupadī of excellent vows. ॥61॥
3.41.62: All the Pāṇḍavas, hearing the whole account and that the supreme Śiva was pleased, were filled with joy and could not have enough of hearing it. ॥62॥
3.41.63: In the hermitage a shower of flowers mixed with sandal paste fell, for the welfare of those great-souled ones. ॥63॥
3.41.64: Joyfully bowing to the blessed Śaṅkara, Śiva, they rejoiced, knowing that the end of the term of exile had arrived and that victory would surely follow. ॥64॥
3.41.65: Meanwhile Kṛṣṇa, hearing that Arjuna had returned, came to meet him, and on hearing everything he was filled with happiness. ॥65॥
3.41.66: Therefore I have proclaimed Śaṅkara as the remover of all sorrows. He is constantly served by me; let him be served by you too. ॥66॥
