3.41.67: Thus has the incarnation of Śaṅkara called Kirāta been told to you. Whoever hears it, or causes others to hear it, will attain all desires. ॥67॥
3.41.iti: Thus ends the forty-first adhyāya, named The incarnation as Kirāteśvara, in the third saṃhitā, the Śatarudra-saṃhitā, of the Śrī Śivamahāpurāṇa. ॥41॥
3.42.1: Nandīśvara said: Hear, O sage, about the supreme incarnations of the all-pervading Lord, twelve in number, which have the form of jyotirliṅgas and bring manifold blessings. ॥1॥
3.42.2: Somanātha in Saurāṣṭra, Mallikārjuna on Śrīśaila, Mahākāla in Ujjayinī, and Amareśvara at Oṅkāra; ॥2॥
3.42.3: Kedāra on the ridge of the Himālaya, Bhīmaśaṅkara in Ḍākinī, Viśveśa in Vārāṇasī, and Tryambaka on the bank of the Gautamī; ॥3॥
3.42.4: Vaidyanātha at Citābhūmi, Nāgeśa in Dārukāvana, Rāmeśa at Setubandha, and Ghuśmeśa at Śivālaya. ॥4॥
3.42.5: This set of twelve incarnations of Śambhu, the Supreme Self, brings every joy to people through seeing and touching them, O sage. ॥5॥
3.42.6: Among them the first is Somanātha, who ended the Moon's suffering; through his worship, O sage, he destroys diseases such as consumption and leprosy. ॥6॥
3.42.7: Someśa, an incarnation of Śiva, abides in the form of a liṅga in Saurāṣṭra, an auspicious land, and was worshipped long ago by the Moon. ॥7॥
3.42.8: There too is the Candrakuṇḍa, which destroys all sins; a wise man who bathes there is freed from all diseases. ॥8॥
3.42.9: Having seen Someśvara, the great liṅga of Śiva, the very embodiment of the Supreme Self, one is freed from sin and obtains both enjoyment and liberation. ॥9॥
3.42.10: The second incarnation of Śaṅkara, named Mallikārjuna, is on Śrīgiri, dear one; he grants devotees the fruits they desire. ॥10॥
3.42.11: That Śiva, who went there from his own mountain with great love in order to see his son, O sage, is praised there in the form of a liṅga. ॥11॥
3.42.12: That second jyotirliṅga, O sage, through seeing and worshipping it, brings great happiness and at the end grants liberation; there is no doubt about this. ॥12॥
3.42.13: Dear one, the incarnation of Śaṅkara named Mahākāla arose in the city of Ujjayinī as the protector of his own people. ॥13॥
3.42.14: He who destroyed the demon named Dūṣaṇa, crusher of Vedic dharma, hater of brahmins, destroyer of all, who had come to Ujjayinī— ॥14॥
3.42.15: —meditated upon by the sons of the brahmin Vedapriya, he swiftly reduced to ashes with a mere huṃ that demon who dwelt on Ratnamāla. ॥15॥
3.42.16: Having slain him, that Mahākāla, entreated by the gods, remained in the form of a jyotirliṅga as the protector of his devotees. ॥16॥
3.42.17: Having seen and diligently worshipped the liṅga called Mahākāla, one attains all desires and afterwards gains the supreme goal. ॥17॥
3.42.18: Oṅkāra and Parameśāna, assumed by Śambhu the Supreme Self, is indeed the fourth incarnation, granting devotees the fruits they desire. ॥18॥
3.42.19: Installed with devotion according to rite, O sage, Mahādeva appeared from his own earthen liṅga, fulfilling the desire of Vindhya. ॥19॥
3.42.20: Entreated there by the gods, he abides in a twofold form; in the form of the liṅga, he who loves his devotees grants enjoyment and liberation. ॥20॥
3.42.21: In the praṇava form the excellent liṅga was named Oṅkāra, and the earthen one was named Parameśvara, O lord of sages. ॥21॥
3.42.22: Whichever of them is seen and worshipped, O sage, should be known to grant devotees their desires. Thus the two most divine jyotirliṅgas have been described to you, O great sage. ॥22॥
3.42.23: The fifth incarnation is Kedāreśa, the supreme Śiva; he abides at Kedāra in the form of a jyotirliṅga. ॥23॥
3.42.24: Entreated by the two incarnations of Hari named Nara and Nārāyaṇa, O sage, who dwelt there, Śiva stays at Kedāra on the snowy mountain. ॥24॥
3.42.25: Worshipped daily by those two and called Kedāreśvara, Śambhu grants devotees their desires through being seen and worshipped. ॥25॥
3.42.26: Though lord of all, he is especially the master of this region; that incarnation of Śiva, dear one, grants all desires. ॥26॥
3.42.27: The sixth incarnation of Śambhu, the great Lord, is called Bhīmaśaṅkara, of great sport, the destroyer of the demon Bhīma. ॥27॥
3.42.28: He protected his devotee Sudakṣiṇa, king and lord of Kāmarūpa, having slain that wondrous demon who tormented the devotees. ॥28॥
3.42.29: Entreated by him, Śaṅkara himself, named Bhīmaśaṅkara, abides in Ḍākinī in the form of a jyotirliṅga. ॥29॥
3.42.30: The seventh, the incarnation Viśveśvara, arose in Kāśī; he has the form of the entire cosmos and grants enjoyment and liberation, O sage. ॥30॥
3.42.31: He is always worshipped with devotion by all the gods led by Viṣṇu, and constantly also by the lord of Kailāsa and by Bhairava. ॥31॥
3.42.32: The Lord, giver of liberation, abides there in the form of a jyotirliṅga; being himself of self-accomplished nature, he dwells thus in his own city. ॥32॥
3.42.33: Those who, with devotion to Kāśī and Viśveśa, repeat their names remain ever untainted by actions and share in the state of liberation (kaivalya). ॥33॥
3.42.34: The incarnation called Tryambaka is the eighth, on the bank of the Gautamī; entreated by Gautama, this form of the moon-crested one manifested. ॥34॥
3.42.35: At Gautama's request, out of love and wishing to please that sage, he stays there immovably in the form of a jyotirliṅga. ॥35॥
3.42.36: Through seeing, touching, and worshipping that great Lord, all desires are fulfilled, and then, ah, liberation follows. ॥36॥
3.42.37: By Śiva's grace, the Gaṅgā, named Gautamī, purifying and dear to Śaṅkara, abides there out of love for Gautama. ॥37॥
3.42.38: The Vaidyanātha incarnation is declared the ninth among them; the Lord, performer of many sports, manifested for Rāvaṇa's sake. ॥38॥
3.42.39: Making a pretext of being carried by Rāvaṇa, Maheśvara established himself at Citābhūmi in the form of a jyotirliṅga. ॥39॥
3.42.40: He became famed in the three worlds by the name Vaidyanātheśvara; through being seen and worshipped with devotion, he indeed grants enjoyment and liberation. ॥40॥
3.42.41: O sage, this teaching on the greatness of Śiva as Vaidyanātheśvara grants worldly enjoyment and liberation to those who read it and also to those who hear it. ॥41॥
3.42.42: The Nāgeśvara incarnation is declared to be the tenth. He manifested for the sake of his devotees and always punishes the wicked. ॥42॥
3.42.43: Having slain the demon named Dāruka, the destroyer of dharma, he protected his devotee, the chief of merchants named Supriya. ॥43॥
3.42.44: For the benefit of the worlds, Śambhu, the Supreme, the performer of many sports, together with Ambikā, remained there assuming the form of a jyotirliṅga. ॥44॥
3.42.45: O sage, by seeing that Śiva-liṅga named Nāgeśvara and worshipping it, heaps of great sins are swiftly destroyed. ॥45॥
3.42.46: The Rāmeśvara incarnation is remembered as Śiva's eleventh; O sage, he did what was dear to Rāmacandra and was installed by Rāma. ॥46॥
3.42.47: Śaṅkara, affectionate to devotees, who, being well pleased, lovingly gave Rāma the boon of victory, manifested as the liṅga. ॥47॥
3.42.48: Earnestly entreated by Rāma, O sage, he remained at Setubandha in the form of a jyotirliṅga, worshipped by Rāma. ॥48॥
3.42.49: The glory of Rāmeśvara became wondrous and unequalled on earth; it grants enjoyment and liberation and always fulfils the desires of devotees. ॥49॥
3.42.50: The man who, with true devotion, bathes that Rāmeśvara with Gaṅgā water is indeed liberated while living. ॥50॥
3.42.51: Having enjoyed here all pleasures, even those hard for the gods to obtain, he then attains supreme knowledge and reaches kaivalya, liberation. ॥51॥
3.42.52: The Ghuśmeśvara incarnation is indeed Śaṅkara's twelfth; he performs various sports, gives joy to Ghuśmā, and is affectionate to devotees. ॥52॥
3.42.53: O sage, in the southern direction, near Devaśaila, the Lord who did what was dear to Ghuśmā manifested in a lake. ॥53॥
3.42.54: O sage, Śambhu, affectionate to devotees, pleased by her devotion, fully restored and protected Ghuśmā's son who had been killed by Sudehā. ॥54॥
3.42.55: Entreated by her, that Śambhu, the granter of desires, remained there in the lake in the form of a jyotirliṅga, named Ghuśmeśvara. ॥55॥
3.42.56: Having seen that Śiva-liṅga and worshipped it with devotion, one enjoys every happiness here and then attains liberation. ॥56॥
3.42.57: Thus I have narrated to you the divine series of jyotirliṅgas, twelve in number, which grants enjoyment and liberation. ॥57॥
3.42.58: Whoever reads or even hears this account of the jyotirliṅgas is freed from all sins and attains enjoyment and liberation. ॥58॥
3.42.59: And this saṃhitā named Śatarudra has been described by me; it celebrates the hundred incarnations and grants the fruit of all desires. ॥59॥
3.42.60: Whoever reads this daily, or listens to it with a concentrated mind, obtains all desires and then surely attains liberation. ॥60॥
3.42.iti: Thus ends the forty-second adhyāya, named The incarnations as the twelve jyotirliṅgas, in the dialogue of Sanatkumāra and Nandīśvara, in the third saṃhitā, the Śatarudra-saṃhitā, of the Śrī Śivamahāpurāṇa. ॥42॥
